title: Agave Dijon Salad Dressing
text: all recipes / salad agave dijon salad dressing tags: vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free, nut-free, soy-free recipe: agave/dijon salad dressing equipment vitamix, 2 pitchers ingredients for 1 batch (~48 servs) 1 ¼ cups apple cider vinegar ½ cup + 2 tbsp dijon mustard ½ cup + 2 tbsp agave 3 ½ cup light olive oil ½ cup water instructions add all except oil in vitamix container and mix on low. drizzle oil into vitamix mixing while you do. gradually increase speed until all emulsified. divide between 2 small pitchers. cover & store in fridge (if not for today, label and date also).

title: Alt Moroccan Red Lentil Soup
text: all recipes / soup alt moroccan red lentil soup tags: vegetarian, gluten-free, nut-free, soy-free opening alt recipe: moroccan red lentil soup page 1 of 3 equipment 32qt (largest) stock pot with pot-saver under it, zester, juicer, mini cuisinart ingredients ~48 (14-15qts) ~⅓ cup olive oil (to coat bottom of stock pot) 2 ½ lbs onions, ½” dice 2 lbs carrots, ½ “ dice 7 stalks celery, ½ “ dice 20 cloves garlic, chopped in mini-cuis (easier if thawed a bit) 3tbls + 1tsp ground coriander //can either toast & grind seeds or use pre-ground 5tsp ground cumin //can either toast & grind seeds or use pre-ground 5tsp tumeric 2 ½ tsp paprika (not smoked, just regular or “hungarian”) 1 ¼ tsp cinnamon 2 ½ tsp salt 1 ¼ tsp pepper 10qts veg broth =1 ¼ jar better than bouillion dissolved in 1qt hot tea water + 9qts water 1 6lb + 1 28oz can diced tomatoes 10 cups red lentils, rinsed 4 bunches kale, torn into pieces ½ cup + 2t (=~3) lemons, juiced ...save some zest in case needed ¼ tsp cayenne 1 ¼ cup flat-leaf parsley, chopped (1cup= after finely chopping) 4 bunches fresh cilantro, roughly chopped, served on the side ~48 oz yogurt on the side (ideally greek) o-night recipe: moroccan red lentil soup page 2 of 3 instructions prepare ingredients locate all ingredients measure out lentils and set aside dice onions, carrots & celerly kale: remove thick stem from center, tear into large bite sized pieced wash lemons zest 1-2 lemons (=scrape off the thin outermost yellow layer of skin) using either the microplane (sharp!) or box grater (suggest wearing the cut-resistant glove for either). set aside in case needed at the end. juice lemons using electric juicer or wooden reamer wash parsley, discard main trunk of stems, finely chop rest chop garlic in mini cuisinart on chop setting (best if thawed) if prefer: toast and grind cumin & coriander using small skillet, watching carefully just till it is fragrant. grind in black spice grinder, wipe out grinder before and after. or just used pre-ground. sauté be sure heat-saver disk (on stove shelf) is placed under stock pot coat the bottom of the pot with olive oil to about ⅛” deep sauté (=fry in a little oil uncovered, stirring occasionally) the onions until they are getting soft. add in the carrots & celery and 2t salt. sauté for 20 minutes or so to develop the flavor. add the garlic, coriander, cumin, turmeric, paprika, cinnamon, salt and pepper and continue cooking for another 2-3 minutes stirring the whole time. o-night recipe: moroccan red lentil soup page 3 of 3 cook lentils (by about 2:30): add broth, tomatoes and lentils. stir well and heat to a boil. be sure there is a pot-saver/heat disperser under the pot. let it simmer at least until the lentils are soft (1 hr or more), fine to leave it on 2hrs or more or until we leave for the meeting stir frequently, add more water if it is getting too thick. add greens (~4:20) just before going to the orientation meeting, stir in the kale. turn the fire off and put a lid on the pot. final seasoning (~5:15 leave meeting early): stir in lemon juice, cayenne, parsley. re-heat ~10 minutes. taste and adjust seasoning (maybe more salt or lemon zest).

title: Steamed Broccoli
text: all recipes / side steamed broccoli tags: vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free, nut-free, soy-free day 6 recipe: steamed broccoli page 1 of 1 equipment 2-6” hotel pans, 2 steamer pans, 2 lids you may need to wash the steamer pans used for the tempeh to reuse for the broccoli, or maybe the veggie choppers have set it up already. we’re doing a whole case, so you may need to do 2 rounds, it can all be finished a bit early, anytime from 11:30 onward or so and be served room temperature if needed. setup 2 steamer assemblies: get the two 6” deep (deepest) solid pans and fill them with 2” of water. set the water filled pans across 2 burners each. divide in the 2 perforated pans as much broccoli as will fit with the lid fully closed set the perforated pans in the water filled pans and put a lid on each instructions turn on both burners. let the broccoli steam for about 5 minutes after the water comes to a boil. carefully lift the lid and check on it. when it looks done, remove the perforated pans from the base pans and empty the broccoli into a large metal serving bowl. refill one or both pans with any remaining broccoli and steam for just 2-3 minutes (we may use some of these for further baking, so leave barely done). leave the pans on the counter (out of the water) so we can serve more if needed.

title: Alt Notes on Recipe Polenta
text: all recipes / side alt notes on recipe polenta tags: vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free, nut-free, soy-free day 3 recipe: polenta page 1 of 2 equipment if supper: 3 full pans. serve the 2 and save the other for supper. if no supper, just 2 full size. use the 4” (medium depth) so it doesn’t slosh when putting in the oven. ingredients: note: simplified to be all vegan no-cheese, serve cheese on the side for the whole meal. note: if making 3 pans: we only have 2 4” deep full pans, so use 2 4” half pans or a 6” deep one for the third and save the 3rd for supper leftover. per full pan: ask km how many pans: usually 2 if no supper or supper “minestrone” soup is planned, 3 if supper casserole is planned. [only 1 for group of ~36 with no supper use] 5 cups polenta 20 cups = 5 qts water with bouillon (3 t bouillon paste mixed with 1 quart of hot tea-urn water per pan), other 4 quarts water cold. (1 t) (the bouillon is salty, probably don’t need this…taste at the end) 2 t olive oil 2 t dried basil 1 t white pepper ½ c?? optional: nutritional yeast (quantity needs to be verified..) ~ ¼ cup per pan optional: earth balance (stir in at the end if using) instructions mix and bake polenta preheat oven to 425. spray pans with spray oil. mix polenta and seasonings in each of the pans you are using. leave pans uncovered and put them in the oven about 10:15. set a timer for an hour. stir & maybe cover about 11:15, carefully with hot pad gloves (and maybe with help) remove the pans and stir. peek every 20 minutes or so. if top is getting too brown, put the lid on. if done, turn off ovens and leave pans inside to stay warm. maybe stir in some earth balance at the end. day 3 alternates recipe: polenta page 2 of 2 alternate versions preferred by some cooks, notes more than recipe stovetop: something like this: use 4:1 water to polenta as above. so the equivalent of the standard 2 oven pans would be maybe 40 c (= 10qt) of water to 10 cups polenta. bring 20c=5qts water to boil. mix polenta with 10 c cold water to make slurry. add to boiling water. stir very often, slowing adding the final 10 cups of water as it thickens. use your judgement if more water is needed to make a thick but ladle-able consistency. salt to taste. notes from cook susan black on another version that makes little squares in a sheetpan: it’s prepared on the stove top, using the amount that the recipe calls for (ie same as stovetop above) it’ss boullion, same amount as other recipe, earth balance, and whatever herb one likes, just not as much as the other recipe, 1/4 to half. and no pepper.. key is to stir in the earth balance as it is becoming polenta, not in the water. the closer to done u add the earth balance u need less and it will taste creamy. quantity of earth balance is about 1/2 cup then to taste. olive oil gives it that little herbaceous taste, u can mix in both. pour into a sheet pan when done, smooth and creamy, where it cools (fast) and can be cut into triangles or squares, whatever. i cook it in two separate pots, 1 per sheet pan. that’s why u can use half, because one sheet pan can be cut into 50 slices that are medium to large. make sure to grease the sheet pan before pouring. but if u make two sheet pans the other one can be used the next day, or frozen and used days later. freezes well. if used the next day it could be fried lightly in earth balance, or oil, crispy then. or, simply brush olive oil or melted earth blance over the top and bake, low as u are reheating, it will crisp up a bit. the creaminess comes from the earth balance, but one could also use olive oil, or any vegan fat. even fancier idea (maybe to make for a supper leftover portion): say you roasted some mushrooms, u could pour the polenta on the mushrooms on the sheet pan and cool, and now u have toasted mushroom polenta. or any veg for that matter, zucchini, bell pepper, really as long as it is roasted and spread out evenly u can just pour the polenta over it and yum.

title: Alt Portuguese Kale White Bean Soup
text: all recipes / soup alt portuguese kale white bean soup tags: vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free, nut-free, soy-free opening alt supper recipe: portuguese kale white bean soup (adapted from moosewood restaurant favorites) (p. 1 of 3) equipment 32qt (largest) stock pot with pot-saver under it, zester, juicer, spice grinder, mini cuisinart (& separate 12 qt pot to give beans a head-start) prep ahead: soak dry cannellini beans overnight...if you forget this, try quick soak method (see side notice area), or use ~ 7 x 28oz canned ingredients ~48 (14-15qts) (this gets eaten, no useful leftovers expected) whole lg jar sun dried tomatoes (whole 32-34oz jar jar of oil-packed), drained, reserve oil for saute if needed olive oil (if needed to supplement sun-dried tomato oil for saute) 4lbs onions, ½” dice 2lbs carrots, ½ “ dice ~4-6 bulbs fresh fennel bulbs (quanity depends on size), ½ “ dice 4lbs potatoes (ideally yukon gold), ½ “ dice 14 cloves garlic, chopped in mini-cuisinart 4 ½ tbls fennel seeds, very lightly toasted and ground 4 ½ tbls thyme 2 ½ tsp salt 1 ¼ tsp pepper 7 qts veg broth =1 jar better than bouillon dissolved in 1qt hot tea water + 6qts water (use the bean cooking water if you did them separately) 1 lg (+ 1 med) canned diced tomatoes (i.e. 1 6lb6oz + 1 28oz) (or= ~4.5 28oz cans) 2 qts dry, cooked cannellini (white) beans (about 2 qts dry??)(or ~6-7 28oz cans) 5 bunches kale, torn into pieces (very roughly 2”x2” sized) ~1 cup (=~8) lemons, juiced ...save some zest in case needed //add to taste recipe: portuguese kale white bean soup (p. 2 of 3) instructions cook beans note: km will have pre-soaked the beans. rinse soaked beans. in a separate 12 qt pot: cover with fresh water, bring to boil and right away turn to a low simmer, skim if needed, toss in a stalk of fresh rosemary. add to main soup pot mid afternoon, they can continue to cook in the soup pot. locate & prepare ingredients strain off the oil from the oil packed sun-dried tomatoes saving the oil, and use it to saute the onions in step below. set aside tomatoes. when ready to transfer beans, use bean broth and/or water as needed to make bouillon with better than bouillon. dice onions, carrots, fresh fennel, potatoes.. kale: remove thick stem from center, tear into large bite sized pieced wash lemons zest 1-2 lemons (=scrape off the thin outermost yellow layer of skin) using either the microplane (sharp!) or box grater (suggest wearing the cut-resistant glove for either). set aside in case needed at the end. juice lemons using juicer (near rice cooker). lightly toast the fennel seeds dry in small skillet. grind using spice grinder. chop garlic in mini cuisinart on chop setting (best if thawed) recipe: portuguese kale white bean soup (p. 3 of 3) sauté be sure heat-saver disk (on stove shelf) is placed under stock pot using the reserved sun-dried tomato oil if you have it, or else olive oil, sauté the onions until they are getting soft. add in chopped garlic and 2 tsp salt. saute another minute add the ground fennel and diced fennel and cook for ~10 minutes. stir in the carrots, potatoes, thyme, sun-dried tomatoes and black pepper and cook for ~20 minutes. combine & cook soup about 2:30-3:00: add tomatoes, bouillon and beans. stir well, bring to a boil and reduce to simmer. be sure there is a pot-saver/heat disperser under the pot. simmer until potatoes are just tender. add greens just before going to orientation meeting:, stir in the kale. final seasoning after orientation meeting just before serving: stir in (some) lemon juice & zest to taste and salt to taste.

title: Alt Recipe Pumpkin Cornbread
text: all recipes / side alt recipe pumpkin cornbread tags: vegetarian, nut-free, soy-free alt recipe: pumpkin cornbread (reg, gf, df versions) pg 1 of 2 equipment 1-4 2” half-sized hotel pans (cooks more reliably in half-pans than whole pans), 2 large bowls, maybe 2 smaller bowls for gf/df version. note: see the simpler “vegan gf cornbread” recipe. all versions of this have eggs. decide with km: how many gf/df or regular to make. typical for a full house would be 3 half pans regular, 1 half pan gf/df. or if too much trouble, you can make it all gf/df. if you have no-egg people, consider making a small sauce pot of polenta on the stove (1 part polenta: 4 parts water). ingredients: per x number of 2” half-size pans: recommend use half-pans for even cooking 4 3 2 1 wet ingredients for a dairy version: 2 ½ c 1 ¾ c + 2 tbls 1 ¼ c ½ c+2tbls canola oil 1c ¾ c ½ c ¼ c brown sugar 20 15 10 5 eggs, beaten 7 ½ c 5c+2tbls 3 ¾ c 1 ¾ c+2tbls yogurt 5c 3 ¾ c 2 ½ c pumpkin puree wet ingredients for a no-dairy version: 2 ½ c 1 ¾ c + 2 tbls 1 ¼ c ½ c+2tbls canola oil 1c ¾ c ½ c ¼ c brown sugar 20 15 10 5 eggs, beaten//or “egg substitute”??? 8c 6c 4 c 2 c pumpkin puree (1 box = 2cups) 4 ½ c 3 ¼ c + 2 tbls 2 ¼ c 1c + 2tbls rice milk recipe: pumpkin cornbread (reg, gf, df versions) pg 2 of 2 ingredients (continued) dry ingredients (vary flour type to get regular or gf version): 4 3 2 1 (for number of 2” half-size pans) 10c 7 ½ c 5c 2 ½ c cornmeal (ideally ~ ⅔ medium grind, ⅓ polenta, but any combo will do including all one or the other) 10c 7 ½ c 5c 2 ½ c flour (either regular white or bob’s 1-1 gluten free) 5 tsp 3 ¾ tsp 2 ½ tsp 1 ¼ tsp tsp salt 10 tbls 7 ½ t 5t 2 ½ t tbls baking powder instructions preheat oven to 350 mix the wet ingredients together in one bowl and the dry in a separate bowl (also keeping the different diet versions separate, so perhaps 4 bowls needed). spray all the pans with spray oil. mix the wet and dry together (for each diet version). just lightly until mixed, don’t over-stir. fill the pans and bake at 350 for about 45 minutes (range could be 30-60). done when lightly brown, lightly patting the top feels solid, toothpick comes out clean. let it cool a bit and pre-slice with bread knife into 4x3=12 or 4x4=16 pieces per pan. serve with butter and earth balance.

title: ALT Recipe Quinoa and Vegetable Stew
text: all recipes / entree alt recipe quinoa and vegetable stew tags: vegetarian, gluten-free, nut-free, soy-free quinoa and vegetable stew this is a hearty, veggie and quinoa packed latin stew. it's full of nutritious ingredients and bright fresh flavors! a healthy soup you'll want all year round! course: soup cuisine: mexican keyword: quinoa soup prep time: 15 minutes cook time: 40 minutes total time: 55 minutes servings: 6 calories: 385 kcal author: jaclyn ingredients 2 st col served ~33 + 4qts left, 1st col est for full house 12 2 tbsp olive oil 6 1 onion, chopped 7 6 1 red bell pepper, stemmed, seeded and cut into 1/2-inch pieces 25 5 garlic, minced 7 6t 1 tbsp paprika 4t+2t 4t 2 tsp ground coriander 3.5t 3t 1 1/2 tsp ground cumin ?10qt 36=9qt 6 cups vegetable broth, then more as needed 7lb 6lb 1 lb. red potatoes, unpeeled, cut into 1/2-inch pieces 7c 6c 1 cup prewashed or rinsed quinoa 7c 6c 1 cup fresh or frozen corn 14 12 2 tomatoes, cored and chopped coarse 7c 6c 1 cup frozen peas salt and pepper 28? 24oz 4 oz queso fresco or feta cheese crumbled 7 6 1 avocado, halved, pitted and diced 4c 3c 1/2 cup minced fresh cilantro instructions heat oil in a dutch oven over medium heat. add onion and bell pepper and saute until softened, about 5 minutes. stir in garlic, paprika, coriander, and cumin and cook until fragrant, about 30 seconds. stir in broth and potatoes and bring to a boil over high heat. reduce heat to medium-low (i covered the pot from this point on) and simmer gently for 10 minutes. stir in quinoa and simmer for 8 minutes. stir in corn (i actually waited to add corn until adding the peas since i used frozen corn) and simmer until potatoes and quinoa are just tender, about 5 - 7 minutes. stir in tomatoes and peas and cook until warmed through, about 2 minutes. remove from heat, season with salt and pepper to taste. (stew can be refrigerated for up to 2 days. add additional broth as needed to thin sauce when reheating). sprinkle each serving with queso fresco, avocado and cilantro before serving. recipe notes do not to omit the toppings as they are key to the flavor of this soup. recipe source: cookingclassy.com adapted from cook's country one pan wonders cookbook

title: Carrot Cashew Soup
text: all recipes / soup carrot cashew soup tags: vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free, soy-free carrot cashew soup (this needs work, placeholder, good enough for now) equipment : heaviest 32qt stock pot, immersion blender ingredients 1 4 lbs carrots //could pre-slice the day before in the robo coupe 3 lbs onions, diced 1 lb ginger (optional: <= 5lbs leftover yams ) 3lbs cashews 2t 5 spice powder instructions : cover cashews with water and soak for 1-2 hours (ie do it at start of veggie chop, leave it till 9:30) dice onions locate ~14lbs of carrots & maybe yams: excess already shredded, leftover roasted yams. chop the ginger in batches in the mini-chopper (grossly cut up first, no need to peel if organic). sauté the onions in the large rondo pan until getting soft (20-30 minutes?..not till browning). add carrots (and yams) and continue to sauté stirring often over low heat until some light browning, not too brown. while these sauté: puree the cashews in the vitamix (multiple batches if needed) add ginger and 5 spice powder & sauté another minute or two add cashew milk and water to bring it up to ~14 qts bring to a boil, reduce to simmer stirring frequently. after all ingredients are soft, use emersion blender to blend smooth. taste for seasonings and salt or add more 5 spice as needed, or salt, pepper, lemon juice? aim to have it about 170 degrees by lunch time. then turn off the gas and leave the pot covered on the stove. it should stay above 145 for the afternoon. reheat at 5:00 to bring it back to 165. optional: serve with yogurt if still leaves 2x32oz left for final breakfast.

title: Apple Cake Easy
text: all recipes / dessert apple cake easy tags: vegetarian, soy-free “easy” spiced apple cake note: this is good with non-diet ingredients, so-so with gf flour, rather weird with vegan-egg. maybe make it non-diet and offer an oat-crumble or baked-apples for diets. so not so “easy” if dietary needs. (4x, orig for full retreat) 4x ½x 1x 2 full pans 8x8 orig: 9x13 3c ½ still too sw 1 (orig: 1-3/4 cups sugar ??? too much!!) 4c ½ 1 cup vegetable oil 12 1 ½ 3 eggs // wouldn’t work without eggs, make baked apples for no-egg side? 4t ½ t 1 teaspoon vanilla extract 8c 1c 2 cups all-purpose flour//fine with gf 5 t ½ + 1/8 tsp 1-1/4 teaspoons baking powder 4t ½ t 1 teaspoon salt 2t 1 t ½ t cinnamon 1t ½ t ¼ t cardamom 1t ½ t ¼ t nutmeg 1t 1/8 t 1/4 teaspoon baking soda 12-20 2-3 3-5 granny smith apples (quantity depends on size of apples) (4 ½ 1 cup chopped walnuts or pecans—optional) 3 pints 1-1/4 cups whipped topping directions quarter and core the apples, then use robocoupe to thin-slice the apples. in a large bowl, beat the sugar, oil, eggs and vanilla until well blended. combine the flour, baking powder, salt, cinnamon and baking soda; gradually beat into sugar mixture until blended. fold in apples [and nuts]. this is a stiff batter, best to do this using (gloved) hands to get it well-mixed. transfer to a greased pan.. bake at 350° for 45-60 minutes or until browning on top & a toothpick inserted near the center comes out clean. serve with whipped topping. make cashew cream (recipe in other recipes folder) for non-dairy. originally published as easy apple cake in light & tasty https://www.tasteofhome.com/recipes/easy-apple-cake

title: Apple Crisp
text: all recipes / dessert apple crisp tags: vegetarian, nut-free, soy-free apple crisp below shows for 1 ½ hotel pans with wheat & butter, plus a half-pan with gf flour and earth balance. ingredients for the filling: for 1 ½ hotel pans: for ½ pan gf: 30-36 (~12+lbs) 10-12 (~4+lbs) large apples (total for 2 pans=16lbs) (half granny smiths half something sweeter) juice of a couple of lemons in water to save apples as you work 1 ½ ½ cup granulated sugar ¾ c 4 tablespoons flour/gf flour 6t 2 teaspoon cinnamon ¾ t ¼ t of kosher salt for the topping: 4 ½ 1 ½ cup flour/gf flour 1 ½ ½ cup granulated sugar 2 ¼ c ¾ cup brown sugar 1 ½ t ½ teaspoon kosher salt 41/2 1 cup oats //adjusted up to 3/4 3cups=6 sticks 1 c butter/earth balance, melted directions: preheat oven to 350 degrees. (peel and) core apples and cut them into large uniform chunks. [can keep apples overnight in lemon water.] place apples in a bowl and toss with lemon zest, lemon juice, granulated sugar, flour, salt and cinnamon. transfer to either 5 one-cup ramekins or an 8″ square baking dish. for the topping: combine flour, sugars, salt, oats, and cold (easer: melted) butter. mix until mixture is well combined and crumbly. spread evenly over fruit mixture and pat down slightly. place baking dish on a cookie sheet and bake for one hour (allow for an hour 15 mins), until top is browned and fruit is bubbly. (you can also refrigerate, covered, and bake later. serve warm with vanilla ice cream.

title: Artichoke Hummus
text: all recipes / side artichoke hummus tags: vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free, nut-free, soy-free artichoke hummus from cook’s website ingredients 3x 6 cups orig makes 2 cups lg jar 1c drained canned or jarred artichoke hearts rinsed and patted dry 1 c ¼ c lemon juice (save zest ..) 1 tsp ¼ t grated lemon zest ¾ c ¼ c water 1c+2tbl 6tbls tahini, stirred well (see note) 6t 2t extra-virgin olive oil , plus extra for drizzling 1 ½ 29oz can 1 14oz cans chickpeas , drained and rinsed (or 3 14oz) 3 1 garlic clove (blender will mince) 2 ½ tsp ½ tsp salt ¼ tsp 0 white pepper 2 pinches? pinch cayenne 2tlb 2tsp fresh parsley or mint (over for instructions—>) set aside 4 whole artichoke pieces for garnish. combine lemon juice and water in small bowl or measuring cup. whisk together tahini and 2 tablespoons oil in second small bowl or measuring cup. combine chickpeas, remaining artichokes, garlic, salt, cayenne, and lemon zest in a bowl. probably you need to do this in 2 batches, so half of each prepared mixture as follows: process half the chickpea etc. mixture in food processor until almost fully ground, about 15 seconds. scrape down bowl with rubber spatula. with machine running, add half the lemon juice-water mixture in steady stream through feed tube. scrape down bowl and continue to process for 1 minute. with machine running, add half the oil-tahini mixture in steady stream through feed tube; continue to process until hummus is smooth and creamy, about 15 seconds, scraping down bowl as needed. make & taste, probably need more lemon & salt, maybe some white pepper. transfer hummus to serving bowl. sprinkle reserved artichokes and parsely or mint over surface, cover with plastic wrap, and let stand until flavors meld, at least 30 minutes. drizzle with olive oil and serve.

title: Artichoke Salad Dressing
text: all recipes / salad artichoke salad dressing tags: vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free, nut-free recipe: artichoke salad dressing equipment vitamix, 2 pitchers ingredients for 1 batch (~48 servs) 33 oz jar marinated artichoke hearts (add all including oil) 1 tsp tamari 3 tbsp dijon mustard 2 ½ tsp agave ½ tsp white pepper 1 cup water ½ cup rice vinegar 1lemon juice and zest of 1 lemon 1 ½ cup light olive oil pinch? salt if needed instructions add all except oil in vitamix container and mix on low, slowly increasing speed until all artichokes are pureed. drizzle oil into vitamix mixing while you do. gradually increase speed until all emulsified. divide between 2 small pitchers. taste and adjust seasonings if needed. cover & store in fridge (if not for today, label and date also).

title: Avocado Salad Dressing
text: all recipes / salad avocado salad dressing tags: vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free, nut-free, soy-free recipe: avocado salad dressing equipment vitamix, electric juicer, 2 pitchers ingredients for 1 batch (~48 servs) 2 cups water 1 cup lime/lemon juice (use 4 limes, top off with lemons if needed..can use rice vin if short of lemons/limes but it tastes much fresher with citrus juice) 5 large-ish avocados ⅓ cup cilantro ½ tsp garlic powder ¼ cup agave ½ tsp cumin powder ¾ tsp white pepper 1 ¼ tsp salt 2 cups light olive oil ~¼ cup water (this is a thick dressing, but if seems too thick, more water..) instructions juice limes and lemons with juicer. add all except oil in vitamix container and mix on low. taste and adjust salt, agave, pepper, lime to taste if you wish to. drizzle oil into vitamix mixing while you do. gradually increase speed until all emulsified. divide between 2 small pitchers. cover & store in fridge (if not for today, label and date also).

title: BABA GANOUSH (EGGPLANT DIP)
text: all recipes / side baba ganoush (eggplant dip) tags: vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free, nut-free, soy-free baba ganoush (eggplant dip) ingredients 2 to 3 medium eggplants (about 3 pounds total) 2 to 3 tablespoons olive oil 1/3 cup tahini 2 cloves garlic, peeled and crushed juice of 2 lemons (about 1/2 cup) kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper n/a freshly ground black pepper preparation 1. preheat the oven to 450°f. rub the outside of the eggplants with olive oil and place them in a roasting plan. roast the eggplant until the skin has charred and the interior is tender, 15 to 20 minutes. let cool. 2. peel and seed the cooled eggplant, roughly chop the flesh, and then transfer it to the bowl of a food processor. 3. into the processor bowl add the tahini, garlic, lemon juice, some salt and pepper to taste, and a few teaspoons of cold water. process the mixture to a coarse paste, adding a bit more water as needed to allow the mixture to blend. 4. adjust the seasoning with salt and pepper to taste and serve.

title: Balsamic Dressing
text: all recipes / salad balsamic dressing tags: vegetarian, gluten-free, dairy-free, nut-free, soy-free balsamic vinaigrette (instructions for double recipe) gather all ingredients below, the vitamix container and a second 4 quart container with lid. you will double this recipe by putting a set of the below ingredients in each container. it’s easiest to add all ingredients except the oil to both containers, then go to the next ingredient. if time: put 12 cloves of fresh garlic in the small skillet, cover with about ½ cup of olive oil and heat over medium heat, watching closely until they sizzle and just begin to turn a bit brown around the ediges. remove skillet from stove and set aside. [if not time, we can use powdered garlic. fresh unpoached is too strong for many people.] ingredients for one container (you will put this much in each one) 1 ½ cups balsamic vinegar 1t sherry vinegar 1 t dijon mustard 1 tsp black pepper ½ tsp honey ½ tsp salt 6 poached garlic cloves with half their cooking oil (see above) (or ¾ tsp garlic powder) drizzle this into the vitamix container slowly as you mix each batch: 4 ¼ cups olive oil (make it 4 ½ if you use powdered garlic) add the above ingredients except the oil to each container. blend the contents of the vitamix container using the vitamix, slowly drizzling in the 4 ½ cups of olive oil through the lid. fill 2 small pitchers with it. pour second set of ingredients into the vitamix container and mix it, again slowly drizzling in the other 4 ½ cups of olive oil. pour the mixed dressing back in the mixing container, cover, label and put in the fridge.

title: Balsamic Salad Dressing
text: all recipes / salad balsamic salad dressing tags: vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free, nut-free, soy-free recipe: balsamic salad dressing equipment vitamix, 2 pitchers, (extra 2qt square container with green lid for second batch) ingredients for 1 batch (~48 servs) note: you may be asked to make 2 batches, first read instructions below for how to do that...these are the quantities for one batch 1 ½ cup balsamic vinegar 2 cups water 2 tsp sherry vinegar 2tbls + 2 tsp dijon mustard 2 tsp agave 1 tsp black pepper ½ tsp salt 4 big cloves garlic minced in mini cuisinart (or 1 ½ tsp garlic powder– fresh is better, but maybe check diets for sensitivity to raw garlic) 2 cups olive oil 1 ¼ cups light olive oil instructions if making 2 batches, measure all but oils of both batches at the same time, putting the second batch quantities into a 4qt square container. mix all except oil in the vitamix until smooth. drizzle oils into vitamix mixing while you do. gradually increase speed until all emulsified. divide between 2 small pitchers. for second batch : pour measured container of ingredients into vitamix pitcher and blend. add second batch of oils as above. pour back into container, label, date and store in fridge for later.

title: Banana Bread with Almond Filling Swirl
text: all recipes / dessert banana bread with almond filling swirl tags: vegetarian, soy-free banana bread with an almond filling swirl. yield: 1 loaf (9×5-inch), keeps ~4 days wrapped (freezes well) ingredients almond filling 2 cups almond flour 3/4 cup granulated sugar 1 large egg 3 tbsp unsalted butter, melted 1/2 tsp almond extract banana bread 6 oz unsalted butter, melted and browned (just over 1/2 cup) 2 cups all-purpose flour 3/4 cup granulated sugar 1 tsp baking soda 1/2 tsp salt 3/4 tsp ground cinnamon 2 large eggs 1 tsp vanilla extract 1/4 cup yogurt 1 1/4 cup mashed banana (about 3 medium bananas) slivered almonds (for topping) powdered sugar (optional, for dusting) preparation make almond filling. mix egg, almond flour, sugar, almond extract, and melted butter. refrigerate. prep oven/pan. heat oven to 350°f. grease and flour a 9×5-inch loaf pan. brown butter. melt butter in a saucepan; cook until nutty-brown. transfer to a bowl to cool. mix dry. whisk flour, sugar, baking soda, salt, cinnamon (and nutmeg if you like). mix wet. whisk eggs, vanilla, and yogurt; whisk in mashed banana; whisk in cooled browned butter. combine. fold wet into dry just until combined (don't overmix). layer. add half batter to pan, spread half almond filling, add remaining batter, then remaining filling on top. sprinkle slivered almonds. bake. bake 50–60 minutes until a skewer comes out clean. cool. rest 15 minutes in pan, then remove and cool completely. dust with powdered sugar if desired.

title: Banana Nut Cookies
text: all recipes / dessert banana nut cookies tags: vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free, soy-free banana nut cookies (vegan gf has nuts) an original recipe of the spirit rock kitchen, especially mary schjeldahl yields approx. 2 dozen cookies ingredients: x2.5 = 5dz orig 2 dz 5 ¾ c 2 1/3 cups unsalted almonds, toasted 4 ¼ c 1 2/3 cups unsalted cashews, toasted 1 ⅔ c 2/3 cup very ripe bananas, frozen and then thawed 2 ½ t 1 tbs vanilla extract 1 ¼ c 1/2 cup maple syrup 2 ½ t 1 tsp baking powder <1tsp 1/3 tsp salt 2 ½ c 1 cup bittersweet chocolate chips directions: pre-heat oven to 350 degrees. using a food processor, finely grind almonds and cashews until they are slightly coarser than sand - don’t over-grind or they will become nut butter! remove nuts from food processor, then transfer to a large mixing bowl. place the thawed bananas, maple syrup, vanilla, baking powder and salt into the food processor. pulse until the mixture is smooth. using a spatula, fold this puree into the ground nuts. once these ingredients are incorporated, fold in the chocolate chips. using a cookie scoop (about 2 tbs), scoop dough into balls. keep mounded high for rounder, chewier cookies, or flatten slightly for crispier cookies. place dough balls onto a cookie sheet lined with parchment paper, or a silpat mat. bake for 10-15 minutes (or ~20) , or until cookies are baked through and turning golden. irc notes: maybe swap racks & turn trays at half the time, back & bottom of oven cooks faster. cool well before you try to pick them up.

title: Barley Vegetable Soup with White Bean
text: all recipes / soup barley vegetable soup with white bean tags: vegan, dairy-free, nut-free, soy-free barley-vegetable soup with white bean for 16 it is from allrecipes.com and says “all rights reserved”, although i modified it – below is what i actually did. just so you’re aware if using it at irc… ingredients 3 t olive oil 4 quarts vegetable broth 1 red onion, chopped 5 small cloves garlic, finely diced 1-3/4 cup uncooked barley 4 large carrots, chopped 6 stalks celery, chopped 2 zucchini, chopped 1 28-oz can diced tomatoes with juice 6 bay leaves 2 teaspoon salt 1 teaspoon ground black pepper 2 teaspoon dried parsley 2 teaspoon curry powder 2 teaspoon smoked paprika 2 teaspoon red wine vinegar 2 (15 ounce) cans white beans (cannellini), drained directions heat the olive oil in a large pot (12-qt). add online and garlic, and saute for a few minutes. add carrots, celery, zucchini, vegetable broth, barley, tomatoes, and bay leaves. season with salt, pepper, parsley, curry powder, smoked paprika, and vinegar. bring to a boil, then cover and simmer over medium-low heat for 60-75 minutes. add beans after about 45 minutes (*). remove bay leaves before serving. (*) i added them with all the other ingredients, but found that they broke down a bit too much. i think adding them later would be better.

title: Basil Salad Dressing
text: all recipes / salad basil salad dressing tags: vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free, nut-free, soy-free recipe: basil salad dressing equipment vitamix, 2 pitchers, (extra 2qt square container with green lid for second batch) ingredients for 1 batch (~48 servs) 1 cup lemon juice 4-5 lemons ½ cup rice vinegar 1 ½ cup water 1 tsp garlic powder ¼ cup dijon mustard ¼ cup agave ½ tsp salt ¾ cup packed down fresh basil leaves (pick off from stems) (= ~¾ of a bunch) ¼ cup packed down fresh parsley (cut off main trunk of stems, ok to use rest) (=~¼ of a bunch) 3 ½ cups light olive oil instructions rinse herbs, no need to chop, vitamix will do it. add all except oils in vitamix container and mix on low. if making 2 batches, measure a second batch except oils into square container. drizzle oils into vitamix mixing while you do. gradually increase speed until all emulsified. divide between 2 small pitchers. for second batch: pour measured container ingredients into vitamix and blend. add second batch of oils as above. pour back into container, label, date and store in fridge for later.

title: Black Bean Soup - Once Upon a Chef
text: all recipes / soup black bean soup - once upon a chef tags: neither, gluten-free, nut-free, soy-free 5/13/2018 black bean soup - once upon a chef https://www.onceuponachef.com/recipes/black-bean-soup.html?recipe_print=yes 1/2 black bean soup by jennifer segal servings: 4 total time: 30 minutes ingredients 2 tablespoons extra virgin olive oil 2 medium yellow onions, roughly chopped 4 large garlic cloves, crushed and peeled 2 carrots, peeled and roughly chopped 2 (15-ounce) cans black beans, drained and rinsed 5 cups low sodium chicken broth (i like swanson) 3/4 teaspoon oregano 1 teaspoon ground coriander 1-3/4 teaspoons ground cumin 1/8 teaspoon cayenne pepper 1/2 teaspoon salt 1 tablespoon fresh lime juice 1/3 cup sour cream handful chopped fresh cilantro instructions heat the olive oil over medium heat in a large soup pan. add the onions, garlic cloves and carrots and cook, stirring occasionally, until onions are soft and translucent, about 8 minutes. do not brown. add the black beans, chicken broth, oregano, coriander, cumin, cayenne pepper and salt and bring to a boil. reduce the heat, cover and simmer gently for about 15 minutes. purée the soup using a hand-held immersion blender until very smooth and creamy. (alternatively, you can use a standard blender to puree the soup in batches; see note.) stir in the lime juice and season with salt and pepper to taste. ladle the soup into bowls and top each bowl with a dollop of sour cream and freshly chopped cilantro. note: if using a standard blender, purée the soup in batches, being careful not to fill the jar more than halfway. be sure to leave the hole in the lid open and loosely cover with a dish towel to allow the heat to escape. pour the blended soup into a clean pot. 5/13/2018 black bean soup - once upon a chef https://www.onceuponachef.com/recipes/black-bean-soup.html?recipe_print=yes 2/2 serving size: about 2 cups calories: 475 fat: 14g saturated fat: 4g carbohydrates: 66g sugar: 5g fiber: 21g protein: 27g sodium: 424mg cholesterol: 10mg nutrition information powered by per serving (4 servings) copyright © once upon a chef https://www.onceuponachef.com/recipes/black-bean-soup.html

title: Black Eyed Peas with Walnuts and Pomegranate
text: all recipes / side black eyed peas with walnuts and pomegranate tags: vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free, soy-free black eyed peas with walnuts and pomegranate from cooks mediterranean 4-5 qts leftover, could be about right for full house this filled lael’s large bowl heaped up (or a med-large metal bowl) off-season suggestions: cranberries & celery?? (but cran & pommol???) x7 for 38 1 ¼ c 3 t evoo 1 ¼ c 3 t dukkah //see recipe below 14 t = ¾ cup+2t 2 t lemon juice & zest of 2-3 lemons 14 t = ¾ cup+2t 2 t pomegranate molasses s&p to taste 14@15oz or 7 28 oz 2 15 oz cans black eyed peas, rinsed note: 1 can = 1 ¾ cups note: 3lbs dry=scan 5qts cooled, added 4 cans = 6qts/24 cups beans 3 ½ c ½ c walnuts toasted and chopped 3 ½ c //used 3 lg poms ½ c pom seeds 3 ½ c //used ~2c ½ cup minced parsley 28 4 scallions sliced thin whisk evoo, ¾ cup of the dukkah, lemon, pom.molasses, 1 ½ t salt, 1t pepper until smooth add black-eyed peas, walnuts, pom seeds, parsley & scallions & toss. season as needed with s & p //i added some aleppo pepper, meh sprinkle with rest of dukkah as garnish *fancy homemade dukkah (or use tjs) 2 cups: 1 15oz can chickpeas 1 t evoo ½ cup pistachios toasted 1/3 cup black sesame seeds, toasted 2 ½ t coriander seeds, toasted 1 t cumin seeds, toasted 2 t fennel seeds, toasted 1 ½ t pepper 1 ¼ t salt preheat oven to 400 rinse & drain & pat chickpeas dry toss with oil, roast until brown and crisp 40-45 mins stirring every 5-10 mins process in food processor until coarse ground pulse pistacious & sesame to coarse ground pulse cor, cum & fen to fine ground add pepper & salt & whisk

title: Black Bean Soup Blended
text: all recipes / soup black bean soup blended tags: vegetarian, gluten-free, nut-free, soy-free recipe: blended black bean soup page 1 of 2 equipment 32qt (largest) stock pot with pot-saver under it ingredients if using dry beans: soak overnight, allow ~1 ½ - 2 hours to cook the beans before adding them to the soup ~50 (~19qts) ~⅓ cup olive oil (to coat bottom of stock pot) 4lbs (~7ea) onions, ½” dice 7lbs carrots, ½ “ dice 25ea garlic cloves, chopped 10 qts cooked black beans = ~7 lbs dry black beans pre-cooked!! 1 jar btb bouillon: dissolve it in ~2qts hot tea-urn water 9 qts total water (2qts hot with bouillon as above, + remaining 7qts cold) 2 ½ t oregano 3 t + 1t ground coriander 5 t + 2t cumin 1 tsp taste cayenne pepper 1 t + to taste salt ½ cup + 1t = ~7ea fresh lime juice, save some zest in case needed //maybe more for avos 3 bu topping: cilantro 2 pints topping: sour cream // and/or see cashew green chili cream recipe 3 cups topping: roasted pumpkin seeds headct / 4 topping: avocadoes, diced and preserved with lime juice recipe: blended black bean soup page 2 of 2 instructions prepare ingredients locate all ingredients dice onions, carrots by hand, chop garlic in mini-cuisinart juice limes. juicer is near rice-cooker. maybe zest a couple and set zest aside. mix bouillon in 2 qts hot tea-urn water. note: this is not a long-cooking soup, about 1 ½ hrs from start to saute to finish blending. beans are pre-cooked separately. make soup be sure heat-saver disk (on stove shelf) is placed under stock pot coat the bottom of the pot with olive oil to about ⅛” deep sauté (=fry in a little oil uncovered, stirring occasionally) the onions, garlic and carrots until the onions are getting soft and translucent (not brown). add rest: black beans, bouillon, water, oregano, coriander, cumin, cayenne and salt. bring to a boil. reduce heat, cover and simmer ~30 minutes. check that carrots are soft. puree the soup until smooth and creamy (there will still be little flecks of beans) using the immersion blender. stir in lime juice and taste (perhaps more salt, pepper, lime zest?, cayenne?) serve with any or all of: cilantro, sour cream and/or vegan green chili cream, diced avocado and roasted pumpkin seeds.

title: Blue Cheese Dressing
text: all recipes / salad blue cheese dressing tags: vegetarian, gluten-free, nut-free, soy-free recipe: blue cheese dressing equipment vitamix, 2 pitchers ingredients //note: you will need to put some non-dairy leftover type out for no-dairy for 1 batch (~48 servs) 4 x 5oz tubs or 3x8oz (tjs) crumbled blue cheese (quality matters..) 3 cups milk ½ cup lemon juice ½ tsp salt (depends on brand of cheese...add slowly & taste) 1 tsp white pepper instructions add all in vitamix container and mix on low. add all to vitamix. gradually increase speed until all emulsified. divide between 2 small pitchers. cover & store in fridge (if not for today, label and date also). -->good to make early because it gets thicker as it sits.

title: Breakfast Stewed Fruit
text: all recipes / side breakfast stewed fruit tags: vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free, nut-free, soy-free breakfast stewed fruit setup the prunes to soak overnight : get the smallest short round 2-handled pot with lid. wash and thinly slice 1 orange including peel into the pot (slice it in half lengthwise, then in quarters lengthwise, then very thinly slice so making very thin quarter moon slices) oranges are usually in the back room middle fridge. wash and cut up a fresh apple and add to the mix also. apples are usually in the bottom of the kitchen pantry its also a good use of any pieces of apple or orange left on the public cutting board (you could collect these in the evening & put in fridge for this purpose). add ~7 cups prunes (or one costco bag) add one 3” cinnamon stick from the spice jars. fill with water to cover all the fruit plus about 1” of water. put the lid on, put the pot in left side of the kitchen fridge wherever you can find room. leave it to soak overnight. in the morning, the breakfast cook brings it to a boil and simmers for a few minutes while the oats cook. we can add to it and reheat for up to 3 days in a row, then start over.

title: Broccoli Cashew Soup
text: all recipes / soup broccoli cashew soup tags: vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free, soy-free vegan cheezy broccoli servings: 50 | difficulty: easy ingredients: 5 cups cashews water 4 lbs onions diced 3/4 cup minced garlic 8 quarts water 8 lbs broccoli 4 lbs potatoes 1 container better than bouillon vegetarian stock 2 cups nutritional yeast juice of lemons to taste (optional) directions: 1. cover raw cashews with water by 2 inches and let sit for 1-2 hrs for cashews to absorb water and soften. blend cashews in water until creamy. 2. sautee onions in large stock pot until soft. add garlic and sauté for 1-2 minutes stirring frequently. 3. add remaining ingredients. bring to a boil and lower to a simmer. once broccoli is cooked, about 15-20 minutes blend with an emulsifying blender. add lemon to taste. sent from paprika recipe manager. http://www.paprikaapp.com from jessica

title: Broccoli-Ricotta Lasagna
text: all recipes / entree broccoli-ricotta lasagna tags: vegetarian, nut-free, soy-free a simple broccoli-and-ricotta lasagna with béchamel and smoked scamorza. yield: ~6 portions (as written) ingredients fresh lasagna sheets — 250 g (or no-boil sheets) broccoli, cleaned — 500 g ricotta — 200 g (sheep's milk if possible) béchamel — 500 ml parmesan, grated — 100 g smoked scamorza, cubed — 100 g salt, to taste béchamel milk — 500 ml butter — 50 g white flour or cornstarch — 50 g salt — a pinch preparation make béchamel. in a pan, whisk milk + butter + salt + flour/cornstarch before heating to dissolve lumps. cook, stirring constantly, until thickened (~10 minutes). prep broccoli + ricotta. steam broccoli, then mash with a fork. reserve ~3 tbsp broccoli for topping. mix ricotta with mashed broccoli. prep cheese. cube smoked scamorza. assemble. spread a layer of béchamel in the pan. add a layer of pasta, then béchamel, parmesan, scamorza, and broccoli-ricotta. repeat until used up; finish with béchamel + reserved broccoli + parmesan. bake. bake at 240°c covered with foil until bubbling, then reduce to 200°c and bake 30–40 minutes total. remove foil for the last ~5 minutes to brown lightly. serve. cool briefly, slice, and serve. for reheating leftovers, add a splash of milk and warm in a pan.

title: Broccoli Salad
text: all recipes / salad broccoli salad tags: neither, gluten-free, dairy-free, soy-free broccoli salad servings: 12 servings calories: 260 kcal author: trish - mom on timeout ingredients 1 cup light mayonnaise 1/3 cup sugar 2 tbsp red wine vinegar 1 tsp celery seed 2 heads of broccoli broken down into small florets 3/4 lb bacon cooked and chopped into small pieces-- 1/2 cup toasted slivered almonds 2 green onions thinly sliced 1 cup chopped celery 1 1/2 cups red seedless grapes halved instructions whisk together mayonnaise, sugar, red wine vinegar, and celery seed in a small bowl. place in refrigerator for at least 30 minutes. combine broccoli, bacon , toasted almonds, green onions, celery and grapes in a large serving dish. (to toast almonds, place on a large baking sheet and bake at 350f for 3-5 minutes stirring in between. do not walk away! they will burn easily. the almonds are toasted when they turn light brown.) toss the dressing with the rest of the salad ingredients and stir. dressing can be added at the last minute if desired. nutrition calories: 260 kcal | carbohydrates: 19 g | protein: 7 g | fat: 18 g | saturated fat: 4 g | cholesterol: 21 mg | sodium: 368 mg | potassium: 477 mg | fiber: 3 g | sugar: 11 g | vitamin a: 14.5 % | vitamin c: 111.1 % | calcium: 7.2 % | iron: 6.9 %

title: BROCCOLI SOUP FROM DEBORAH MADISON
text: all recipes / soup broccoli soup from deborah madison tags: vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free, nut-free broccoli soup from deborah madison vegetable soups from deborah madison's kitchen (via lael) 42 ~6 x7 14lbs scant 2 pounds broccoli (3 or 4 broccoli “trees”) to saute 1 tablespoon neutral oil, safflower etc. 6 onion, thinly sliced or finely diced 7 large garlic clove, chopped (2 jalapeño chile seeded and diced ) 7t ginger, peeled and chopped 1 ¾ cup minced cilantro stems and/or chopped cilantro leaves 7 small potato, 10 qts water //added in two stages note: not veggie broth grated sea salt to taste 1 cup white miso // if no-soy people, save some out & add last roasted sesame oil 1. separate the broccoli crowns from the stalks and cut them into florets more or less the same ﻿size, small or large. thickly peel the stalks so that none of the thick fibrous outer layer remains, then slice them thinly. 2. heat the oil in a wide soup pot. when hot, add the onion, garlic, chile, ginger, and cilantro and sauté, stirring rapidly, for 1 minute. add the potato and broccoli stems, season with a scant teaspoon salt, add ~2qts of the water, and simmer, covered, until the onion is soft, about 5 minutes. add the broccoli florets and rest of the water and simmer just until the broccoli is tender, 5 to 10 minutes once it comes to a boil. let cool briefly, then puree until smooth, leaving only minuscule nubbins of broccoli. 3. save some out for no-soy diets, then mix the miso with some of the soup to dilute it, then pour it back into the pot. taste for salt. 4. stir in with ~1 t toasted sesame oil.

title: Brownies Vegan GF
text: all recipes / dessert brownies vegan gf tags: vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free, soy-free brownies (vegan & gf) --based on minimalistbaker.com version note: one 2” hotel pan can serve 52 by cutting 8x6 & cut large corners in half, or might want a second half-pan for more. 1 ½ pans 1 pan 4.5 c=3 ¾ tubs 3 cups vegan butter eg. earth balance (=2 ½ tubs) 6 ¾ cups 4.5 cups cane sugar 18=1c+1t ve,,2 1/4c water 12 vegan eggs (eg bob’s ¾ cup powder in 1 ½ cups water) 3t 2t vanilla 3t 2t baking powder 2 ¼ tsp 1 ½ t salt 4.5 cups 3 cups cocoa powder 6 ¾ cups 4.5 cups gluten free flour (eg bob’s 1-1) optional: 3 cups 2 cups walnuts or pecans preheat oven to 350 and spray hotel pan. prepare vegan eggs in small bowl, whisk well & let rest for 5 minutes. melt earthbal on stove in sauce pan. mix melted earthbal, sugar, vanilla, vegan-eggs, baking powder, salt and cocoa powder in large bowl. whisk to combine. lastly add the flour in stages and combine. fold in nuts if using. fill pan or muffin tins (¾ full). bake for 22-26 minutes (or more like 35--check often). shake hotel pan and done when center is stable and sides are pulling away. remove and let rest & cool for serving. serve or store in airtight container for a couple of days or freeze. yummy with or without ice cream ;-).

title: Caesar Salad Dressing (Vegan)
text: all recipes / salad caesar salad dressing (vegan) tags: vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free, soy-free recipe: vegan caesar salad dressing equipment vitamix, juicer, 2 pitchers ingredients for 1 batch (~48 servs) 3 ½ cups raw cashews, soaked (could be overnight, at least 2 hrs) 1 ¾ cup water ¾ cup + 2t ev olive oil 7 t lemon juice 3 ½ t dijon mustard 3 ½ tsp garlic powder 6 small cloves of garlic 3 ½ t vegan worcestershire sauce (wizard’s...might be some in top of fridge) 4 tbls + 2 tsp capers ~1 tsp each salt & pepper (adjust to taste) instructions soak cashews covered with water (ideally km would do this early). juice lemons with juicer. add all except salt & pepper in vitamix container and mix on low. add salt & pepper to taste cover & store in fridge (if not for today, label and date also).

title: Carmelized Onion Black Bean Dip
text: all recipes / side carmelized onion black bean dip tags: vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free, nut-free, soy-free carmelized onion black bean dip ingredients: 2 /15 oz cans black beans/drained and rinsed 4 medium red onions chopped 2 tbs olive oil 1 tbs balsamic vinegar 1/2 tsp salt 1/2 tsp paprika 1 tbs chopped parsley cook oil and onions for about 10 mins until golden brown add vinegar and salt and paprika and cook 2 mins longer process in blender for 20 to 40 seconds or until dip consistency garnish - with 1 tbs chopped parsley

title: Carrot Cashew Soup
text: all recipes / soup carrot cashew soup tags: vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free, soy-free carrot cashew soup (this needs work, placeholder, good enough for now) equipment : heaviest 32qt stock pot, immersion blender ingredients 1 4 lbs carrots //could pre-slice the day before in the robo coupe 3 lbs onions, diced 1 lb ginger (optional: up to 5lbs yams, raw or cooked, peeled & diced) 3lbs cashews 2t 5 spice powder instructions : cover cashews with water and soak for 1-2 hours (ie do it at start of veggie chop, leave it till 9:30) dice onions locate ~14lbs of carrots & maybe yams: excess already shredded, leftover roasted yams. chop the ginger in batches in the mini-chopper (grossly cut up first, no need to peel if organic). sauté the onions in the large rondo pan until getting soft (20-30 minutes?..not till browning). add carrots (and yams) and continue to sauté stirring often over low heat until some light browning, not too brown. while these sauté: puree the cashews in the vitamix (multiple batches if needed) add ginger and 5 spice powder & sauté another minute or two add cashew milk and water to bring it up to ~14 qts bring to a boil, reduce to simmer stirring frequently. after all ingredients are soft, use emersion blender to blend smooth. taste for seasonings and salt or add more 5 spice as needed, or salt, pepper, lemon juice? aim to have it about 170 degrees by lunch time. then turn off the gas and leave the pot covered on the stove. it should stay above 145 for the afternoon. reheat at 5:00 to bring it back to 165. optional: serve with yogurt if still leaves 2x32oz left for final breakfast.

title: Carrot Soup Tofu Spread
text: all recipes / soup carrot soup tofu spread tags: vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free carrot soup, tofu spread prep equipment: 24qt stock pot, med. plastic bowl ingredients for 44 (aiming to make 8qts beans not counting excess water) soup: carrots, chopped 13lbs onions, diced 4lbs ginger, chopped 2lbs ??garlic?? (yams, cubed or pulp) 10lbs or whatever is leftover water to make 19 qts, aiming for 18qts when done cashews 3lbs five spice powder 2t ??check with anna some of the below for the dip? tofu spread tofu 6lbs vegenaise 2c celery, fine dice 4c turmeric 2t dijon mustard 6t nut. yeast 6t parsley 1 bu dill or tarragon 1 bu scallions, chopped 3 bu corn cakes 8 packs carrot soup, tofu spread instructions: carrot soup puree the cashews in the robo coupe chop the carrots in the robo coupe ?? saute the onions in the stock pot until translucent. add carrots, ginger, (yams), cashews, 5-spice & water to stock pot. bring to a boil, reduce to active simmer, stir frequently. whisk or use emersion blender to blend smooth after all ingredients are cook very soft. taste for seasonings & salt. tofu salad crumble the tofu to the texture of crumbled eggs... wash & chop the herbs. add the other ingredients and mix. taste for salt, pepper, seasoning. refrigerate until serving time. serve with corn cakes. lunch: carrot soup, tofu salad (hearty items for salad bar..) supper: (help anna o. prep for celebration dinner). suggested meal timeline prev day pm veggie washers prev day pm preppers wash carrots, celery, scals & yams if time: make salad dressing ------------------- -------------------------------------- ---------------------------------------------------------------- 7:30 veggie choppers fine dice celery cube yams chop or robo the carrots lunch cook assist cook 9:30-10:15 chop onions finish veggie prep if needed saute onions crumble tofu start soup make tofu salad 10:15 – 11:00 finish above and help anna with supper? 11:00 – 12:00 blend the soup help anna with supper? put out crackers 12:00-12:15 put food out set up serving ware help put food out ------------------- -------------------------------------- ---------------------------------------------------------------- 2:30 (n/a..retreat ending) (n/a..retreat ending) 3:50 5:00

title: Cashew Green Chili Cream
text: all recipes / side cashew green chili cream tags: vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free, soy-free recipe: cashew green chili cream page 1 of 1 equipment vitamix ingredients goes well with “blended black bean soup” recipe. ~48-50 4 ½ cups cashews, soaked in water as long as overnight, or as short as needed. 2 cups water (fresh, for blending, not the soaking water) 5-6 sm cans *diced green chilis, drained (or start with a bit less water) ¼ cup lime juice 6 garlic cloves (blending will chop) 1 tsp salt ½ tsp ground cumin pinch (> ⅛ tsp) cayenne (if using mild chilis) instructions: soak cashews as long as you can (longer is smoother, but grainy is fine). drain them. add all ingredients to vitamix blender (works better than robocoupe for this. blend until smooth. taste and fiddle with seasonings until you like it! *confession: just guessing on the quantity of green chilis, i used about ¾ cups of a tastier, hotter, fancier bottled brand from new mexico...

title: Cashew Ranch Salad Dressing
text: all recipes / salad cashew ranch salad dressing tags: vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free, soy-free recipe: cashew “ranch” salad dressing equipment vitamix, 2 pitchers ingredients for 1 batch (~48 servs) 4 cups raw cashews 2 ¼ cups light olive oil ¾ cup apple cider vinegar 3 cups water 2 cloves (or ½ tsp) garlic cloves (or powder) 1 ½ tsp salt 1 ½ tbsp dill, fresh or dried 2 ½ tbsp parsley leaves, chopped 1 ½ tbsp oregano 1 tsp rosemary (check garden outside kitchen door, finely chop) 1 tsp pepper instructions add all ingredients to vitamix container and mix on low, slowly increasing speed until all pureed. taste and adjust seasonings if needed. divide between 2 small pitchers (save any extra in storage container). cover & store in fridge (if not for today, label and date also).

title: Cashew Whipped Cream (2)
text: all recipes / dessert cashew whipped cream (2) tags: vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free, soy-free cashew whipped cream https://healthyblenderrecipes.com/recipes/raw_vegan_vanilla_cashew_cream makes 1 ¼ cups. 1 cup raw unsalted cashews, soaked for 2 hours 1/2 cup (120ml) filtered water, plus more to taste 2 tablespoons maple syrup, plus more to taste 1 teaspoon vanilla, plus more to taste pinch salt drain the cashews, and discard the soaking water. pour the fresh 1/2 cup filtered water into the blender, and add the soaked cashews with the maple syrup, vanilla, and salt. blast on high for 30 to 60 seconds, until smooth and creamy. tweak water, sweetener, and vanilla to taste. transfer to a sealed container in the fridge, and chill for a few hours to thicken. the cream will keep in the fridge for about 5 days.

title: Cashew Whipped Cream
text: all recipes / dessert cashew whipped cream tags: vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free, soy-free cashew whipped “cream” 1 cup raw unsalted cashews , soaked for 2 hours 1/2 cup (120ml) filtered water, plus more to taste 2 tablespoons pure maple syrup , plus more to taste 1 teaspoon natural vanilla extract , plus more to taste pinch of celtic sea salt drain the cashews, and discard the soaking water. pour the fresh 1/2 cup filtered water into the blender, and add the soaked cashews with the maple syrup, vanilla, and salt. blast on high for 30 to 60 seconds, until smooth and creamy. tweak water, sweetener, and vanilla to taste. transfer to a sealed container in the fridge, and chill for a few hours to thicken. the cream will keep in the fridge for about 5 days.

title: Cauliflower Bake
text: all recipes / side cauliflower bake tags: vegetarian, gluten-free, nut-free, soy-free cauliflower bake //for a supper from hollyhock cookbook equip: lg skillet, 2 2” deep hotel pans, container for no-dairy portion (to be reheated on stove top) ingredients enough canola oil to saute the onions (~1/2 cup?) 3qts chopped onions 8 leeks rinsed & chopped ¼ cup crushed garlic 6 coarsely chopped heads of cauliflower 2t dried dill //or ¼ cup fresh if some is around 4 cups rough chopped kalamata olives (or no more than one jar..)//be sure no pits! 1 cup chopped parsley 4 tsp black pepper 2 tsp salt 8 cups grated cheese (cheddar or feta or swiss/gruyere mix) 12 cups cooked quinoa or rice paprika to garnish directions km: try to do this during veg chop period: set up a steamer set to steam the cauliflower for ~5 minutes (not all the way done). km: perhaps even do this in the veg period: in the large skillet, saute the onion and leeks in the oil until transparent. mix all ingredients except cheese in a very large bowl. set aside no-cheese portion in smaller put-away container (this will be reheated with some stock on the stove top later). est. ~ 1 cup each for no-dairy people. mix cheese into remaining mixture in the big bowl. spray the hotel pans with oil. divide between the 2 hotel pans. sprinkle with a bit of paprika for garnish. cover & fridge. at night: bake at 350 for 30-40 minutes (so put in cold into un-preheated oven before talk…should be ok for an hour). mix some bouillon (from jar) and add enough to moisten the no-cheese part…heat in a sauce pan on the stove.

title: Cauliflower Recipe
text: all recipes / side cauliflower recipe tags: vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free, nut-free, soy-free day 4 recipe: cauliflower and pea page 1 of 2 equipment ~3 large baking sheets (as needed for single-layer) note: some kms prefer to skip this recipe and just steam or roast plain cauliflower--consult km, if steaming, start it about 11:30, if roasting, about 11:15. ingredients #servings with supper leftovers #servings no supper leftovers [qty] [qty] [ingredient description] 1 case + 3 extra heads ~1 case cauliflower chopped into bite size trees 3lbs..[note bag size, if 10oz, use 4 bags] frozen peas 1 ½ cups olive oil 3t ground coriander 3t ground cumin 4 ½ t curry powder 3t turmeric 3t ground ginger add after cauliflower is roasted 3t ground fresh ginger 3t lime zest or amchur mango powder if we have any salt and pepper day 4 recipe: cauliflower and pea page 2 of 2 instructions turn on oven to 400 degrees mix oil coriander, cumin, curry powder, turmeric and ground ginger. in the largest bowl, in two batches, add the cauliflower and coat in spice mixture lay cauliflower evenly on baking sheets cook about 45 minutes starting at 11:15 about 11:45, add the peas and cook another 10-15 minutes or until cauliflower is tender remove from oven, combine trays into large serving bowl and sprinkle with grated lime (or amchur) and fresh ginger. squeeze a little lime juice to taste with salt and pepper if you wish.

title: Chai Apple Crumb Cake
text: all recipes / dessert chai apple crumb cake tags: vegetarian, nut-free, soy-free a chai-spiced apple crumb cake with optional glaze. prep time: ~40 minutes cook time: ~50 minutes total: ~1.5 hours yield: 1 (9") cake, ~12 slices ingredients chai spice mix 2 1/2 tsp ground cinnamon 1/2 tsp each: allspice, cardamom, cloves, ginger chai apples 3 small apples, peeled & thinly sliced 40 g light brown sugar (about 3 tbsp) 1 tbsp chai spice mix streusel 60 g unsalted butter (1/4 cup), melted 90 g light brown sugar (1/3 cup + 1 tbsp) 120 g all-purpose flour (1 cup) 1 1/2 tsp chai spice mix butter cake 210 g all-purpose flour (1 3/4 cups) 2 tsp baking powder 1/2 tsp salt 125 g unsalted butter (1/2 cup + 1 tbsp), room temp 175 g granulated sugar (3/4 cup + 2 tbsp) 2 eggs, room temp 2 tsp vanilla 135 g whole milk (1/2 cup + 2 tbsp), room temp 75 g sour cream (5 tbsp), room temp 180 g apple butter (2/3 cup), optional optional glaze 90 g powdered sugar 1–2 tbsp reserved chai-apple juices (or milk) preparation prep pan. heat oven to 350°f / 175°c. generously butter a 9" pan. press in parchment (crumple/uncrumple helps it fit). make chai apples. toss sliced apples with brown sugar + chai spice. set aside and save the juices for glaze. make streusel. mix melted butter + brown sugar + flour + chai spice with a fork until clumpy. make batter. whisk flour + baking powder + salt. beat butter + sugar 3–4 min until fluffy. beat in eggs + vanilla (~1 min). mix in half the dry ingredients, then sour cream + milk, then remaining dry — fold gently. assemble. spread half batter in pan. dollop/spread apple butter (optional). add remaining batter. top with apples (leave juices behind). sprinkle streusel on top. bake. bake 40–50 minutes until a toothpick comes out clean / with a few moist crumbs. cool. cool until manageable, then lift out using parchment. optional glaze. whisk powdered sugar with reserved apple juices (or a splash of milk) to desired consistency; drizzle over cake.

title: Chai
text: all recipes / side chai tags: vegetarian, gluten-free, nut-free, soy-free chai surya 1 gal water 1/3 cup grated ginger a spice ginder top full of whole green cardomon + it whole coriander tsp whole cloves not ground cinnamon stick simmer for an hour sit overnight to steep bring back to a boil add a palm of loose black tea (assam, breakfast, darjeeling) add ½-1 cup sugar cook 5-10 minutes strain & cool = chai base serve 3:1 whole milk, reheat //for me, all of above + 2/3 gal of milk, served 18 good source of cheap cardamom: united natural foods frontier herb about #l = $15 but you need to find a non-profit that bulk orders from them to piggyback onto chai masala (indian spiced tea) published: december 7, 2010 4 teaspoons tea leaves 1 teaspoon coarsely chopped ginger (no need to peel) 2 green cardamom pods, cracked 1/2 cup milk sugar, to taste. pour six cups water, tea, ginger, and cardamom into a saucepan, bring to a boil and cook 3 minutes. add milk, and sugar to taste, and boil 2 minutes more. strain and serve.

title: Cilantro Lime Salad Dressing
text: all recipes / salad cilantro lime salad dressing tags: vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free, nut-free, soy-free recipe: cilantro lime salad dressing equipment vitamix, 2 pitchers, (extra 2qt square container with green lid for second batch) ingredients taste this and adjust recipe please, needs testing for 1 batch (~48 servs) note: you may be asked to make 2 batches, first read instructions below for how to do that...these are the quantities for one batch 1 ½ cup lime juice ¾ cup lemon juice 4 cloves garlic 1 ½ tbls sugar 2 tsp salt 1 tsp ground cumin 1 tsp ground coriander 1 ½ cup cilantro 1 ½ cups olive oil 2 ¼ cups light olive oil instructions add all except oils in vitamix container and mix on low. if making 2 batches, measure a second batch except oils into square container. drizzle oils into vitamix mixing while you do. gradually increase speed until all emulsified. divide between 2 small pitchers. for second batch: pour measured container ingredients into vitamix and blend. add second batch of oils as above. pour back into container, label, date and store in fridge for later.

title: Cowboy Cookies Vegan GF
text: all recipes / dessert cowboy cookies vegan gf tags: vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free, soy-free cowboy cookies (vegan, gf) from moosewood restaurant favorites yield: approximately 60 large cookies put 4x6=24 each on 2 lg + 3x4=12 on half-size baking sheets = 60 5 cups gf flour 2 ½ tsp baking soda 1 ½ tsp baking powder 1 ½ tsp salt ---- 2 ½ c earthbalance 1 ¼ c sugar 1 ¼ c brown sugar 5 “vegan eggs” look for packets in pantry 2 ½ tsp vanilla --- 4 c. oats (should be gf, warn if not) 2 c. coconut (ideally large flake, else whatever) 3 c. choc chips 2 c. raisins or mix of raisins & cranberries 3 c. chopped nuts (any or mix of walnuts, pecans, slivered almonds) directions-->over directions: preheat both ovens to 350. mix vegan egg with water per directions on package, let sit until ready to use. in a large bowl, whisk together flour, baking powder, baking soda, and salt. in a separate large bowl, use electric mixer to beat sugars with earthbalance until very well mixed. beat in vegan eggs and vanilla. if the red table mixer is available, use it for next step. else use large spoon & spatula. it’s pretty stiff: add the flour mixture to the sugar mixture. add oats. put on latex gloves and mix in all the goodies (nuts, fruit, chips) by hand. line 2 large, 1 half sheet pan with parchment. make large scoops (~¼ cup or a little more) with your gloved hands, flatten onto the sheets pans. bake ~20 mins, time varies, start checking at 15. should be medium brown on bottom, very light brown on top. cool on racks. store in red-snap lid boxes (kept above kitchen desk).

title: Creamy Avocado
text: all recipes / salad creamy avocado tags: vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free, nut-free, soy-free avocado dressing updated by chris 7/30/2015 to remove yogurt so its vegan 1 ½ qts : ½ cup water 1 ¼ cup lime/lemon juice (~4 limes, rest lemons) 4 lg avocadoes 1/3 c. cilantro ½ tsp garlic powder ½ tsp cumin ½ tsp white pepper ½ tsp salt 3 ¾ cups canola oil add all except oil to the blender. blend. drizzle in the oil while mixing (or just pour it all in & mix, works fine..) for one meal: fill 2 small pitchers.

title: Brown Rice
text: all recipes / side brown rice tags: vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free, nut-free, soy-free week 2 day 1 recipe:brown rice page 1 of 1 equipment large strainer, rice cooker ingredients #servings with supper leftovers #servings no supper leftovers or ~36 with supper [qty] [qty] [ingredient description] 14 cups 12 cups short grain brown rice (preferred) 16 cups 14 cups water (ratio = 1r:1w + 2 cups) or--- --- --- 14 cups 12 cups brown basmati rice 21 cups 18 cups water (ratio = 1r:1.5w) instructions ~10:30-11 rinse the rice well using the large double-mesh strainer (may take several batches). put the damp rice in the cooker. about 11:00 add water to the rice in cooker per above. plug in and turn on the cooker. it will take about 50-60mins to cook, then it switches to warm. before serving, check that is has switched to warm. if so, carefully open the lid and fluff it with a wood or plastic tool . serve with wooden spoons so as not to scratch the container.

title: Blended Simple Black Bean Soup
text: all recipes / soup blended simple black bean soup tags: vegetarian, gluten-free, nut-free, soy-free recipe: blended black bean soup page 1 of 2 equipment 32 qt (largest) stock pot with pot-saver under it ingredients if using dry beans: soak overnight, allow ~1-2 hours to cook before adding them to the soup for ~50 (~19qts) for ~36 w supper with some leftover as a base for a supper soup with lots of added veggies & broth, tomatoes etc. ~⅓ cup ~⅓ cup olive oil (to coat bottom of stock pot) 4lbs (~7ea) 3lbs onions, ½” medium/large dice - rough chop 7lbs 5 ½ lbs carrots, ½ “ medium/large dice - rough chop 25ea 20ea garlic cloves, chopped 10 qts cooked = ~4.5 qts dry 8qts cooked ~3.6 qts dry black beans [or ~13 29oz cans!!] [or 6.6lbs dry for shopping, best to measure in quarts] 1 jar btb ¾ jar bouillon: dissolve it in ~2qts hot tea-urn water ~9 qts total 7.5 qts total water (use 2qts hot with bouillon as above, + bean cooking or canned water, plus remaining cold to reach the total on left.) 2 ½ t 2 t oregano 3 t + 1t 3t ground coriander 5 t + 2t 4.5 t cumin 1 tsp taste ¾ t cayenne pepper 1 t + to taste 1t to taste salt ½ cup + 1t = ~7ea ½ cup fresh lime juice, save some zest in case needed //maybe more for avos 3 bu 2 bu topping: cilantro 3 pints 2 ½ pints topping: sour cream maybe mixed with green chilies //and/or see vegan cashew green chili cream recipe 3 cups 3 cups topping: roasted pumpkin seeds recipe: blended black bean soup page 2 of 2 instructions prepare ingredients cook the beans if not using canned. empty soak water, cover by 2” with fresh water, save (&measure?) cooking water to use as part of the soup liquid. dice onions, carrots by hand, chop garlic in mini-cuisinart juice limes. juicer is near rice-cooker. maybe zest a couple and set zest aside. mix bouillon in 2 qts hot tea-urn water. note: this is not a long-cooking soup, about 1 ½ hrs from start to saute to finish blending. beans are cooked separately. make soup be sure heat-saver disk (on stove shelf) is placed under stock pot coat the bottom of the pot with olive oil to about ⅛” deep sauté (=fry in a little oil uncovered, stirring occasionally) the onions, garlic and carrots until the onions are getting soft and translucent (not brown). drain beans saving liquid and use the liquid as part of the water measure. add rest: black beans, bouillon, water, oregano, coriander, cumin, cayenne and salt. bring to a boil. reduce heat, cover and simmer ~30 minutes. check that carrots are soft. puree the soup until smooth and creamy (there will still be little flecks of beans) using the immersion blender. stir in lime juice and taste (perhaps more salt, pepper, lime zest?, cayenne?) serve with any or all of: cilantro, sour cream and/or vegan green chili cream, diced avocado and roasted pumpkin seeds.

title: Kale with Mushrooms
text: all recipes / side kale with mushrooms tags: vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free, nut-free, soy-free week 2 day 2 recipe: kale with mushrooms page 1 of 1 equipment roasting sheet, 2 steamer pan setups ingredients #48 (lunch only) ~⅓ cup? olive oil, enough to lightly coat sliced mushrooms 1 case + 6 heads dino kale dino kale, de-stemmed and torn each leaf-side into 3-4 pieces 4lbs sliced mushrooms instructions first thing in the morning (ie before you need the oven for the tofu): pre-heat oven to 350 toss sliced mushrooms in olive oil, spread on baking sheet. roast for ~15-30 minutes at 350. time depends on how thick they were sliced. check every 10 mins, stir, swap pans on oven shelves as needed. set aside when done (= appealing to eat in your opinion!) or: some prefer to saute them in the largest skillet (check overhead rack or in apron area for large skillets0 ~11:00 about 11:00: steam kale using 2 steamer setups. it will probably take two rounds of 2 steamers each. each one takes about 10 minutes to cook the kale. or: some prefer to saute the kale in the rondo (big round pan under the rice cooker) transfer cooked kale layering with roasted mushrooms into a 4” deep hotel pan to serve. cover to keep warm.

title: Vegan GF Cornbread
text: all recipes / side vegan gf cornbread tags: vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free, nut-free, soy-free tab 3 vegan gluten free cornbread adapted from nisha vora rainbowplantlife.com this fits nicely in two 2”deep hotel pans each cut 6x8. this can take a couple of hours of off & on attention from someone (km?) so consider that. some approx. times below. measurements with “g” need a precision grams scale (we have one or more above the spice shelf, looks like an ipad). ingredients: ½ gallon oatly full fat oat milk (from whole fds) 4 tbls apple cider vinegar 1170g stone-ground medium corn meal (not the polenta, that is too coarse) 564g gluten free all-purpose flour 8tbls=½ cup baking powder 3 tsp salt 336g vegan butter, melted 336g extra virgin olive oil 240g brown sugar 504g agave 24g=6t finely chopped (use spice grinder) rosemary (from the kitchen garden) directions (timing aiming for still warm to serve): preheat oven to 400 (with the vulcan, try 450 and watch it) ~10:15? stir vinegar and oat milk and set aside at least 10-20 minutes to curdle in a large bowl combine flour, cornmeal, baking powder and salt. whisk well. ~10:30? pour in the melted vegan butter, oil, brown sugar, agave & curdled oatmilk. careful not to overmix, some lumps ok. should look like pancake mix. fold in the rosemary. allow batter to rest 10min to 1 hour. ~11:10 heat the empty pans in the over while batter is resting for about 10 minutes. remove from over, add more lumps of vegan butter to melt and coat the pan. sprinkle pan bottom with cornmeal. pour in batter, dividing between 2 pans. ~11:20 bake 25-35 minutes (in vulcan, rotate frount/back and top/bottom half way thru, might take longer than 25. test with toothpick or knife. cool for 15 mins before slicing 6x8 each pan.

title: Steamed or Roasted Green Beans
text: all recipes / side steamed or roasted green beans tags: vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free, nut-free, soy-free week 2 day 3 recipe: roasted or steamed green beans page 1 of 1 roasted (and steamed a bit first on the trays..): equipment: 2 large baking trays, foil toss beans in olive oil, sprinkle with salt and maybe pepper. heat oven to 350 these will need to be done early to have time for the tempeh to use the oven. they can be served room temp. we found it best to “steam” them for 20-30 minutes first by covering the trays of beans with foil, when almost soft enough to eat, remove the foil and roast for another ~10 mins until slightly browning. or simple steamed: equipment steamer pan setup (either 1 re-used for 2 batches or 2 setups) you may need to wash the steamer pans used for the tempeh to reuse for the beans. these can be done anytime and served either warm or room temp. steam the beans for ??20 minutes until they are as soft as you like them. be sure to check that the water doesn’t all boil off.

title: Quinoa
text: all recipes / side quinoa tags: vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free, nut-free, soy-free day 6 (or alt 5) recipe: quinoa page 1 of 1 equipment rice cooker ingredients serves ~50 with supper leftover if no supper or for 36 9 cups 8c quinoa (red, white or mix,whatever we have, all cooks the same) 11 ¼ cups 10c water (1q:1.25w) instructions rinse the quinoa very thoroughly or it has a bitter taste, using the large double-mesh strainer (may take several batches). you can do this early and let it sit in the turned-off rice cooker. about 11:00: add water. plug in and turn on the cooker. it will take about 45mins to cook, then it switches to warm. let it sit for a few minutes, then carefully open the lid and fluff it with a wood or plastic tool . unplug the machine to turn off the “warming”. serve with wooden spoons so as not to scratch the container.
