title: Fennel Leek Potato Soup
text: all recipes / soup fennel leek potato soup tags: vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free, nut-free, soy-free fennel leek potato soup for supper for 36 (created on the fly 10/27/16) saute 4 chopped onion add 7 chopped garlic cloves & saute add 4 each chopped carrot and celery stalks chopped 9 leeks, 6 bulb fennel and 10lbs? yukon gold potatoes saute all that awhile and add better than bouillon "no-chicken" broth paste & water per jar instructions (enough to look soup-like) add ~1t oregano immersion blend some of the soup & leave some whole. salt & pepper to taste we served this with a caesar salad (parm, croutons, romaine, see vegan caeaer dressing).

title: Frittata Lunch Recipe Two Quantities First go
text: all recipes / entree frittata lunch recipe two quantities first go tags: vegetarian, gluten-free, nut-free, soy-free recipe: frittata equipment rondo, two full 2 inch hotel pans and 1half 2 inch hotel pans ingredients #servings with supper leftovers #servings no supper leftovers 10lbs mushrooms sliced 1 cup olive oil split in two 7 lbs greens roughly chopped 6 cups onions chopped 30 cloves garlic 4 cups parmesan cheese 8 dozen eggs 4 cups half and half 24 scallions chopped 4 cup smoked gruyere cheese for beans: 6 to 8 -29oz cans cannellini beans drained and rinsed ? cups mushrooms and veggies recipe: frittata instructions cook veggies preheat oven to 425 degrees. heat rondo on medium heat and add oil to pan. once hot add mushrooms allowing to brown on each side. once mushrooms are browned add onion and cook until tender. then add garlic for and cook for a min or two until fragrant and add greens until wilted. remove approximately ⅓ of veggie mixture for bean salad. constructing frittata while veggies are cooking, mix eggs, half and half, parmesan cheese and scallions. add veggie mixture to egg mixture and place in 2 full hotel pans and sprinkle with gruyere cheese. place in oven at 11 am and cook for 45-60 min or until frittata is firm in center. remove from oven and cut into 24 portions per pan. for bean salad add 6-29? ounce cans cannellini beans to veggies. taste to ensure flavor.

title: Frittata Lunch Recipe Two Quantities
text: all recipes / entree frittata lunch recipe two quantities tags: vegetarian, gluten-free, nut-free, soy-free recipe: frittata equipment rondo, two full 2 in hotel pans ingredients #servings with supper leftovers #servings no supper leftovers 7-10 lbs veggies of choice (red pepper, zucchini, kale, spinach, mushroom etc…) 6 cups onions sliced 30 cloves garlic olive oil 4 cups parmesan cheese 10 dozen eggs 5 cups milk or half and half if you have on-hand 24 scallions chopped 4-6 cups cheese shredded or crumbled 2-29 oz cans white beans recipe: frittata instructions cook veggies preheat oven to 350 degrees. heat rondo on medium heat and add oil to pan. once hot add onions. once onions begin to get tender add garlic and cook for a min or two until fragrant. add chopped veggies of km’s choice constructing frittata while veggies are cooking, mix eggs, milk, parmesan cheese and scallions. once veggies are cooked reserve 2 cups of veggie mixture for alternative diet folks if relevant this meal. then proceed to add veggies to two hotel pans evenly. top veggies with cheese and pour egg mixture over, distributing between two pans evenly. place in oven at 11:00 am and cook until frittata is firm in center 45-60 min. remove from oven and cut into 24 portions per pan. for bean salad add 2- 29 oz cans white beans to reserved veggies. taste to ensure flavor, salt and pepper as needed.

title: Galette (Sweet or Savory)
text: all recipes / dessert galette (sweet or savory) tags: vegetarian, nut-free, soy-free a basic galette dough (sweet or savory) plus filling ideas. yield: 1 large galette (about 14-inch round) ingredients (dough) 1 1/2 cups flour 1 1/2 tsp sugar (sweet only; omit for savory) 1/4 tsp salt 8 tbsp cold unsalted butter, cubed (1/2" pieces) 1/3 cup ice water 2 tbsp melted butter (for brushing) turbinado/raw sugar (sweet only; omit for savory) preparation make dough. in a food processor, pulse flour + sugar (if using) + salt. add butter; pulse 8–10 times to coarse crumbs. add water. run processor and add ice water 1 tbsp at a time until dough comes together. chill. form into a 4-inch disk, wrap tightly, and chill at least 30 minutes (or overnight). preheat. heat oven to 375°f. line a sheet pan with parchment. roll + fill. roll dough into a ~14-inch round. add filling, leaving a 1–2 inch border. fold + finish. fold edges up, pleating as you go. brush edges with melted butter; sprinkle sugar for sweet galettes. bake. bake 35–45 minutes until golden. cool ~15 minutes. filling ideas savory roasted red onion rosemary chorizo balsamic reduction sweet apple clementine zest cardamom cinnamon ginger lemon juice cocktail (ideas) gin (small amount) rosemary simple syrup lemons seltzer

title: Gazpacho Toledano
text: all recipes / soup gazpacho toledano tags: vegetarian, nut-free, soy-free gazpacho toledano x8 (this had ~7qts left with a group of ~39) 56 7-8 medium-sized ripe tomatoes 16 2 medium-sized cucumbers 8 1 green pepper 8 1 small onion 20 2-3 cloves garlic omit or gf 1 ½ slices french bread 12 1 ½ cups cold water 3c 6 tbs. olive oil 32? 4-5 tbs. wine vinegar, or to taste get 24 3 tsp. salt, or to taste 16? 2 tsp. paprika 8p pinch ground cumin fresh ground pepper to taste garnish: hmm…..big bowl of mixed extras? @1/4 c each = 10-12 cups croutons //we have bread for side chopped onions chopped red and green bell peppers chopped cucumber we just did these 3 (cucumber & tomato & parmesan) chopped tomatoes maybe parmesan? cut the tomatoes into quarters. peel and seed cucumbers and cut into approximately 1-inch pieces. seed bell pepper and cut into approximately 1-inch pieces. peel and coarsely chop onion. put garlic through a press. cube bread now put the prepared ingredients, 2 to 3 cups at a time, into a blender, adding a little of the water each time. blend at medium or high speed until the vegetables and bread are pureed. pour the puree into a large bowl. add the oil and vinegar, the remaining water, and the seasonings and whisk vigorously until all is blended. if the soup is too thick, it may be thinned with a little more cold water. chill the soup in the refrigerator for several hours before serving. arrange the garnishes attractively on a large platter and pass them around the table as you serve the soup. serves 6 to 8. maybe put some canned white beans & walnuts out for salad topping for protein?

title: Ginger Miso Salad Dressing
text: all recipes / salad ginger miso salad dressing tags: vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free, nut-free recipe: ginger miso salad dressing equipment vitamix, 2 pitchers ingredients for 1 batch (~48 servs) ½ cup apple cider vinegar ½ cup tamari ½ cup agave ¾ cup yellow miso (or any kind will do) ¼ cup chopped ginger (rough chop, let vitamix take it from there) ½ cup water 1 tsp toasted sesame oil 4 cups light olive oil instructions rough chop the ginger. add all except oil in vitamix container and mix on low. drizzle oil into vitamix mixing while you do. gradually increase speed until all emulsified. taste & adjust seasoning if needed. divide between 2 small pitchers. cover & store in fridge (if not for today, label and date also).

title: Glazed Tempeh
text: all recipes / entree glazed tempeh tags: vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free, nut-free glazed maple-mustard tempeh strips with collards – page 1 of 2 sweet and sticky with just a little kick, these sliced tempeh strips are briefly marinated, baked, then re-glazed to trap in maximum flavor and tender texture. ingredients: serves 6 (serving 6 x 6, make twice the amount of sauce) 2 8-oz. pkg. (x6 12 8-oz.pkg.) tempeh, sliced into ½-inch strips ⅓ cup (x12 4 cup) maple syrup ¼ cup (x12 3 cup) orange juice ¼ cup (x12/6 1 ½ & ¾ cup) safflower oil, divided 2 tbs. (x12 1 1/2 cup)ketchup 2 tbs. (x12 1 1/2 cup) dijon mustard 1 tbs. (x12 ¾ cup) sriracha sauce 1 tbs. (x12 ¾ cup) low-sodium tamari 1 tsp. (x12 ¼ cup) freshly ground black pepper ¼ tsp. (x12 1 tbl.) ground cinnamon 2 cloves (x12 12 cloves) garlic, minced (2 tsp. (x12 1/2 cup)) 2 12-oz. (x6 12 12-oz.) bunches collard greens, stems and ribs removed, leaves thinly sliced 2 cups (x6 12 cups) frozen fire roasted corn, thawed glazed maple-mustard tempeh strips with collards – page 2 of 2 instructions: 1 | place tempeh strips in medium heat-proof bowl. set aside. 2 | whisk together maple syrup, orange juice, 2 tbs.(x12 1 ½ cup) oil, ketchup, mustard, sriracha, tamari, pepper, and cinnamon in medium saucepan. bring to a simmer over medium heat, and cook 5 to 7 minutes, or until slightly thickened. pour hot mixture over tempeh strips, cover, and let marinate 30 minutes, or overnight. 3 | preheat oven to 350°f. line baking sheet with foil, and coat with cooking spray. arrange marinated tempeh strips on prepared baking sheet; reserve marinade. cover baking sheet tightly with foil, and bake 15 minutes. remove foil, and flip tempeh pieces. bake, uncovered, 5 minutes more, or until tempeh is slightly browned. remove from oven, and brush tempeh with remaining glaze. 4 | meanwhile, heat remaining 2 tbs.(x6 ¾ cup) oil in large saucepan over medium-high heat. add garlic, and cook 30 seconds. add collard greens in two batches, wilting first batch before adding second. stir in corn, and season with salt and pepper, if desired. cook 5 to 7 minutes or until greens are tender, stirring occasionally. serve topped with tempeh slices. serves 6 or 36 0

title: Golden Beet Borscht
text: all recipes / soup golden beet borscht tags: vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free, nut-free golden beet borscht from spirit rock we were blown away the first time we made this soup – it is delicate but full of flavor, satisfying and savory but full of the sweetness of perfectly cooked vegetables, and wonderfully adaptable for colder or warmer seasons. it quickly became one of our year-round go-to dishes for retreat suppers! traditionalists can serve the soup with a dollop of herbed sour cream, but the original recipe from the world-famous bay area vegan restaurant millennium offers a delicious non-dairy alternative. makes 8 servings adapted from a recipe by eric tucker & john westerdahl, from “the millennium cookbook” ingredients: soup 2 quart vegetable stock 2 large yellow onions, thinly sliced 6 medium carrots, thinly sliced ¾ cup dry sherry, white wine, or nonalcoholic wine 4 medium yellow beets, peeled and thinly sliced 1 bay leaf 1/2 tsp toasted and ground caraway seeds 2 tsp fresh thyme, minced 3 1/2 tbs white miso, or more to taste 1 tbs sherry vinegar (opt) ¼ cup minced fresh dill salt and freshly ground pepper, to taste tofu dill sour cream 3 1/4 oz silken tofu 1 tbs white miso, to taste (optional) ¾ cup fresh lemon juice 4 tbs minced fresh dill 1/2 tsp ground nutmeg, to taste ¾ cup water, plus more as needed directions: if you are making your own stock from scratch, begin by making your stock. a light, soft broth is nice in the summer, whereas a hearty, dark roasted broth can be nice in the winter. if you have a nice pre-made stock that you enjoy, feel free to use it as a short cut! coat the bottom of a large soup pot with a thin layer of sunflower oil. place over a medium heat. when the oil is hot add the onions, carrots, and sherry, and cook until the onions are soft, about 15 minutes (we’re keeping the vegetables nice and light, so no need to do any heavy browning on the vegetables before adding the cooking liquid). add the beets, bay, caraway, thyme and vegetable stock. cover and reduce heat to medium-low, and simmer for 40 minutes or until the beets are very tender. meanwhile, make the tofu topping. in a blender or food processor, blend all ingredients until smooth. thin out with as much of the water as needed. set the topping aside in a bowl, and garnish with dill or other herbs immediately prior to service. to finish the soup, pull one cup of broth into a small prep bowl, and whisk in the miso paste to make a slurry. pour the miso broth into the soup and stir to combine. add vinegar and the fresh dill. season with salt and pepper and serve hot. alternately, if you would like a blended soup rather than a brothy soup, blend prior to adding the dill.

title: Greek Lemon Salad Dressing
text: all recipes / salad greek lemon salad dressing tags: vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free, nut-free, soy-free recipe: greek lemon salad dressing equipment vitamix, microplane zester (or box grater), electric juicer, 2 pitchers ingredients for 1 batch (~48 servs) ~½ tbsp zest of 1 lemon //zest is just the outermost colored layer of the peel ½ cup lemon juice (about 6 lemons) 2 limes juice of two limes (optional if no limes..) 1 cups rice vinegar ⅓ cup agave 2 tbls dijon mustard 6 cloves (or 1 ½ tsp) garlic cloves (or powder) 1t oregano 2 cups olive oil 2 cups light olive oil ¾ cup water ½ tsp salt instructions zest lemons with zester. be careful! very sharp! juice lemons with press juicer. add all except oil in vitamix container and mix on low. drizzle oil into vitamix mixing while you do. gradually increase speed until all emulsified. taste & adjust seasoning if needed. divide between 2 small pitchers. cover & store in fridge (if not for today, label and date also).

title: Herb Vinaigrette--update
text: all recipes / salad herb vinaigrette--update tags: vegetarian, gluten-free, dairy-free, nut-free, soy-free herb vinaigrette (also used for “tarragon” in menus) ~1 ½ qts ~3qts (for 2 meals) 1 ½ c 3c rice vinegar ¼ c ½ cup honey ¼ c ½ cup dijon mustard 6 cl 12 cloves garlic ~¾ c ~1 ½ cups fresh herbs note: for our “herbal” use 1 bunch basil, ½ bunch parsley for our “tarragon” use 1 clamshell of tarragon 4 c 8 c canola oil ½ c 1 c water salt to taste rinse the herbs & pick the leaves off the stems. poach the whole peeled garlic cloves in one cup of the oil (one cup out of the amt. called for) in the small saucepan or skillet on medium heat for ~5 minutes to make them more mild. add all except the rest of the oil to the blender (poached garlic cloves and their oil can be added unchopped). blend. if room in the vitamix, drizzle in the oil as you keep blending. if no room, transfer to a larger container and whisk in the oil or use the emersion blender. taste (drizzle a little into a separate spoon) and adjust salt, pepper or other seasonings. for one meal: fill 2 small pitchers. serve with smallest ladles.

title: Herbal Dressing
text: all recipes / salad herbal dressing tags: vegetarian, gluten-free, dairy-free, nut-free, soy-free herbal vinaigrette (instructions for double recipe) gather all ingredients below, the vitamix container and a second 2 or 4 quart container with lid. you will double this recipe by putting a set of the below ingredients in each container. it’s easiest to add each ingredient to both containers, then go to the next ingredient. ingredients for one container (you will put this much in each one) 1 cup water ¾ tsp garlic powder (on spice shelf far left) or if time: poach in oil or boil in water 6 cloves of garlic (don’t use just raw garlic…too strong) 3 ¾ cup canola oil 2 cup rice vinegar ¼ cup honey ¼ cup dijon mustard ½ cup fresh basil ½ cup fresh parsley pick fresh basil leaves until you have a loosely packed cup. pick fresh parsley leaves until you have a loosely packed cup. rinse both herbs and divide each in half. add the above ingredients list to each container. blend the contents of the vitamix container using the vitamix. fill 2 small pitchers with it. pour second set of ingredients into the vitamix container and mix it. pour the mixed dressing back in the mixing container, cover, label and put in the fridge.

title: Herbal Salad Dressing
text: all recipes / salad herbal salad dressing tags: vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free, nut-free, soy-free recipe: herbal salad dressing equipment vitamix, 2 pitchers, (extra 2qt square container with green lid for second batch) ingredients for 1 batch (~48 servs) note: you may be asked to make 2 batches, first read instructions below for how to do that...these are the quantities for one batch 1 ¾ cup rice vinegar 1 ½ cup water 1 tsp garlic powder ¼ cup + 2 tbsp dijon mustard ⅓ cup agave ½ tsp salt 1 tsp pepper ½ bunch fresh basil leaves (pick off from stems) (= ~½ cup packed down) ½ bunch fresh parsley (cut off main trunk of stems, ok to use rest) (=~½ cup packed down) 3 ½ cups light olive oil instructions rinse herbs, no need to chop, vitamix will do it. if making 2 batches, measure a second batch except oils into square container. add all except oils in vitamix container and mix on low increasing to high. drizzle oils into vitamix mixing while you do. gradually increase speed until all emulsified. divide between 2 small pitchers. for second batch: pour measured container ingredients into vitamix and blend. add second batch of oils as above. pour back into container, label, date and store in fridge for later.

title: Hollyhock Salad Dressing
text: all recipes / salad hollyhock salad dressing tags: vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free, nut-free recipe: hollyhock salad dressing equipment vitamix, 2 pitchers ingredients for 1 batch (~48 servs) ¾ cup apple cider vinegar ¾ cup water ¾ cup tamari 9 cloves (or 2 tsp) garlic cloves (or powder) 1 cup nutritional yeast (yellow stuff in pantry near oatmeal) 3 cups + 3 ½ cups light olive oil (added in 2 batches) instructions add all vinegar, water, tamari, garlic and first 3 cups of canola oil to vitamix container and mix on low. add nutritional yeast and blend in thoroughly. drizzle remaining oil into vitamix mixing while you do. gradually increase speed until all emulsified. divide between 2 small pitchers. cover & store in fridge (if not for today, label and date also).

title: Hollyhock
text: all recipes / salad hollyhock tags: vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free, nut-free hollyhock dressing updated by chris 7/30/2015 from notes by michelle makes 1.5qts blend the below well in the vitamix: ¾ cup water ¾ cup tamari ¾ cup apple cider vinegar 9 cloves garlic 3 c canola or other non-olive oil add & blend well again: 1 cup nutritional yeast add and blend well again: 3.5-4 cups canola oil fill 2 small pitchers if for today, or else store in 2quart (smallest square) container with label & date.

title: Honey Mustard
text: all recipes / salad honey mustard tags: vegetarian, gluten-free, dairy-free, nut-free, soy-free honey mustard 1 ½ qts 3qts (2 meals) 1 ¼ c 2 ½ cups apple cider vinegar ½ c +2 t 1 ¼ cups dijon mustard ½ c + 2t 1 ¼ cups honey (hint: coat cup with oil, honey slides right out..) 3 ½ c 7 cups canola oil add all except oil to the blender. blend. if room in the vitamix, drizzle in the oil as you keep blending. if no room, transfer to a larger container and whisk in the oil. taste (drizzle a little into a separate spoon) and adjust salt, pepper or other seasonings. for one meal: fill 2 small pitchers. serve with smallest ladles.

title: Kale Salad from Carol Collins
text: all recipes / salad kale salad from carol collins tags: vegetarian, gluten-free, soy-free kale salad from carol collins ½ cup lightly roasted walnuts 8 oz. kale (i prefer the smooth lacinato) 1 cup red cabbage ½ cup dried cranberries 1 medium granny smith apple 2 oz. soft goat cheese, chilled dressing: 3 t olive or canola oil 1½ t apple cider vinegar 2 teas rice vinegar 1 t smooth dijon mustard 1½ teas honey pull kale leaves off from the tough stems and discard stems. chop the kale and the cabbage into small, bite-sized pieces chop the apple into small, bite-sized pieces and add to small bowl of cold water with about 1 t of lemon juice. transfer to a large bowl. sprinkle small amount of sea salt or kosher salt and massage the leaves with your hands by lightly scrunching big handfuls at a time, until the leaves are darker in color and fragrant. add the cranberries and walnuts. drain the apple and add to mix. crumble the goat cheese over the top. in a small bowl, whisk the dressing ingredients together vigorously and pour over the salad. toss until the salad is evenly coated with dressing. allow the salad to marinate for an hour or so before serving. ` serves 4 as main dish

title: Lael Simple Dal
text: all recipes / entree lael simple dal tags: vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free, nut-free, soy-free lael’s simple dal (if we’re tired of onion & tomato) 6 qt red lentils 12 qt water ¼ c + 2t turmeric ¼ c salt 4oz chopped ginger + 4 oz pureed ginger (added later) 1/2c cumin seeds 1/3 cup ground coriander ¼ cup garam masala ¾ tsp cayenne ~¼ cup oil ½-1 c. lemon juice optional: spinach or other greens bring lentils, water, turmeric, chopped ginger and salt to a boil and then simmer until done. when nearly done: fry cumin seeds in oil for 1 min, add coriander, garam masala & cayenne. add fried spices to dal. add greens to dal if using. just before serving stir in 4 oz pureed ginger and the lemon juice to taste. taste for salt, lemon.

title: Lasagna notes
text: all recipes / entree lasagna notes tags: vegetarian, nut-free, soy-free layers for 1 hotel pan 2c sauce 7 ½ sheets tjs lasagna noodles 6c cheese/spin mix 3 c sauce 3c moz 7 ½ sheets tjs lasagna noodles 6c cheese/spin mix layer of julienned basil? 3c sauce 7 ½ sheets tjs lasagna noodles 3 c sauce 2c parm + 1 c. bread crumbs + 1c. moz totals: 12 c cheese/spin (see below) = 24cup = 8qts 11 c sauce x2.5 = 28 23 sheets tjs (about 21 per box) so x2 = 3boxes 4c moz = 8c 2c parm =4c 2c bread crumbs x2 = 4 cheese mix: (need 12cups) 1c ric: .5c spin 4c prepd 1cup cooked = 1lb raw or 10oz froz, so x2.25 = 9lbs raw or 9 10oz froz 7c=4lb ricotta for 2 = 8lbs ,7.5= ~5x32oz enough o r 8 15ozers 1c goat 2tj tub of goat or sm. log = ~1c x2 = 4 4 eggs = ~1c //x2 =8 1 c bread crumbs // buy 1t nutmeg salt & pepper total ingredients for 2 reg, ¼ sn 3 boxes noodles 1 box gf noodles 8 10oz frozen spin bags 5x32oz ricotta 4 tubs tj goat = 2cups 8 eggs 4 cups bread crumbs 2lbs tofu 28c or 8.5qts sauce with mushrooms & onions, so less… 8c moz 1 no-dairy cheese? 2 lemons half case mushrooms 4lbs onions basil dry basil? nutmeg sauce for this: bottled + sautéed 4lb mushroom & 4lb onion alt: ¼ pan for 6 //sauce & cheese mix for quilley (no gluten, no tofu)? 1lb adult spin rice lasagna? 1lb tofu tofu, lemon juice, 2 garlic, ¼ c. non-dairy milk,2t fresh basil…vitamix 4c sauce alt cheese for top? saute mushrooms & onion maybe w/some extra dry basil & oreg mix in sauce steam spin & press dry //set aside some spinach for special needs version(s) beat eggs, mix cheeses w/ spin & nutmeg, //km: make tofu ricotta, add spin.. layer 11:00 bake 1 hr, sit 15

title: Lemon Tahini Dressing-IF
text: all recipes / salad lemon tahini dressing-if tags: vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free, nut-free lemon tahini dressing gather all ingredients below and one vitamix container. if needed, double the recipe using two vitamix containers. ingredients for one vitamix container (do this twice if making extra) 1 cup lemon juice (juice from about 4 fresh lemons) ¾ cup parsley 5 cloves garlic 2 ½ cups water 1 ½ tablespoon tamari (if no soy yogis use salt instead) 2 teaspoons ground cumin ½ teaspoon white pepper 2 ½ cup tahini using electric juicer, juice the lemons. wash parsley and cut off stems (some of the upper stems are ok). add all ingredients in order above to vitamix container. repeat if making two batches in second vitamix container. fill two small pitchers with each vitamix container of salad dressing made.

title: Lemon Tahini Salad Dressing
text: all recipes / salad lemon tahini salad dressing tags: vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free, nut-free recipe: lemon tahini salad dressing equipment vitamix, electric juicer, mixing bowl, whisk, 2 small pitchers ingredients note: this needs reworking, we currently prefer the orange tahini for 1 batch (~48 servs) 2 ½ cups water 1 cup lemon juice (4-6 lemons) ¾ cup parsley 5 cloves or 1 ¼ tsp fresh garlic or powder 1 ½ tblsp tamari 2 tsp cumin ½ tsp white pepper 2 cups tahini (=1 whole tin of joyva, or measure out bulk ½ cup light olive oil instructions using juicer, juice the lemons. wash parsley and cut off stems (some of the upper stems are ok). in a medium sized bowl, use a hand whisk to mix lemon juice, tahini and 1 cup of the water so that tahini is not too clumpy (or else it will stall the vitamix) then blend in the vitamix with rest of ingredients. divide between two small pitchers. cover & store in fridge (if not for today, label and date also).

title: Lemon Cookies (2)
text: all recipes / dessert lemon cookies (2) tags: vegan, dairy-free lemon cookies (makes 18 cookies) cookies ● ½ c refined coconut oil melted ● ¾ c sugar ● 3 t mylk ● 2 t lemon zest (about 2 lemons) ● 1 tsp vanilla ● 1.5 c flour ● 1 tsp cornsarch ● ½ tsp baking powder ● ½ tsp salt 1.oven to 350 2.using fork or electric mixer beat sugar and oil together 3.add mylk, zest and vanilla beat till it resembles applesauce 4.add ½ the flour and remaining cornstarch, baking powder and salt 5.add remaining flour 6.spoon about 2t per cookie, flatten with hands 7.bake 10­12 min until bottoms are golden brown lemon glaze ● 2 c powdered sugar ● 3t lemon juice ● ½ tsp vanilla ● 1t refined coconut oil sift powdered sugar and add remaining ingredients, whisk well then drizzle on completely cooled cookies and place in fridge to harden the glaze.

title: Malaysian Tofu
text: all recipes / entree malaysian tofu tags: vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free recipe: malaysian influenced tofu (from deborah madison) pg 1 of 2 equipment 2 lg baking sheets, rondo (or lg stock pot) ingredients 48 servings (maybe some lo) 48 servings no supper leftovers 15lbs 12lbs tofu, cubed 3/4” cubes as needed as needed spray oil 1 #10 can+1small can 1#10 can coconut milk (whole, not lite, add water as needed).. tbd est water amt. ½ cup + 2t ½ cup brown sugar ¾ cup ⅔ cup coriander seeds, lightly toasted & ground 10t 8t curry powder 2 ½ t 2t tumeric ½ tsp + pinch ½ tsp cayenne pepper (start with this, check for not too hot..) ¼ c + 1t ¼ cup tamarind paste 1 16 oz jar 1 16oz jar cashew butter [* bought, or see recipe below] or: 4 cups cashews + 2 tsp coconut oil 17 cloves 14 cloves garlic, chopped in mini-cuis ¾ cup ⅔ cup ginger, chopped in mini-cuis 6lbs 5lbs mushrooms, cut chunky (~ in fourths) 1 lg can +1med can 1 lg can diced tomatoes 4 bu 3 bu scallions, sliced thin including greens (for garnish) recipe: malaysian tofu pg 2 of 2 instructions bake tofu preheat oven to 350. cube tofu into ¾” cubes, layout on baking sheets on parchment and spray with oil. (this may not be cubed until ~10:15) bake for ~30-40 minutes, stirring occasionally until lightly browned. while they cook, proceed with next steps. if needed make cashew butter if not using bought: 4 cups cashews, roast lightly (@350 for ~10 mins, watching carefully!), puree until very fine, in robo-coupe, add ~2tsp oil & puree more until no longer grainy, almost dough or butter like (doesn’t have to be really all the way to commercial butter). start sauce by ~10:30 //check allergies…maybe make a no_cashew side version?? could try with some tahini?? mix all sauce ingredients except for mushrooms, tomatoes and scallions in the rondo (or lg stock pot if no rondo) on a flame disperser. heat on the stove, whisking to blend. reduce to simmer for 10 minutes. once the sauce is smooth and heated, add the mushrooms. add tofu and garnish about 11:00, add the tofu and tomatoes to the sauce and stir. watch for low simmer and non-sticking. garnish with chopped scallions just before serving.

title: Rice Pilaf
text: all recipes / side rice pilaf tags: vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free, soy-free week 2 day 6 recipe: rice pilaf page 1 of 2 equipment large strainer, largest skillet or rondo, rice cooker, maybe large bowl to mix & serve ingredients #48 w/ no supper #36 note: no supper because we make soup of the lo tagine 14 cups 10 cups short grain brown rice (ideally, could use basmati if all we have) 17 ½ cups 12 ½ cups water (ratio of r:w we use here is 1:1 ¼ ) (make some into bouillon using better than bouillon see instructions). 2 cups 1 ½ cups raisins 2 cups 1 ½ cups chopped dried apricots 2 cups 1 ½ cups coarsely chopped almonds (or mix of almonds & pistachios) 4 each 3 ea chopped onions 2 oranges 1 ½ zested week 2 day 6 recipe: rice pilaf pg 2 of 2 instructions prep: chop apricots and almonds and/or pistachios, measure out raisins. chop onions. zest oranges. rinse the rice using the large double-mesh strainer . make bouillon with ~2 qts hot tea water water and ~⅓ cup better than bouillon. add rest of water cold. make rice using bouillon & rest of water, make rice in the rice cooker. saute while the rice is cooking, saute the onions, when translucent, add the fruit and saute a bit. finish when rice is done, stir in the sauted onions, apricots and raisins. let it sit for ~10 mins covered. stir in the orange zest. maybe set aside a no-nuts portion. stir in the nuts just before serving.

title: Two Quantities Baked Potato Bar
text: all recipes / side two quantities baked potato bar tags: vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free, nut-free, soy-free recipe: baked potato bar equipment 2-3 large baking sheets ingredients #servings with supper leftovers #servings no supper leftovers 25 lbs [qty] white potatoes 15 lbs sweet potatoes olive oil instructions prep potatoes preheat ovens to 400 degrees. rub potatoes with olive oil and sprinkle with salt and pepper and place on baking sheets bake bake 1-2 hrs?, if still need more time turn and continue baking

title: Mexican Hot Chocolate Snickerdoodles
text: all recipes / dessert mexican hot chocolate snickerdoodles tags: vegan, dairy-free, soy-free mexican hot chocolate snickerdoodles makes 2 dozen cookies a beautiful crackle topped chocolate cookie with a spicy cayenne kick and a sugary cinnamon coating. sold? for the topping: 1/3 cup sugar 1 teaspoon ground cinnamon for the cookies: 1/2 cup canola oil 1 cup sugar 1/4 cup pure maple syrup 3 tablespoons almond milk (or your preferred non-dairy milk) 1 teaspoon vanilla extract 1 teaspoon chocolate extract (or more vanilla extract if you have no chocolate) 1 2/3 cups flour 1/2 cup unsweetened cocoa powder 1 teaspoon baking soda 1/4 teaspoon salt 1/2 teaspoon cinnamon 1/2 teaspoon cayenne preheat oven to 350 f. line 2 large baking sheets with parchment paper. mix the topping ingredients together on a flat plate. set aside. in a medium mixing bowl, use a fork to vigorously mix together oil, sugar, syrup, and milk. mix in extracts. sift in remaining ingredients, stirring as you add them. once all ingredients are added mix until you’ve got a pliable dough. roll dough into walnut sized balls. pat into the sugar topping to flatten into roughly 2 inch discs. transfer to baking sheet, sugar side up, at least 2 inches apart (they do spread). this should be easy as the the bottom of the cookies should just stick to your fingers so you can just flip them over onto the baking sheet. bake for 10 to 12 minutes, they should be a bit spread and crackly on top. remove from oven and let cool for 5 minutes, then transfer to a cooling rack to cool completely.

title: Minty Pea Dip (2)
text: all recipes / side minty pea dip (2) tags: vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free, nut-free, soy-free minty pea dip/spread from martha stewart website via lael vegan, nut free for full for ~36 orig 12 9 3 cups frozen peas 1 ¾ ¼ cup mint leaves 4 3 1 lemon, zest and juice of 4 3 1 clove garlic 8 6 2 tbls olive oil 4 3 1 tbls tahini to taste salt & pepper blanch peas in salted boiling water <~1 minute, cool & drain. pulse peas in robo coupe with all other ingredients. season to taste with salt & pepper. serve, maybe garnish with drizzle of olive oil, mint sprig.

title: Moroccan Lentil Soup
text: all recipes / soup moroccan lentil soup tags: vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free, nut-free, soy-free moroccan red lentil soup ingredients for 12 qts 6 tbsp. extra virgin olive oil 5 large onion, chopped 6 celery stalk, chopped 6 carrot, chopped 16 garlic cloves, chopped 8 tsp. ground coriander 4 tsp. ground cumin 4 tsp. ground turmeric 2 tsp. sweet paprika 1 tsp. ground cinnamon 2 tsp. sea salt 1 tsp pepper 8 qts vegetable broth, (i used 1 jar of betterthanbouillon dissolved in 1qt tea water+ 7qts water) 1 lg can crushed tomatoes (or diced tomatoes) 8 cups red lentils, picked over, washed and rinsed until water runs clean ½ c. ~6 lemons, juiced ~ ¼ tsp cayenne 1cup fresh flat-leaf parsley, chopped (on the side) fresh cilantro, chopped instructions heat olive oil in large pot over medium-high heat. add the onions, carrots and celery and sauté until tender (about 15 minutes). add the garlic, coriander, cumin, turmeric, paprika, cinnamon, salt and pepper and continue cooking for another 2-3 minutes stirring the whole time. add the broth, tomatoes, and lentils stir well and heat to a boil. simmer uncovered on low heat for about 45 minutes to 1 hour, stirring occasionally. blend with immersion blender (don’t have to blend all the way, more than half maybe). stir in the lemon juice, red pepper flakes, parsley and cilantro, cover and cook for 10 minutes. garnish with cilantro if you desire.

title: Mu Shu Wraps
text: all recipes / entree mu shu wraps tags: vegetarian, dairy-free mu shu wraps @ 1 ½ per person 2 people 14 people 21 p 30 p 3 wraps 21 wraps 30 w 45 wraps lg onion slivered 1/5 1 1 ½ 3 garlic minced 1 lg 4 6 9 ginger minced 1tsp 2t1t 3t 4 ½ t ginger slivered 1 t ½ c ?? 3/4c 1 ¼ c carrots julienned ¼ large 2 3 5 or robo-shredded 5-spice tofu julienned 1/8 14oz box 1 ½ box 2 boxes 3lbs recipe below tree ear mushrooms a few 1 oz 1.5 oz 2.25oz dried pre-shredded shitake mushrooms 2 14 21 ~30 lily buds, dried ~10 70 100=2-3oz 150 cabbage 1/5 1lb 1 ½ lb 2lb 3lbs sauce: tamari 1t 7 10t 1 cup rice vinegar 1t 7 10t 1 cup brown sugar 1t 7 10t 1 cup hoisin 1t 7 10t 1 cup fixins: hoisin sauce 3t 1 ¾ cup 2 ¼ c 3 ½ c reserved shitake juice 3t 1 ¾ cup 2 ¼ c 3 ⅓ c scallions slivered 2 14 21 30 fajita type wheat tortillas 3 21 30 45? (rice for gluten free) night before: marinate tofu (see below) first thing: bake marinated tofu slices at 350 until dry & firm looking (keep an eye, turn over half way..) figure out strategy for special needs (like no-tofu = some with scrambled eggs, alt sauces etc.) soak all dried stuff in boiling water about 30 mins cut lily buds in half after soaking stir-fry onion, minced ginger, garlic add tree ears, shitakes, lily buds (set off fire until steamed parts are nearly ready) add sauce to stir-fry steam in steam tray (allow 30 min): cabbage, ginger slivers, carrots mix together the steamed stuff, stir-fry and tofy. maybe heat tortillas (the thin ones don’t need it) serve with sliced scallions, ½ hoisin/ ½ mush lqd mix, tortillas & instructions to spread some hoisin and scallions on tortilla and then add some mushu, then wrap. good served with butternut squash or yams, kale salad with orange and roasted cashews with miso dressing for example. *5-spice tofu: try to make day before: press tofu cut loaf into thin-ish slices horizontally marinate in 1 t soy, 1 1 t water, ¼ t 5-spice powder, 2 drops sesame oil (i like to use large baggies to marinate it) refridgerate over night next day: bake on baking sheet at 350 for an hour or so, turn halfway, check often for burning and add a little water. you want it to dry out and get more firm. cut slices into matchsticks for the mushu. homemade hoisin sauce (adjustable for various special needs): makes about a cup 4 tablespoons dark brown sugar 4 tablespoon chinese black bean and garlic paste ///or i have used 2/3 can of blackbeans drained, plus 1 tsp chopped garlic 2 tablespoons tamari 1 tablespoon honey 4 teaspoons rice vinegar //or lemon if avioiding vinegar 1/2 teaspoon chinese five-spice powder 2 tablespoon peanut butter ¼ tsp sale you could cook this a little on the stove or not, its ok just blended.

title: Mushroom gravy
text: all recipes / side mushroom gravy tags: vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free, nut-free, soy-free recipe: mushroom gravy equipment : rondo ingredients #leftover amount ½ cup earth balance vegan butter 3 lbs onions 5 lbs mushrooms 3 qts water 1 cup cornstarch ½ jar veggie stock 2 t rosemary from garden 2 t sage from garden ¾ cup nutritional yeast salt and pepper instructions saute melt butter on medium heat in rondo and add onions. saute for 5-10 minutes until they begin to soften. add mushrooms and saute until liquid begins to release. mixing mix water, veggie stock and cornstarch and add to mushroom and onion mixture. add ingredients and finish add remaining ingredients, rosemary, sage, nutritional yeast and bring to boil and reduce to simmer until thick and delicious. add salt and pepper to taste

title: north african stew
text: all recipes / entree north african stew tags: vegetarian, nut-free, soy-free north african bean stew with barley and winter squash melissa clark time1 hour 45 minutes yield 8 to 10 servings this warming, highly spiced stew is rich in beans, grains and chunks of sweet winter squash. feel free to substitute other grains for the barley. farro works particularly well. if you’d prefer something soupier, thin it with a little broth or water before serving. featured in: cooking beans at home, leaving the can behind . ingredients ⅓ cup extra-virgin olive oil, more for serving 2 leeks, white and green parts, diced 1 bunch cilantro, leaves and stems separated 1 cup finely diced fennel, fronds reserved (1/2 large fennel bulb) 3 garlic cloves, finely chopped 2 ½ tablespoons baharat recipe for a batch of it: 2 tablespoons sweet paprika, 1 tablespoon ground coriander, 1 tablespoon ground cumin, 1 tablespoon ground turmeric, 2 teaspoons black pepper, 1 teaspoon grated nutmeg, 1 teaspoon ground cardamom 1 teaspoon allspice. ½ cinnamon stick 2 tablespoons tomato paste 2 quarts chicken or vegetable broth ½ cup pearled barley 2 ½ teaspoons kosher salt, more as needed large pinch saffron, crumbled (optional) 4 cups cooked beans or chickpeas 2 cups peeled and diced butternut squash (1 small squash) ¾ cup peeled and diced turnip (1 medium) ½ cup red lentils plain yogurt, for serving aleppo pepper or hot paprika, for serving preparation in a large pot over medium heat, heat oil and cook leeks until they begin to brown, 10 to 12 minutes. finely chop cilantro stems. stir into pot, along with diced fennel and garlic. cook for 2 minutes. stir in baharat, cinnamon and tomato paste, and cook until paste begins to caramelize, about 2 minutes. stir in broth, 3 cups water, the barley and the salt. bring to a gentle boil, stir in saffron, if using, and reduce heat to medium. simmer uncovered for 40 minutes. stir in beans, squash, turnip and lentils; cook until barley is tender, about another 20 to 30 minutes. taste and adjust seasonings, if desired. remove cinnamon stick. ladle stew into bowls. spoon a dollop of yogurt on top and drizzle with olive oil. garnish with cilantro leaves, fennel fronds and aleppo pepper or paprika.

title: Cheese Polenta
text: all recipes / side cheese polenta tags: vegetarian, gluten-free, nut-free, soy-free cheesy (and not) oven polenta: ingredients & setup equip: two 4” full-sized hotel pans, one half-sized 4” hotel pan (they won’t be full, but easier if they don’t slosh, so use 4”). preheat the oven to 425. turn down if needed after 30-40 minutes. in each of the two large pans, mix: 5 cups polenta (coarse corn meal) 20 cups water 1 t salt in the half pan, mix: 2 ½ cups polenta 10 cups water ½ t salt mix together in a bowl and set aside for adding (at the end) to the 2 large pans: 1.5 lb shredded swiss/gruyere mix, (or other “italian mix” or jack..ask km). 2 tubs of crumbled blue or gorgonzola cheese 2 t dried basil 1 ½ t black pepper set aside for the tops of the large pans (at the end): 3 cups shredded parmesan cheese (1 ½ cups each) for the smaller no-cheese pan, mix and set aside: 1 t olive oil 1 t dried basil 2 tsp black pepper cheesy (and not) oven polenta: baking instructions oven bake the polenta: put lids on the pans and put them in the oven about 10:15. set a timer for an hour. mix the cheeses & spices as described above. about 11:15, carefully with hot pad gloves (and maybe with help) stir the pans. don’t worry if not thick yet. set the timer for another 15-20 mins. if not thick yet. when the polenta has become thick (after ~60-80 mins) , add the cheese to the cheese-y versions: again carefully with gloves and help: stir half the jack/blue/basil/pepper mix into each of the two full-sized pans. sprinkle half the parmesan cheese over each of the two large pans. don’t stir in cheese in the half-pan! stir in the olive oil, basil, pepper mix. return all pans to the oven uncovered for about half an hour (or ok to leave for longer). if the cheese is getting too brown on top, put the lids back on, if it is not getting brown, turn the heat up to 500 for a few minutes.

title: Artichoke Salad Dressing
text: all recipes / salad artichoke salad dressing tags: vegetarian, gluten-free, dairy-free, nut-free artichoke salad dressing 1.5qts 33oz marinated artichoke hearts add all including oil) 1t tamari (omit if no-soy people on the retreat, probably need more salt at the end..) 1t dijon mustard ½ t honey ½ t white pepper (or more to taste..) ½ c water ½ c white wine vinegar (or rice vinegar) 1 c canola oil salt to taste add all except oil to the blender. blend. if room in the vitamix, drizzle in the oil as you keep blending. if no room, transfer to a larger container and whisk in the oil taste (drizzle a little into a separate spoon) and adjust salt, pepper or other seasonings for one meal: fill 2 small pitchers. serve with smallest ladles.

title: Herbal Dressing
text: all recipes / salad herbal dressing tags: vegetarian, gluten-free, dairy-free, nut-free, soy-free herbal vinaigrette (instructions for double recipe) updated by chris 7/30/2015 for a bit milder & less gather all ingredients below, the vitamix container and a second 2 quart (smallest square) container with lid. you will double this recipe by putting a set of the below ingredients in each container. it’s easiest to add each ingredient to both containers, then go to the next ingredient. ingredients for one container (you will put this much in each of the vitamix and the side container) 1 ½ cups rice vinegar 1 ½ cups water 1 tsp garlic powder (on spice shelf far left) ¼ cup honey (tip: coat cup with oil, honey slides right out) ¼ cup dijon mustard ½ tsp salt ½ bunch fresh basil leaves (pick off from stems) (~½ cup packed down) ½ bunch fresh parsley (cut off main trunk of stems, ok to use rest) ( ~ ½ cup packed down) 3 ½ cups canola oil rinse the herbs (no need to chop, vitamix will do it) . add the above ingredients list to each container. blend the contents of the vitamix container using the vitamix. fill 2 small pitchers with it. pour second set of ingredients into the vitamix container and mix it. pour the mixed dressing back in the mixing container, cover, label and put in the fridge.

title: Lemon Tahini Dressing-IF
text: all recipes / salad lemon tahini dressing-if tags: vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free, nut-free lemon tahini dressing updated by chris 7/30/2015 for clarity, quantity adjustment ~1.5 qts gather all ingredients below and one vitamix container. if needed, double the recipe using two vitamix containers. ingredients for one vitamix container (do this twice if making extra) 1 cup lemon juice (juice from about 4-6 fresh lemons) ¾ cup parsley 5 cloves garlic 2 ½ cups water 1 ½ tablespoons tamari 2 teaspoons ground cumin ½ teaspoon white pepper 1 whole tin of joyva tahini (=~2c) ½ cup canola oil using electric juicer, juice the lemons. wash parsley and cut off stems (some of the upper stems are ok). in a medium sized bowl, use a hand whisk to mix lemon juice, tahini and 1 cup of the water so that tahini is not too clumpy (or else it will stall the vitamix). then blend in the vitamix with rest of ingredients. fill two small pitchers if serving today, else put in a 1qt (smallest square) container.

title: Orange Ginger Salad Dressing (2)
text: all recipes / salad orange ginger salad dressing (2) tags: vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free, nut-free, soy-free recipe: orange ginger salad dressing equipment vitamix, microplane zester (or box grater), juicer, 2 pitchers ingredients for 1 batch (~48 servs) ~1 tbsp zest of 2 limes //zest is just the outermost colored layer of the peel ~2 tbsp zest of 2 oranges ~1-2 tbsp juice of the two limes 3 cups juice of about 4 oranges, top off with apple cider vinegar 2” piece ginger, roughly chopped 1 tbsp agave 1 ½ tbsp cumin 1 cup olive oil 2 ½ cups light olive oil 2 tsp salt instructions zest limes and oranges with zester. be careful! very sharp! juice limes and oranges with juicer (next to rice cooker). rough chop ginger (vitamix will do the rest). add all except oil in vitamix container and mix on low. drizzle oil into vitamix mixing while you do. gradually increase speed until all emulsified. divide between 2 small pitchers. cover & store in fridge (if not for today, label and date also).

title: Orange Ginger Salad Dressing
text: all recipes / salad orange ginger salad dressing tags: vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free, nut-free, soy-free orange ginger salad dressing 1.5qts ~1t zest of 2 limes ~2t zest of 2 oranges ~1-2t juice of the 2 limes 3 c juice about 4 oranges and top off with apple cider vinegar 2t chopped ginger (about a 2” piece…coarse chop it and let the vitamix chop it fine along with the rest) 1 ½ t ground cumin (pre-ground is fine) 1 c olive oil 2 ½ c canola oil using the microplane zester or box grater, scrape off just the colored layer of rind from the limes and oranges, try not to get much of the white (it is more bitter). be careful with your fingers and knuckes, this tool is very sharp ! using the electric juicer, juice the limes and oranges. add all except oil to the blender. blend. if room in the vitamix, drizzle in the oil as you keep blending. if no room, transfer to a larger container and whisk in the oil taste (drizzle a little into a separate spoon) and adjust salt, pepper or other seasonings for one meal: fill 2 small pitchers. serve with smallest ladles.

title: Orange Tahini Salad Dressing
text: all recipes / salad orange tahini salad dressing tags: vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free, nut-free, soy-free recipe: orange tahini salad dressing equipment vitamix, 2 pitchers ingredients for 1 batch (~48 servs) 2 ¼ cups orange juice (check if we bought some, else squeeze ~4-6 oranges), use at least one or two fresh oranges (ie the 2 you zest below) 2 oranges zest of two oranges 2 tbsp lemon juice 1 cup tahini (1st use up any partial jars on the breakfast tray..) 1c=½ jar 1 cup water 2 ¾ tsp salt 1 ½ tbls agave 2 ½ tbls finely chopped ginger 5 tbls apple cider vinegar 2 cups light olive oil instructions add all except oil in vitamix container and mix on low, gradually increasing speed. drizzle oil into vitamix mixing while you do. gradually increase speed until all emulsified. divide between 2 small pitchers. cover & store in fridge (if not for today, label and date also).

title: Orange Vinaigrette
text: all recipes / salad orange vinaigrette tags: vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free, nut-free, soy-free recipe: orange vinaigrette equipment vitamix, microplane zester (or box grater), electric juicer, 2 pitchers ingredients for 1 batch (~48 servs) ~1 tbsp zest of 2 limes //zest is just the outermost colored layer of the peel ~2 tbsp zest of 2 oranges ~1-2 tbsp juice of the two limes 2 ½ cups see if there is store-bought fresh oj, if not, juice ~6 oranges ½ cup apple cider vinegar ½ cup dijon mustard ½ cup agave 1 cup olive oil 2 cups light olive oil 1 t salt 1 tbls black pepper instructions zest limes and oranges with zester. be careful! very sharp! juice limes and oranges with juicer (next to rice cooker). add all except oil in vitamix container and mix on low. drizzle oil into vitamix mixing while you do. gradually increase speed until all emulsified. divide between 2 small pitchers. cover & store in fridge (if not for today, label and date also).

title: Pasta Puttanesca Notes
text: all recipes / entree pasta puttanesca notes tags: neither, nut-free pasta puttanesca a la dan landry notes from watching dan make it ingredients: for ~50 + supper lo lots of evoo (coat rondo to 1/8 “ or more) ~40 cloves garlic, chopped in mini-cuis ~1 ½ cups black olives cured in oil, chopped roland foods oil cured black olives pitted whole olives specialty imported food 5-pound bag (far less than this needed…1lb or less plenty—actually would be fine with our kalamatas, maybe better even. calabrian peppers seeded and chopped roland foods calabrian chili peppers in vinegar, specialty imported food, 17.5-ounce package oregano, fresh if we have: 3-4 long stems leaves chopped, (or probl 3-4 t dry) ~2 ½ c capers save caper liquid mix (lg) jar of caper liquid with equal parts? water 12x14 oz cans crushed tomatoes 3-4 c flat leaf parsley, chopped save some for garnish 8lbs spiral pasta, plus 1-2 lbs of gf as needed optional: pan fried chunks of tofu mixed in service with parmesan cheese directions: 🡪 start 32 qt pot of water boiling at 9:30 --takes long time to boil 1 ½ hrs even. (our pasta insert pan isn’t really big enough). prep all ingredients. about 11:00: heat a large skillet (rondo??) over medium heat and add oil, garlic, anchovies, and chopped black olives??. saute mixture until anchovies melt into oil and completely dissolve and garlic is tender, about 3 minutes: your kitchen never smelled so good! add olives, capers. saute some more, let it sit awhile on very low or off to blend flavors. if using: pan fry chunks of x-firm tofu (we used frozen/thawed which was the best consistency)—he had it in big chunks, i might have liked smaller or none. add tomatoes, oregano, calabrian peppers, caper water, black pepper, and parsley. [take out a no-tofu portion if needed. add tofu to rest.] bring sauce to a bubble, reduce heat, and simmer 8 to 10 minutes. save some sauce out for the gf portion (and/or maybe no-soy portion if using tofu)l 2. while it simmers, make 2 kinds of pasta (wheat for most, gf for however many): you could make the gf pasta by just pouring some of the clean boiling water over the gf (or get tea water)….let is sit about a minute. when the pasta is a couple of minutes from done (less done than al dente), don’t just drain it, lift pasta out with big ladel including some water & ,add it to the sauce, maybe add more pasta water to the sauce and [bring the whole thing back to boil—see next sentence], hard to really mix and get that effect in the full rondo, but do add the pasta water and try to keep it mixed it…it won’t really come to a boil, don’t burn it, but the idea is this binds the starches in the pasta & pasta water with the sauce & make it creamy. garnish with parsley. serve with parmesan & vegan parm.

title: Pasta Sauce
text: all recipes / side pasta sauce tags: vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free, nut-free, soy-free alt week 2 day 7 pg 1 of 2 make ahead recipe: pasta sauce for lasagna equipment rondo or large sauce pot note: for retreat use, this part must be made ahead and frozen (no time on the retreat day of serving!) this makes about 14 quarts (freezes in 2 8qt cambros) for serving as a sauce: ingredients (note: this probably is not enough for just serving over pasta, it is enough for lasagna for 2 4” deep pans of lasagna per the recipe in the folder.) 50 servings olive oil as needed 4lbs 3 lbs onions chopped 4lbs 3lbs mushrooms, sliced 30 24 cloves garlic, minced in mini-cuisinart 4 6lb cans 2 6lbs cans tomato sauce (or if only diced tomato blend in vitamix to make a sauce) 5 cans 3 cans tomato paste 1 + 2t c ¾ cup dry basil 8 t 6 t oregano 5 t 3 t thyme 10 8 bay leaves ?to taste ¼ cup sugar [2c 1 ½ cups] sun dried tomato (optional) to taste salt and pepper to taste 6lbs 4 lbs spinach frozen or wait and add when thawing add water if too thick (should be pretty thick though). alt week 2 day 7 recipe: pasta sauce pg 2 of 2 instructions sauteing add olive oil to pan on medium-high heat and add onion. when onions are partly soft, add mushrooms and saute until water is released & mostly cooked off.] cook until onions softened then add garlic. cook garlic for 1-2 minutes until fragrant then proceed to add ingredients add ingredients. add tomato sauce, tomato paste, basil, oregano, thyme, bay leaves and sugar. if using sun-dried tomatoes they can be added now too. bring to boil, then lower to simmer. simmer for 1-3 hours to let flavors integrate. salt and pepper to taste. add spinach note: this step can be done at end of making the sauce ahead of time, or best: just before using it for lasagna: if using frozen: thaw and squeeze dry (thoroughly very important!), then add after the sauce is done.

title: Peanut Lime Dressing
text: all recipes / salad peanut lime dressing tags: vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free peanut lime dressing page 1 of 1 note: this is intended to be served on the side with the thai salad for first day supper. equipment vitamix, bowl ingredients for ~48 2 ¼ c peanut butter 2c water 1 ¾ c lime juice (10-12 limes), keep zest of ~4 (ok to top off with lemons if limes are short or not juicy) ¾ c rice vinegar 3 tsp sesame oil ½ cup agave ½ cup tamari 6 cloves garlic (vitamix will chop) 1 t ginger (rough chop, vitamix will fine chop) 1 ½ cups light olive oil instructions: mix peanut butter and water in a bowl with a whisk. add that and all else except light oil to the vitamix, mix. drizzle in oil while mixing to emulsify. taste & adjust balance of agave, tamari, vinegar, water..

title: Peanut Sesame Dressing
text: all recipes / salad peanut sesame dressing tags: vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free peanut sesame dressing page 1 of 1 equipment vitamix, bowl ingredients for ~48 as a pre-tossed salad, either the supper noodle or rice, or a slaw, not enough for a self-serve 1t light olive oil 2t sesame oil ½ cup ginger, chopped in mini-cuisinart 6 cloves garlic, chopped in mini-cuisinart (easiest when thawed) 2 cups peanut butter 3 cups water ¾ cup rice vinegar ¾ cup tamari ½ cup agave instructions: pre-mix pb & water with a whisk (too thick for vitamix to handle). vitamix the rest & add in the pb/water mix.

title: Pumpkin Chocolate Chip Cookies
text: all recipes / dessert pumpkin chocolate chip cookies tags: vegetarian, nut-free, soy-free pumpkin chocolate chip cookies yield:60 cookies ingredients 1 cup (2 sticks) unsalted butter, softened 1 cup white sugar 1 cup light brown sugar 2 large eggs 1 teaspoon vanilla extract 1 cup canned pumpkin puree 3 cups all-purpose flour //did it with tj’s gluten free…yummy 2 teaspoons baking soda 1/2 teaspoon salt 1 teaspoon ground cinnamon 1/2 teaspoon ground ginger 1/4 teaspoon ground nutmeg 1/4 teaspoon ground cloves 2 cups (12-ounce bag) chocolate chips nonstick cooking spray or parchment paper directions heat the oven to 350 degrees f. spray cookie sheets with nonstick spray or line them with parchment paper. using a mixer, beat the butter until smooth. beat in the white and brown sugars, a little at a time, until the mixture is light and fluffy. beat in the eggs 1 at a time, then mix in the vanilla and pumpkin puree. in a large bowl, whisk together the flour, baking soda, salt, cinnamon, ginger, nutmeg, and cloves. slowly beat the flour mixture into the batter in thirds. stir in the chips. scoop the cookie dough by heaping tablespoons onto the prepared cookie sheets and bake for 15 to 20 minutes , or until the cookies are browned around the edges. remove the cookie sheets from the oven and let them rest for 2 minutes. take the cookies off with a spatula and cool them on wire racks. recipe courtesy george duran, foodnetwork.com save

title: ALT Supper Dal Soup or Casserole
text: all recipes / soup alt supper dal soup or casserole tags: vegetarian, gluten-free, nut-free, soy-free if day 5 alt supper recipe: dal soup or casserole soup: use largest 32 qt stock pot, making ~15-16 qts soup ingredients what you have leftover curried cauliflower (if you made plain steamed, look at the curry recipe and add some of those spices and some frozen peas) ~4qts leftover dal ~3 med cans tomatoes with juice 1 lg can coconut milk broth water + bouillon paste as needed to make total ~15-16 qts of soup 1-2 qts leftover rice instructions: mix it all up, bring to a boil, taste, turn off, cover and should keep hot for the afternoon. serve with sides of leftover raita or yogurt, and leftover chutney or raisins. casserole: fill two 2” deep hotel pans at least half full casserole ingredients for ~48 leftover dal (~ 4-5 quarts..if less than this, add a can of white or garbanzo beans. leftover cauliflower and peas (add more frozen peas if short). mix veggies with 2 small cans of coconut milk. leftover rice (~ 4-5 quarts, if short, make some more on the stove) if you added a lot of new unseasoned stuff, stir in 1-2 tsp curry powder. instructions: layer food into the 2 pans: rice, veggies, dal. serve with sides of leftover raita or yogurt, and leftover chutney or raisins.

title: Black Eyed Pea Salad
text: all recipes / salad black eyed pea salad tags: vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free, soy-free week 2 alt recipe: black eyed pea salad page 1 of 3 equipment if making peas & rice: 2 10-12 qt sauce pans ingredients: (assumes dukkah spice mix is pre-made–see recipe below, do ahead) #50, some lo 8 cups dry black-eyed peas = ~6.25 qts cooked 3 cups dry wild rice = ~4qts cooked 1.5 cups ev olive oil 1 ½ cups dukkah (mideast spice mix, not dukkha we hope–try to pre-make) 1 cup + zest lemon juice, plus zest all the lemons and set aside to use as needed 1 cup + ~1 cup pomegranate molasses //we always wind up adding another cup at the end 4 cups walnuts toasted & chopped (still big chunks, like cut halves in half..) 4 cups pomegranate seeds (=4 or 5 large poms, seeded) 3 cups minced parsley 1 cup minced mint 6 bunches thin sliced scallions (white & green parts) salt & pepper to taste week 2 alt recipe: black eyed pea salad page 2 of 3 instructions first thing: cook & cool peas, rice. toast walnuts. assuming pre-soaked: rinse peas & cover with water by ~3” in a 12qt stock pot, bring to boil, reduce to simmer, cover. cook ~20-40 mins or until done (let’s see…never done this…ests vary). we want them al dente, not mushy for the salad . drain, maybe spread out on a sheet pan to let cool off when done. it’s a room-temp salad. rinse rice & add 4:1 water in a 10-12qt stock pot, bring to boil, reduce to simmer, cover. cook ~40 mins or until well done (all soft). drain if needed and maybe spread out on a sheet pan to let cool off when done. put walnuts in to toast in ~250 oven…check every 10 mins, not too dark. mix sauce whisk the ev olive oil, the dukkah, lemon juice, 1 c. pomegranate molasses, 1t salt, 2tsp pepper. mix salad mix the room-temp peas, rice, ~¾ of the pomegranate seeds (saving rest for garnish), parsley, mint, scallions and sauce. if more than ½ hour before serving: refrigerate and bring back out ~½ hour before serving. just before serving: taste and add: typically the 2nd cup of pom. molasses, quite a bit of the lemon zest, maybe another t of salt… mix in the toasted walnuts. garnish with the rest of the pomegranate seeds. week 2 alt recipe: dukkah p 3 of 3 makes 2 cups, plenty for above 15 oz can chickpeas/garbanzo beans 1 t olive oil ½ cup pistachios toasted 1/3 cup black sesame seeds, toasted 2 ½ t coriander seeds, toasted 1 t cumin seeds, toasted 2 t fennel seeds, toasted 1 ½ t pepper 1 ¼ t salt roast/toast rinse & dry one 15oz can of chickpeas. toss with olive oil. roast in 350 oven for ~40-50 mins, tossing every 10 mins. set aside to cool. also toast pistachios a few minutes in the same oven if not pre-toasted (no oil), watch carefully. lightly and separately (because of differences in timing and grinding instructions) toast sesame seeds, coriander & cumin on the stove in a skillet. grind & mix process cooled roasted chickpeas in mini cuisinart until coarse ground. put in bowl. pulse toasted pistachio & sesame to coarse ground. add to bowl. pulse coriander & cumin to fine ground. add to bowl. add to bowl pepper & salt & mix it all together. keeps for a week or so in a jar in fridge.

title: Blackbean Burgers
text: all recipes / entree blackbean burgers tags: vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free, nut-free week 2 day 7 recipe: blackbean burgers page 1 of 2 equipment : big bowl, robocoupe, mini-cuisinart, sheet pans ingredients for ~50 servings =66 burgers for 36 using ⅓ cup per, this larger recipe made 66 burgers, quite a few people ate 2. the smaller (~⅔) made 46, was way too many for 36 light eaters! you might want to cut these down further for light eaters or fewer people [ingredient description] 11 t 8t vegan egg + water as directed on package 2 c 1 ⅓ c finely chopped (ie in robo coupe) re-hydrated shitake mushrooms ¾ c ½ c finely minced onion (mini cuis?) 25 16 cloves garlic, finely minced (mini cuis?) 8 ¼ c 6c rolled oats (our std. oatmeal), quickly pulsed 5-6 times in robocoupe (not all the way to flour, in between oats and flour) 16 c = 2 6lb or < 6 29oz cans or (~7c dry) 4 x29 oz cans= 4 ½ c dry already cooked black beans. (start at 6:40 if need to cook them, or use an instant pot) 3 c 2c sunflower seeds 3 c 2c shredded carrots 1 ½ c 1c shredded beets 1 ½ t 1t chili powder 5 t 3t1t smoked paprika 3 t 2t ground cumin ½ c 6t olive oil 3 t 2t salt 2 ¾ tsp 2t balsamic vin. 2t?? 1 ½ t ?? vegan liquid smoke if we have any (new idea, start small) 2 ¾ c 2c chopped parsley week 2 day 7 recipe: blackbean burgers page 2 of 2 instructions early: maybe at 6:40 …set the shitakes to soak in hot (tea machine) water [if you don’t have canned or pre-made beans, start the black beans and plan to stay with them until done or turn off for sit.] ~9:30 prep ingredients mix the vegan egg per package instructions strain canned beans saving liquid in case needed (probably not) lightly pulse the oats in robocoup (using the clear plastic setup) (5-6 quick pulses) squeeze shitakes dry, trim hard stems, chop in mini-cuisinart, or robocoup or by hand until finely chopped, not all the way to paste. mince onions & garlic (by hand or in mini-cuis) chop parsley mix roughly mix all ingredients in a large bowl in batches as it fits, pulse mixture in robocoupe–not all the way to a puree, leaving some rough texture. if needed, add some bean liquid or more oats to get a good texture for forming into patties. shape scoop out 1/3 cup portions and shape by hand (wearing gloves) into burger patties. make them on the thin side (~1/4 “), they are dense. let patties sit about 5 minutes before baking. bake at 350 for 15 minutes, flip over and bake 15 mins on other side. ?cheese maybe add cheese on the diet-appropriate quantity for last few mins. a popular option with the dairy eaters. or serve on side. we do now have sliced vegan cheese to put out, but leave several plain.

title: Blended Simple Black Bean Soup
text: all recipes / soup blended simple black bean soup tags: vegetarian, gluten-free, nut-free, soy-free day 5 recipe: blended black bean soup page 1 of 2 equipment 32 qt (largest) stock pot with pot-saver under it ingredients if using dry beans: soak overnight, allow ~1-2 hours to cook before adding them to the soup for ~50 (~19qts) for ~36 w supper with some leftover as a base for a supper soup with lots of added veggies & broth, tomatoes etc. ~⅓ cup ~⅓ cup olive oil (to coat bottom of stock pot) 4lbs (~7ea) 3lbs onions, ½” medium/large dice - rough chop 7lbs 5 ½ lbs carrots, ½ “ medium/large dice - rough chop 25ea 20ea garlic cloves, chopped 10 qts cooked = ~4.5 qts dry 8qts cooked ~3.6 qts dry black beans [or ~13 29oz cans!!] [or 6.6lbs dry for shopping, best to measure in quarts] 1 jar btb ¾ jar bouillon: dissolve it in ~2qts hot tea-urn water ~9 qts total 7.5 qts total water (use 2qts hot with bouillon as above, + bean cooking or canned water, plus remaining cold to reach the total on left.) 2 ½ t 2 t oregano 3 t + 1t 3t ground coriander 5 t + 2t 4.5 t cumin 1 tsp taste ¾ t cayenne pepper 1 t + to taste 1t to taste salt ½ cup + 1t = ~7ea ½ cup fresh lime juice, save some zest in case needed //maybe more for avos 3 bu 2 bu topping: cilantro 3 pints 2 ½ pints topping: sour cream maybe mixed with green chilies //and/or see vegan cashew green chili cream recipe 3 cups 3 cups topping: roasted pumpkin seeds day 5 recipe: blended black bean soup page 2 of 2 instructions prepare ingredients cook the beans if not using canned. empty soak water, cover by 2” with fresh water, save (& measure?) cooking water to use as part of the soup liquid. dice onions, carrots by hand, chop garlic in mini-cuisinart juice limes. juicer is near rice-cooker. maybe zest a couple and set zest aside. mix bouillon in 2 qts hot tea-urn water. note: this is not a long-cooking soup, about 1 ½ hrs from start to saute to finish blending. beans are cooked separately. make soup be sure heat-saver disk (on stove shelf) is placed under stock pot coat the bottom of the pot with olive oil to about ⅛” deep sauté (=fry in a little oil uncovered, stirring occasionally) the onions, garlic and carrots until the onions are getting soft and translucent (not brown). drain beans saving liquid and use the liquid as part of the water measure. add rest: black beans, bouillon, water, oregano, coriander, cumin, cayenne and salt. bring to a boil. reduce heat, cover and simmer ~30 minutes. check that carrots are soft. puree the soup until smooth and creamy (there will still be little flecks of beans) using the immersion blender. stir in lime juice and taste (perhaps more salt, pepper, lime zest?, cayenne?) serve with any or all of: cilantro, sour cream and/or vegan green chili cream, diced avocado and roasted pumpkin seeds.

title: Bread sides for White Bean Soup
text: all recipes / side bread sides for white bean soup tags: vegetarian, nut-free, soy-free week 2 day 4 recipe: bread side options for white bean soup equipment either: large trays or 4” hotel pan, foil for bread, bowls for butters either garlic bread or plain artisan bread with “basil butter” (either only if not having butternut squash–check with km what’s planned and what ingredients we have) for garlic bread: 4-5 loaves of sourdough or other “white” artisan bread olive oil (?1 cup to start?) ~20 cloves of garlic minced in the mini cuisinart optional: dried basil and marjoram (~1t each) mix oil and garlic & herbs if using. put mix on the needed number of regular gluten free slices. (do the gf first to avoid contamination of oil & utensils) slice bread in half lengthwise (separating top half and bottom half) spread both with garlic oil mix. put uncovered on large trays. about 11:30: bake at 350 for ~½ hour or until lightly browning. (gf may take less..) slice each baked half into ~1 ½” thick slices. serve in a basket with a decorative cloth (bottom of cloth rack) for “basil butter” and plain heated artisan bread 4-5 loaves mixed artisan breads, sliced thick (or use 2-3 of tj’s big triangles of whole wheat bread, cut triangle in thirds or fourths, then slice) gluten free bread slices as needed (~1 ⅕ per gf person) 1 ¼ lb regular butter ½ tub of earth bal //check quantity est. with no-dairy head-count 1 bunch basil put regular butter out early to soften a bit (not so important if using robocoupe). wash basil proportion the basil between the regular and earth balance. works well to mix the regular in the robo coupe (clear bowl setup) and the non-dairy in the little mini-cuisinart. put sliced bread into a hotel pan, cover with foil or domed lid. ~ 11:30: heat at 350. serve in a basket with butters on the side.

title: Brown Basmati Rice Curry
text: all recipes / entree brown basmati rice curry tags: vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free, nut-free, soy-free week 2 day 5 recipe: brown jasmine or basmati rice equipment large strainer, rice cooker ingredients: note: there may be bags of tj brown jasmine in either pantry, and replace or supplement with brown basmati (they cook together ok). #48 servings with supper leftovers #36 servs with supper [qty] [qty] [ingredient description] 16 cups 12 cups brown jasmine or basmati rice 24 cups 18 cups water instructions rinse the rice well using the large double-mesh strainer (may take several batches). between 10:30-11:00 add water in the ratio of 1 ½ cups of water for each cup of rice. about 10:45: plug in and turn on the cooker. it will take about 50-60mins to cook, then it switches to warm. before serving, check that is has switched to warm. if so, carefully open the lid and fluff it with a wood or plastic tool . unplug the machine to turn off the “warming”. serve with wooden spoons so as not to scratch the container.

title: Butternut Squash Soup
text: all recipes / soup butternut squash soup tags: vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free, nut-free, soy-free week2 alt recipe: butternut squash soup page 1 of 2 equipment 32qt (largest) stock pot with pot-saver under it ingredients *see squash ordering note at bottom ~50 (24qts) with supper lo see how these quantities are looking, consult with km on squash and bouillon amounts.. ~⅓ cup light olive oil (to coat bottom of stock pot) 4 cups thinly sliced onions (ok if they get diced too) 4 cups n/a thinly sliced shallots 8 cups thin sliced leeks (white part only) (see bouquet garnis below, maybe save some greens) 4 cups 2 smallish diced carrots 24 cloves 12 garlic, roughly chopped in mini cuisinart 25lbs cubed butternut squash (see *ordering note at end) ½ cup ¼? agave 1 jar btb bouillon: dissolve it in ~2qts hot tea-urn water 12 qts total water (2qts hot with bouillon as above, + remaining 10 qts cold) 32 sprigs fresh thyme = ~2 packs 8 sprigs parsley 8 bay leaves 2 tsp black peppercorns made into 4 bouquet garni packets (either bags for that purpose or tied in cheesecloth pieces or wrapped well in leek greens) each containing : 8 springs fresh thyme for half: 16, 4 parsley, 4 pay1 tsp pepp 2 sprigs italian parsley 2 bay leaves ½ tsp black peppercorns or pepper salt to taste 1 t + to taste salt 2 quarts optional topping: could have greek yogurt (+vegan), fine without optional topping: could make a shaker of nutmeg (shakers in stair pant) week 2 alt recipe: butternut squash soup page 2 of 2 instructions prepare ingredients locate all ingredients make bouquet garni slice/dice all the onions, leeks, shallots & carrots if not done. mix bouillon in 2 qts hot tea-urn water. saute be sure heat-saver disk (on stove shelf) is placed under stock pot coat the bottom of the pot with light olive oil to about ⅛” deep sauté (=fry in a little oil uncovered, stirring occasionally) the onions, leeks, shallots and carrots until the onions are getting soft and translucent (not brown). add the diced squash, garlic, 3t salt, and 1 ½ t pepper and cook gently for a few minutes, reducing the heat as necessary to keep the garlic and squash from coloring. may need to add a little of the stock to make it stirrable. stir in the agave and cook, stirring, for a few more minutes, stirring often. add stock & simmer add the stock and bouquet garni bags, bring to a simmer and cook until the squash is tender. puree puree the soup until smooth and creamy using the immersion blender. taste and salt as needed. *squash ordering note: i used to try to pre-order 1 week in advance 25lbs of pre-cubed squash from coast, but they have a terrible record of forgetting it, messing it up, bringing the wrong thing..). way too hard for yogis to peel and cube that much hard squash along with everything else needed for the meal. new discoveries: order or buy ~30 lbs = ~10 each of whole butternuts and freeze them whole, then thaw them overnight. now really soft skin and easy enough for yogis to peel and cube. too watery to roast but ok for soup. or better: poke several holes in them with a fork, roast them the day before whole in the oven for ~1hr at 400, let that cool. then easy to peel. or can microwave, but pre-roasting might be easier for 10.

title: Cashew Green Chili Cream(1)
text: all recipes / side cashew green chili cream(1) tags: vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free, soy-free recipe: cashew green chili cream page 1 of 1 equipment vitamix ingredients goes well with “blended black bean soup” recipe. for a simpler alternative: add some lemon juice and salt (both to taste) to a carton of the vegan cashew yogurt, add green chilies if you like & no chili allergies ~48-50 smaller amt for vegan only 4 ½ cups 2 cups cashews, soaked in water as long as overnight, or as short as needed. 2 cups ¾ cup water (fresh, for blending, not the soaking water) (maybe start with a bit less, see what’s needed for thick sauce) 4-5 sm cans 3 sm cans diced green chilis, drained (or start with a bit less water) ¼ cup 2 t lime juice 6 3 garlic cloves (blending will chop) 1 tsp ½ tsp salt ½ tsp ¼ tsp ground cumin pinch (> ⅛ tsp) tiny pinch cayenne (if using mild chilis) instructions: soak cashews as long as you can (longer is smoother, but grainy is fine). drain them. add all ingredients to vitamix blender (works better than robocoupe for this. blend until smooth. taste and adjust seasonings until you like it!

title: Chicken Fried Tofu
text: all recipes / entree chicken fried tofu tags: vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free, nut-free, soy-free week 3 day 3 recipe: chicken fried tofu page 1 of 2 equipment 4 large baking sheets & 1 half sheet, or sometimes 3 large & 3 halves if you roasted the beans. note: best with no parchment, hard to serve with it ), 3 medium metal bowls ingredients note: set aside equiv of one whole sheet if you want to make a leftover out of it for a full house, people will over-eat this until it’s all gone! you may need to put the last ½ sheet to cook over lunch while you serve the other 3 1/2 . 48 servings with leftover supper 48 servings, no leftover supper (avg 2.5 slices each) or ~36 with supper 16lbs=x12 slices per lb= 192 slices= 4 ½ pans @42 per pan 12lbs 144 slices=3 pans @42ea +one half pan tofu sliced thin: try to get 12 slices per lb (eg for a 1lb slab, cut in half, cut each half in half again and then each of the fourths into thirds. for the bigger quantity, bake 4 pans for lunch and stick the ½ pan in as soon as you can and take it out at the end of lunch (~30 minutes). this pan will all go to making the supper (plus hopefully some leftovers of the other 4 pans–set some aside!) ~4cups ~3cups canola oil set up in 1-2 medium small metal bowl for dipping coating mix: 5 ½ cups 4 cups nutritional yeast (ideally “large flake”, but regular works ok too) 5 ½ cups 4 cups “no-chicken” vegetable broth (pseudo-chicken) powdered broth mix (frontier brand)--in stair pantry spice boxes. 2 cups 1 ¾ cup corn starch 3 ½ tbl 2 ½ tbl sage 3 ½ tbl 2 ½ tbl thyme week 3 day 3 recipe: chicken fried tofu page 2 of 2 instructions setup preheat oven to 350 (assume morning yogi has sliced the tofu.) mix coating mix. use “large flake” nutritional yeast if we have it. plan to do this with all 3 cooks: setup one bowl of oil and 2 bowls of coating mix. no parchment! efficient layout on the center island: uncoated tofu sheet-pan mix-bowl oil-bowl mix-bowl sheet-pan person1 person2 person3 coat pieces person 2 dips each slice of tofu in oil and places them alternately in one of the 2 mix bowls. persons 1 and 3 pat the coating onto both sides of the slices and lay them flat (very close to each other but not overlapping) on the sheet pans. takes ~15 mins. bake allow about 30 mins to bake, but keep an eye on browning process. no need to flip the pieces, just check for crispy looking golden brownness on both sides of sample pieces. if done early, maybe turn off oven and leave them in to stay warm. if you plan on supper, hold back at least ¾ or 1 whole tray for that, people tend to just eat this till its gone..;-) serve on the baking sheets.
