title: Chili
text: all recipes / entree chili tags: vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free, nut-free, soy-free chili with yams and peppers page 1 of 2 equipment 32qt (largest) stock pot for beans, rondo for chili, mini cuisinart to cook dry beans: #servings with supper leftovers #servings no supper leftovers (assumes supper leftovers is eg light sprinkle on top of nachos, not a whole other serving) 4 quarts dry pinto beans (km soaks them the night before) water to cover beans instructions rinse beans in a strainer, place in 32 oz stock pot and cover with water by a 6-8 inches. bring to a boil, lower to a simmer and cook for 1-1 ½ hours until beans are tender. add water if too dry. for chili: 1 cup olive oil 8 lbs chopped yellow onion 7lbs red bell pepper chopped 5 lbs sweet potato peeled and chopped into small pieces 50 cloves garlic minced in mini cuisinart 1 ¾ cup chili powder (more if needed) 1/2 cup oregano ¼ cup smoked paprika ½ cup cumin 6lb can diced tomatoes to taste salt cooked beans chili with yams and peppers page 2 of 2 instructions saute heat olive oil in rondo and add onions. saute until translucent. maybe separate out a second no-bell pepper version here (for andrea or other teacher need) add bell peppers and yams until they begin to soften. add ingredients add chili powder, oregano, and cumin to saute mixture and cook for a few minutes. add tomatoes, bring to a boil and lower to a simmer. add beans we keep cooking the beans separately because they need to be cooked almost all morning to get soft, might not have enough heat mixed in with the rest too soon. when the beans are soft enough to eat, mix them in with the rest of the stew. finish let simmer until serving time, adding bean liquid as needed if getting too thick. (or you can cover & turn it off, it will stay warm).

title: Chutney Raita
text: all recipes / side chutney raita tags: vegetarian, gluten-free, nut-free, soy-free day 4 recipe: chutney page 1 of 1 note: usually done by 9:30 yogi helper ingredients apricot/mango chutney 4 cups dried apricots, chopped tip: put some oil on a paper towel and oil the knife frequently, cuts sticky apricots more easily! 3 cups raisins 4 cups = ~1 lb dry dried mango, pre-soaked (save water), cut into bite sized pieces. ¾ cup coconut 6 cups water (include mango water if saved) 3 t rice vinegar 1 ½ t cloves (ground, see below) 2 t coriander seeds (ground, see below) instructions soak the mangos in a metal bowl using hot water (from tea machine) for a few minutes, save water. cut into bite sized pieces. cut the apricots into fourths or sixths. grind the cloves and coriander in the black spice grinder (together is fine). mix all the ingredients together in the smallest stock pot. bring to a boil, reduce heat to simmer and let simmer for about 15 minutes. remove from heat, cool, refrigerate if for next day. nice to garnish with nasturtiums or herbs. day 4 raita page 1 of 1 note: usually done by 9:30 yogi helper make 2 versions, one dairy (larger), one vegan (smaller) (check roster, maybe adjust dairy:vegan proportions, below assumes fewer than ~10 vegan, rest dairy) for dairy for vegan 2 ½ hothouse ½ cucumber (shredded with hand box-grater, or with robocoupe) 1 ½ cartons dairy yog. ½ carton vegan yog. yogurt (use more yogurt if not enough cucumber) ⅓ cup chopped 2t cup chopped mint (maybe irc garden outside kitchen if any, else look for bought) ½ lemon ~1tsp lemon juice and zest 1 t ¼ t ground cumin ½ t lg pinch white pepper ½ t ¼ t garlic powder salt to taste instructions wash mint, pick leaves and cut into thin strips. mix with yogurts. [add shredded cukes if using.] add spices & mix. cover and refrigerate.

title: Curried Cauliflower and Peas
text: all recipes / entree curried cauliflower and peas tags: vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free, nut-free, soy-free recipe: curried cauliflower equipment one 6” (deepest) full-sized hotel pans with lid ingredients #servings with supper leftovers #servings no supper leftovers [qty] [qty] [ingredient description] 16 small heads=1 case cauliflower 3lbs..[note bag size, if 10oz, use 4-5 bags] frozen peas ½ cup canola oil 4t curry powder 1t paprika 4t spice mix for the dal 1-6lb can coconut milk 2 cans 2-14oz cans diced tomatoes recipe: curried cauliflower and peas instructions make sauce, add veg and cook on stove top open the cans of coconut milk & tomatoes so they are ready to pour. mix the curry powder, paprika and dal spice mix together. fry the spice mix for a minute or so in the oil in bottom of the hotel pan on low heat watching and stirring the whole time. add the coconut milk and tomatoes to the fried spices mix. add the cauliflower and stir up a bit if possible. cover and cook over medium heat, lower the heat once it gets going? cook about 30 mins…start maybe 11:15, check and stir occasionally. about 11:45, add the peas and stir it all up if possible.

title: Dal
text: all recipes / entree dal tags: vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free, nut-free, soy-free day 4 recipe: red lentil dal page 1 of 2 equipment 32 oz stockpot (largest one,) largest skillet ingredients //note has a few changes from lael 11/2023 #50w/ supper leftovers 50 w/no supper 36 with supper 5 qts 4qts 3 qts red lentils (d1:c3) 9 qt 7 qts 5 ½ qts water (add more if needed, plus we use the liquid from the tomatoes below) 4 t 3 ½ t 3 t salt 3 ½ lbs 3lbs 2lbs onions, medium dice 1 ¼ cup 1 cup ⅔ c chopped ginger 1 ¼ cup = 7.5 oz) (+ 2t if making fancy cauli) 30 cloves 25 cl 20 cl garlic (chopped, divide the total in half, use in 2 ways below) 4 tbs 3 ½ t 3 tbl turmeric 1 ½ cups 1 ¼ c 1 cup light olive oil 4 tbl 3 ½ t 3 tbl mustard seeds 4tbl 3 ½ t 3 tbl cumin (pre-ground or toasted & ground from whole) 4tbl 3 ½ t 3 tbl coriander (pre-ground or toasted & ground from whole) 1 ½ tbl 1 t 1 tbl fenugreek ¼ tsp ¼ t ¼ tsp cayenne pepper, maybe more..taste! 1 6lb +1 28oz or 4 28oz 1 6lb or 3 28oz 2 28oz canned tomatoes (do use juice) (note 1 6lb can = 3.6 28oz cans) 4ea 4ea 3ea bay leaves ½ cup ~⅓ c ~⅓ c lime juice (save rinds to zest if using roasted cauli recipe) as needed as need as ned salt , juice 1-2 lemons? day 4 recipe: red lentil dal page 2 of 2 instructions start lentils simmering saute the onions in some oil in the bottom of the stock pot. rinse the lentils in the strainer under running water. tends to clump, separate with your fingers. this may take several batches in the strainer. put lentils, bay leaves, water & salt in the stock pot. bring to a boil and skim off foam. after foam is skimmed off, lower heat add ginger and half the garlic. reduce to an active simmer. check frequently that it is still actively simmering, but not over-boiling. stir often all the way to the bottom. always put a heat-deflector under this pot, easy to burn! . maybe use big paddle. if it seems to be getting too thick, you can add more water. it should be thick, but still pourable. preparing the spice mixture once dal is cooked add spices to dal shortly before serving, about 12:00. once dal is cooked prepare spices. begin by heating the oil in the large skillet until hot. add mustard seeds and stir cooking just until they pop, just a few seconds. once they pop add cayenne, tumeric, bay leaves, cumin, coriander, fenugreek and rest of garlic stirring a few times. turn heat to low and allow spice mixture to cook until garlic just begins to brown. add tomatoes and cook a few minutes stirring often. remove bay leaves from dal if you can find them and add the spice/tomato mixture to dal along with juice of limes. taste for heat and salt. (probably add juice of 2 lemons, maybe a little brown sugar also...have all the cooks taste it!)

title: Fancier Mushroom Gravy
text: all recipes / side fancier mushroom gravy tags: vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free, nut-free recipe: mushroom onion gravy page 1 of 2 equipment large skillet, small rondo (aka prune pot) or 10qt pot ingredients 48 with supper leftovers 48 with no supper leftovers 6lbs 5lbs onions, slivered 5lbs 4lbs regular white or brown mushrooms, sliced 7 6 dried shitake mushrooms (optional, usually don’t have) 20 cups 16 cups stock: cups of water as shown + 1tsp betterthanb. per cup. (use mushroom btb if we have any, else “no-chicken” is fine) 2 ½ tbls 2 tbls sage 2 ½ tbls 2 tbls thyme 7 tbls 6 tbls tamari 5 tbls 4 tbls sherry vinegar 2 ½ tsp 2 tsp black pepper if needed if needed salt (taste after adding tamari..) 8 tbls 7 tbls corn starch dissolved in cold water..start with less and see recipe: fancier mushroom onion gravy page 2 of 2 instructions: prepare in largest skillet, begin to carmelize the onions. [carmelize means fry them in oil but on very low heat for a long time (~30-40 mins?) stirring occasionally until they all turn brown but not burned] . this is optional, can just saute them until soft if short of time. start stock mix the bouillon, add in the dry shitakes if using and simmer. (ideal to use the 8qt “prune pot”) chop shiktakes when shitakes are soft, fish them out, remove stems, chop them up & return them to stock. saute mushrooms when the onions are done, set aside and saute the mushrooms in the same skillet (you may need more oil). when done, you could “deglaze” the skillet: put a cup or so of stock water in the skillet and stir it up to capture the flavored oil and carmelized bits, pour it back into the stock. add rest add the carmelized onions, sauted mushrooms and all other seasonings except the cornstarch to the stock. thicken mix cornstarch with enough cold water to dissolve it. add to the gravy. bring to a boil for 3-5 minutes until it thickens. return to simmer. taste and adjust seasoning if needed.

title: Ginger Tofu
text: all recipes / entree ginger tofu tags: vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free, nut-free day 1 recipe: ginger tofu page 1 of 2 equipment two (&½?) large baking trays, blender, large 4qt pitcher ingredients #48 (lunch + some lo for yam side 15 lbs tofu (we use a whole case of 12x15.5oz packs, plus another 2 pounds if we have it), sliced into 12 slices per pack (by morning prep yogi) sauce: 1 ¼ cups chopped ginger (= ~7.5 oz ginger root) 15 cloves garlic 3 cups= 1 ½ containers miso (whatever color we have in stock…eg red, white, yellow..) ~1 tsp sesame oil 1 ½ cups agave 1 ½ cups rice vinegar 2 ¼ cups tamari 4 cups water garnish: 2 bunches scallions, thin slices white and light green parts day 1 recipe: ginger tofu page 2 of 2 instructions preheat oven to 400 (after assist has toasted seeds) slice each ~pound of tofu into 12 long-way rectangular slices (ie 6 per half-pack in our usual brand). layout flat on sheet pans. (prep yogi usually does this) find and set out all the sauce ingredients rough cut the ginger into chunks about ½ inch long. no need to peel it. using one of the blender pitchers (you can share the machine base with the assist cook if needed): put ginger chunks, garlic, miso, sesame oil, agave, rice vinegar and tamari (ie all sauce ingredients except water) in the blender and process gradually raising the speed until smooth. pour into large plastic pitcher and add 4 cups of water, whisk. pour the sauce over the tofu. let the tofu sit in the marinade until time to bake it. put the pans in the oven uncovered for 45-60 minutes total. set a timer to baste every 20 mins or so. if looking too dark, turn heat down or off. if not getting brown by last 20 minutes, turn heat up. just before serving, garnish pans with scallions.

title: Kale with Mushrooms
text: all recipes / side kale with mushrooms tags: vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free, nut-free, soy-free day 1 recipe: kale with mushrooms page 1 of 1 equipment roasting sheet, 2 steamer pan setups ingredients #48 (lunch only) ~⅓ cup? olive oil, enough to lightly coat sliced mushrooms 1 case + 6 heads dino kale dino kale, de-stemmed and torn each leaf-side into 3-4 pieces 4lbs sliced mushrooms instructions first thing in the morning (ie before you need the oven for the tofu): pre-heat oven to 350 toss sliced mushrooms in olive oil, spread on baking sheet. roast for ~15-30 minutes at 350. time depends on how thick they were sliced. check every 10 mins, stir, swap pans on oven shelves as needed. set aside when done (= appealing to eat in your opinion!) or: some prefer to saute them in the largest skillet (check overhead rack or in apron area for large skillets0 ~11:00 about 11:00: steam kale using 2 steamer setups. it will probably take two rounds of 2 steamers each. each one takes about 10 minutes to cook the kale. or: some prefer to saute the kale in the rondo (big round pan under the rice cooker) transfer cooked kale layering with roasted mushrooms into a 4” deep hotel pan to serve. cover to keep warm.

title: Lasagna
text: all recipes / entree lasagna tags: vegetarian, gluten-free, nut-free, soy-free alt week 2 day 7 recipe: lasagna page 1 of 2 equipment 2 2-inch deep (or could use 4” deep for no-slosh, but only half fill) full-sized hotel pans, mixing bowl, 12 qt for side pasta, or another pan or ½ pan if making vegan lasagna ingredients could either make an extra no-dairy no-egg lasagna with the “vegan ricotta” recipe and vegan mozzarella if shopped for, or have sauce, spinach, beans and gf rotelli on the side. 48 servings 36 servings makes 2 full pans / 1 ½ pans 1 recipe ¾ recipe pasta sauce pre-made (see other recipe) 6lbs 4lbs frozen spinach (also listed in the sauce recipe as an option, best to add here) 6 lbs 5 lbs ricotta 8 6 eggs eggs 5 lbs 4 lbs shredded mozzarella separated in half 2 t 1 ½ t salt 1 t ¾ t pepper 3-4 packages as needed no-boil gluten free lasagna (4 10oz packs of barilla or 3 tj 1lb packs seemed plenty) for simple gf,vegan alternative: or if planned ahead: make 1 or ½ pan vegan tofu based lasagna. see “vegan ricotta” recipe infolder and use vegan mozz. our sauce is vegan. ~¾ cup per person pre-made sauce including spinach 1/4 cup per person white (cannelini) beans see pkg portion per person gf pasta such as spirals alt week 2 day 7 recipe: lasagna page 2 of 2 instructions (this assumes the sauce was pre-made earlier..see separate recipe) prepping ingredients preheat oven to 375. start sauce re-heating. see if you need to add the spinach and if so, drain it very well, ie press hard with spoons into large strainer). mix ricotta, eggs, half the mozzarella, salt and pepper. maybe reserve: reserve some sauce (see headcount) for the gf/df alternative (see below). reserve some mozzarella and/or parmesan for a side condiment for diets. layering spray pans with spray oil!! layer the lasagna per pan: bottom (first) => thin layer of sauce to coat the pan noodles ricotta mix (if doing 2 pans, use 1/4th of the total here, if doing 1 ½, use ⅓ the total here) thicker layer of sauce (5-6 cups for a whole pan) light sprinkling of mozzarella noodles ricotta mix (another 1/4th or ⅓ of the total here) thicker layer of sauce (5-6 cups for a whole pan) light sprinkling of mozzarella noodles thin layer of sauce top (last)==> generous sprinkling of mozzarella baking top the pans with the new dome-lids (on top of pan rack), or make peaked lids of foil bake 60 minutes, remove lids and bake another 20 minutes. remove from oven and let set for 20-30 minutes before serving. make gf dairyfree alternative if needed: make gf spiral pasta per package instructions so it is done just prior to serving (typically boils 6-10 mins). heat reserved sauce and white beans in a sauce pan. combine pasta with sauce & beans.

title: Lentil Grape Salad
text: all recipes / salad lentil grape salad tags: vegetarian, gluten-free, soy-free day 6 (or alt 5) recipe: lentil grape salad page 1 of 2 equipment 12 qt stock pot, large skillet, large metal mixing/serving bowl ingredients for #50 with supper leftover for #50 no supper or 36 w/sup 12 cups uncooked 9 cups uncooked french green lentils (the small dark green ones) to cover by ~3” to cover by ~3” water (we will drain them, so plenty is fine) 3 3 bay leaves 4t 3t salt, + to taste ~½ cup ~½ cup olive oil (as needed to saute, maybe use a little more to make the whole dish less dry) 24 each = ~16lbs 18 each = ~12 lbs leeks, thin sliced, use only the white to light green parts (sold as bunch of 3, so 8bu or 6bu) 7 t 5t dijon mustard // more to taste 2 cups 1 ½ cups sherry vinegar //more to taste 2 ¼ cup 1 ¾ cups chopped fresh mint (maybe from the garden outside kitchen door or bought in clamshell packs) 1 ¼ cup 1 cup chopped fresh parsley 4 cups 3 cups **nuts, usually pecans or shelled pistachios 6lbs 4lbs red grapes, cut in half to release some juice ~2lbs ~2lbs feta cheese, crumbled on the side if we have some left (set up by assistant) **consider nut allergies, maybe set aside no-nut portions for lunch & supper day 6 (or alt 5) recipe: lentil grape salad page 2 of 2 instructions cook lentils rinse the lentils, put lentils, water, salt and bay leaves in a stock pot. bring to a boil and lower to an active simmer. stir occasionally and add water if it gets low. simmer about 20-30 minutes until lentils are cooked but not mushy. when the lentils are done, strain them in a colander and remove the bay leaves if you can find them. make leeks and sauce sauté the leeks in the olive oil until soft, using the large skillet or the rondo. make a sauce of the mustard and sherry vinegar and a bit more olive oil and mix (note: we now add this to the warm lentils, not sauteed with the leeks). mix salad mix the lentils, mustard sauce, grapes, mint, parsley and sauteed leeks in a large metal or plastic bowl. just before serving: **check nut allergies, maybe set aside a no-nut portion. add nuts to main portion. serve in a large plastic or metal bowl. serve with crumbled feta cheese on the side if there is enough.

title: Lentil Soup
text: all recipes / soup lentil soup tags: vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free, nut-free, soy-free opening recipe: lentil soup page 1 of 3 equipment 32qt (largest) stock pot with pot-saver under it, small skillet, zester, juicer, mini cuisinart ingredients ~48 (14-15qts) ~⅓ cup olive oil (to coat bottom of stock pot) 4lbs onions, ½” dice 4lbs carrots, ½ “ dice 1 head celery, ½ “ dice 4lbs yukon potatoes, ¾ ” dice 2t salt 10c lentils (if we have plain ones, use them, otherwise use “french green”) 4 bay leaf 12 qts water (add more later if too thick) 2c = ~1 ½ bun. parsley finely chopped 4 stalks marjoram (from the garden, or 2t dry or 2t dry thyme) 4t cumin seeds 25 +5 for later garlic cloves (probably in white yogi freezer) 4 bunches greens, usually collards, could be kale etc. ~2t zest~½ c juice zest and juice of 2 lemons 4t sherry vinegar 3t smoked paprika rest of paste: ½ c more olive oil, the 5 garlics saved above 2t each, to taste salt and pepper (add each gradually & taste) o-night recipe: lentil soup page 2 of 3 instructions prepare ingredients locate all ingredients measure out lentils, check for stones, rinse and set aside dice onions, carrots, celery and potatoes collards: remove thick stem from center, slice leaf halves crosswise into 1” wide strips wash lemons zest lemons (=scrape off the thin outermost yellow layer of skin) using either the microplane (sharp!) or box grater (suggest wearing the cut-resistant glove for either) juice lemons using electric juicer or wooden reamer wash parsley, discard main trunk of stems, finely chop rest chop garlic in mini cuisinart on chop setting (best if thawed) toast and grind cumin using small skillet, watching carefully just till it is fragrant. grind in black spice grinder, wipe out grinder before and after. sauté be sure heat-saver disk (on stove shelf) is placed under stock pot coat the bottom of the pot with olive oil to about ⅛” deep sauté (=fry in a little oil uncovered, stirring occasionally) the onions until they are getting soft. o-night recipe: lentil soup page 3 of 3 (sauté, cont’d) add in the carrots & celery and 2t salt. sauté for 20 minutes or so to develop the flavor. add in the potatoes and sauté for another 10 minutes. tip: you may want to stand on a stool and/or use the big paddle to get good stirring leverage. cook lentils add the lentils, bay leaves, marjoram, cumin, garlic, parsley and water to the pot and stir. gradually bring to a boil on medium high heat. then reduce to an active simmer. let it simmer at least until the lentils are soft (1 hr or more), fine to leave it on 2hrs or more or until we leave for the meeting stirring occasionally, add more water if it is getting too thick. prepare paprika mix (~4:00) prepare the final paprika mix to add in later: chop the extra garlic, sauté it with the smoked paprika in the extra olive oil in the small skillet for about a minute. turn the fire off and leave it. add greens (~4:20) just before going to the orientation meeting, stir in the greens. turn the fire off and put a lid on the pot. after meeting: (~5:10) leave meeting early. add lemon juice, zest, sherry vinegar & smoked paprika oil mix. add half the suggested salt & pepper, taste and add more as needed. put gluten free bread in the oven just to warm up a bit. help get the main bread into a basket.

title: Mashed Potatoes
text: all recipes / side mashed potatoes tags: vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free, nut-free recipe: mashed potatoes page 1 of 1 equipment 2 6” deep hotel pans, large metal bowl, potato masher (hand tool), maybe mixer ingredients 48 servings with supper leftover 48 servings no supper leftover or ~36 w/supper 20lbs 15 lbs yellow, white or red potatoes cut into quarters yukon gold are the best if avail.. ~ 1 ½ cups 1 cup earth balance (no-soy if needed) 1 tbls+to taste 2 tsp+ to taste salt instructions: put into 2 deep hotel pans and cover with water & 1tsp salt per pan cover and bring to a boil cook until tender (est 40-45 mins) drain each pan into large collander and put back in the pan working in batches, mash with hand-held pastry cutter (or you could try the electric mixer or immersion blender if you like super smooth, but rough is fine) add in earth balance as needed for good mash-potato texture. salt to taste (lightly, they can always add).

title: Moroccan Chickpeas and Chard
text: all recipes / entree moroccan chickpeas and chard tags: vegetarian, gluten-free, nut-free, soy-free week 2 day 6 recipe: moroccan chickpeas and chard p. 1 of 2 equipment rondo for stew ingredients #48 servings with supper #36 servings with supper leftovers [qty] [qty] [ingredient description] 4lbs 3 lbs chickpeas, qty=dry (soaked overnight or quick soaked by km) 5lbs 3.5 lbs yellow onions chopped 2 lg 1 ½ lg jalapeno pepper, seeded & chopped fine 20 15 cloves garlic ⅓ cup 4 tbls ginger 2 t 1 ½ t salt 3t 2 t + 1 t tumeric 3t 2 t + 1 t paprika 2t 1 ½ t cinnamon 1 ½ t 1 t + 1 t cumin 1 ½ t 1 t + 1 t black pepper ?½ tsp pinch cayenne (to taste, not too hot for yogis, more if no jalapeno) 2 6oz cans 1 ½ tomato paste 8 bulbs 6 bulbs fennel bulb (save fronds for garnish) 9 bunches 7 bu rainbow chard (stems chopped separately, leave in lg chunks) 15 11 carrots , diced //convert to lbs! 14 lg-ish 12 lg-ish yukon potatoes //convert to lbs! 3 cups 2 ¼ cup dried apricots, diced week 2 day 6 recipe: moroccan chickpeas and chard p. 2 of 2 ingredients, cont’d ½ cup 6 t lemon juice, save zest also 2x32oz 1 ½? greek yogurt (for side) 4 bunches 3 bu cilantro (for side) instructions note: we’re not cooking the chickpeas separately, just add into stew per below 10:15 step. saute steps heat oil in rondo pan over medium heat. add onion and jalapeño and sauté until limp, a few minutes. add garlic, ginger, salt, turmeric, paprika, cinnamon, cumin, black pepper and cayenne and sauté until they release their fragrance, about 2 minutes. add tomato paste and sauté for another minute, until darkened but not burned. (if tomato paste looks too dark too quickly, lower heat.) add fennel, chard stems, carrot and turnip/potatoes and continue to sauté until vegetables start to soften, about 20 minutes? add chickpeas by about 10:15: rinse, drain soaking chickpeas, add to stew. add fresh water to cover. return heat to high if you lowered it and bring to a simmer. partly cover pot, lower heat to medium low, and simmer for about 1 1/2 to 2 hours (ie for the rest of the morning), until chickpeas are softened. add more water as needed (this should be like a stew and nearly fill the rondo once the chard is added) finish about 11:30: add apricots about 11:50: add chard leaves,and lemon juice & zest to taste, continue simmering until chard is tender, about 5 minutes longer. season with more salt if desired, and serve garnished with reserved fennel fronds. serve with greek yogurt and cilantro on side

title: Peanut Stew
text: all recipes / entree peanut stew tags: vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free, soy-free week 2 day 1 recipe: peanut stew page 1 of 2 equipment : rondo ingredients 48 servings with supper lo ~36 servings with supper lo [qty] [ingredient description] 2qts dry 1 ½ qts dry chickpeas (pre-soaked) (or ~6 28oz cans for lg, 4.5 forms) ~3 ~3 bay leaves (for cooking chickpeas, or add to stew if canned) ½ cup as needed olive oil 5 lbs 4 lbs red onions chopped ¾ cup 4 ½ tbls minced ginger 30 cloves 23 cloves garlic minced 2 ½ cups 2 cups peanut butter 9lbs 7lbs yams chopped into 1-inch (not too small) cubes 6lbs 5 lbs zucchini, cut 4x by length and 1” cubes [optional] 1 6 lb cans <=(less ~ 1.5 cups) chopped tomato w/liquid (have another med. can in reserve if needed) ½ tsp ¼ tsp cayenne (more to taste if needed, not too hot for yogis) 6 quarts water + ¾ jar broth paste 4 qts 2 cups water + ½ jar broth paste broth: mix 3 quarts of hot tea-urn water with all the veggie broth paste, then use the rest of the water cold as needed. 9 bunches 7 bu kale (stems removed) and roughly chopped 4 cups 3 cups peanuts separated in half. half will go in whole into the stew and half will be chopped and added for garnish salt and pepper to taste week 2 day 1 recipe: peanut stew page 2 of 2 instructions note: will thicken once kale is added. cook chickpeas these should have been soaked overnight or “quick soaked” by km earlier. drain soaking water, rinse, cover with fresh water. add ~3 bay leaves & bring to a boil, reduce to simmer. let them cook while you get the rest of the stew ready, checking occasionally for done. saute saute onion until translucent. add garlic & ginger and saute another minute. add remaining ingredients in steps add yams, tomato, peanut butter, cayenne, & veggie broth (as needed). bring to boil and lower to a simmer. cook until sweet potatoes are tender. 11:15 add zucchini and drained chickpeas about 11:30, add kale & half the whole peanuts. check seasoning. garnish with rest of chopped (or whole) peanuts to serve.

title: Pinto Beans
text: all recipes / side pinto beans tags: vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free, nut-free, soy-free day 2 recipe: pinto beans page 1 of 2 equipment 20 qt stock pot for the beans, large skillet for the onions. ingredients ~50 with supper ~50 with no supper increased quantities 8/2019: use the left column unless you have a very small retreat ~30, or you are not wanting any leftovers for a supper casserole. it’s a popular leftover for rvs. [qty] [ingredient description] 5 qts 3.5qts pinto beans [pre-soaked, rinse soaked beans] 9 qts 7qts fresh water 4 tbls 3 tbls salt 4 3 bay leaves oil as needed to coat the pan 4 ½ lbs 3lbs onions,medium chopped 25 cloves 20 cloves garlic 5 cans 3 cans tomato paste (mix with ½ cup water to aid in mixing if helpful) 6t 4t whole cumin 4 ½ t 3t oregano 2 t 1 1/2t chili powder ¾ t ½ t cayenne pepper (add gradually and taste, heat varies) 3 t 2t brown sugar 20oz (=5 sm cans) 12oz (=3 sm cans) green chiles –look at can size, may vary, go by oz more salt to taste? recipe: pinto beans page 2 of 2 instructions prepare and start beans rinse the soaked beans. put beans, salt and fresh water in stockpot. bring to a boil and skim off any foam. when done skimming, add bay leaves. turn down to a vigorous simmer..check frequently to be sure it is still simmering actively and has adequate liquid. prep other ingredients chop garlic in mini-cuis toast & grind cumin saute other ingredients in the large skillet or small brazier, sauté the onions. when they are translucent, add the garlic. stir tomato paste with 1/2c. water and add to the onion mix, simmer 10 minutes. add all the other seasonings (cumin, oregano, chili powder, brown sugar,salt). simmer another 10 minutes stirring frequently. combine and finish scrape the onion & spice mix into the bean pot. put a heat deflector under the bean pot!! let it continue to simmer, checking and adding water as needed to make a good burrito filling consistency (not too soupy, not too thick to burn). about 11:45: add the green chilies, check taste & add salt as needed serve with slotted spoons if still watery.

title: Polenta
text: all recipes / side polenta tags: vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free, nut-free, soy-free day 3 recipe: polenta page 1 of 2 equipment if supper: 3 full pans. serve the 2 and save the other for supper. if no supper, just 2 full size. use the 4” (medium depth) so it doesn’t slosh when putting in the oven. ingredients: note: simplified to be all vegan no-cheese, serve cheese on the side for the whole meal. note: if making 3 pans: we only have 2 4” deep full pans, so use 2 4” half pans or a 6” deep one for the third and save the 3rd for supper leftover. per full pan: ask km how many pans: usually 2 if no supper or supper “minestrone” soup is planned, 3 if supper casserole is planned. [only 1 for group of ~36 with no supper use] 5 cups polenta 20 cups = 5 qts water with bouillon (3 t bouillon paste mixed with 1 quart of hot tea-urn water per pan), other 4 quarts water cold. (1 t) (the bouillon is salty, probably don’t need this…taste at the end) 2 t olive oil 2 t dried basil 1 t white pepper ½ c?? optional: nutritional yeast (quantity needs to be verified..) ~ ¼ cup per pan optional: earth balance (stir in at the end if using) instructions (see p2 for stove-top version instructions) mix and bake polenta preheat oven to 425. spray pans with spray oil. mix polenta and seasonings in each of the pans you are using. leave pans uncovered and put them in the oven about 10:15. set a timer for an hour. stir & maybe cover about 11:15, carefully with hot pad gloves (and maybe with help) remove the pans and stir. peek every 20 minutes or so. if top is getting too brown, put the lid on. if done, turn off ovens and leave pans inside to stay warm. maybe stir in some earth balance at the end. day 3 alternate: stovetop polenta page 2 of 2 alternate versions preferred by some cooks (from lael) this stovetop version is good and does free up the oven so that you can pre-roast more of the ratatouille veggies, which improves that dish. but this takes some attention. bring 10 quarts water to boil (get this going early, ~10:45?). be sure a heat deflector is under the pot! add ⅓ cup salt about 11:20: slowly pour 10 cups polenta into pot whisking constantly to avoid lumps. keep whisking while it thickens. when thickened, turn down flame to a bare simmer. stir every 10 minus for 40 minutes. this long simmer brings out the sweet corn flavor. add more boiling (tea machine) water if too stiff. stir in some earthbalance (any brand vegan butter) to taste. note on possible use of leftovers for the next night supper: if there is quite a bit left (~4 qts?), best to do this right after lunch, during the put-away period): grease sheet pan with olive oil. spread the polenta on the sheet pan to ~½-¾” thick. ¾ of a sheet pan is enough. sprinkle with basil and vegan parmesan and put the sheet in the fridge (maybe with foil or another sheet pan covering it). at 5:00 on supper day: put in a 400 oven for the half-hour. cut into ~7x8 pieces. you could probably do this with oven polenta but it’s harder to spread.

title: Portuguese Kale White Bean Soup
text: all recipes / soup portuguese kale white bean soup tags: vegetarian, gluten-free, nut-free, soy-free week 2 day 4 recipe: portuguese kale white bean soup (adapted from moosewood restaurant favorites) (p. 1 of 3) equipment 32qt (largest) stock pot with pot-saver under it, zester, juicer, spice grinder, mini cuisinart (& separate 12 qt pot to give beans a head-start) prep ahead: soak 2qts dry cannellini beans overnight, or quick soak in am, or use ~ 7 x 28oz canned (not as good, gets mushy). ingredients ~48 (14-15qts) ~36 (~11 qts) (this gets eaten, no leftover meal expected) whole lg jar ¾ jar sun dried tomatoes (whole 32-34oz jar jar of oil-packed), drained, reserve oil for saute if needed if needed olive oil (if needed to supplement sun-dried tomato oil for saute) 4lbs 3 lbs onions, ½” dice 2lbs 1 ½ lbs carrots, ½ “ dice ~4-6 bulbs 4 bulbs fresh fennel bulbs (quantity depends on size), ½ “ dice 4lbs 3 lbs potatoes (ideally yukon gold), ½ “ dice 14 cloves 11 cloves garlic, chopped in mini-cuisinart 4 ½ tbls 3 ¼ tbls fennel seeds, very lightly toasted and ground 4 ½ tbls 3 ¼ tbls thyme 2 ½ tsp 1 ¾ tsp salt & to taste at end 1 ¼ tsp 1 ¾ tsp pepper & to taste at end 7 qts water + 1 jar btb 5 qts + 1 cup water + ¾ jar btb better than bouillon dissolved in 1qt hot tea water + 6qts (or 4 qts 1 cup) cold water (can use the bean cooking water, not the soaking water) 1 lg (+ 1 med) 1 lg canned diced tomatoes (i.e. 1 6lb6oz + 1 28oz) 2 qts dry 1 ½ qts dry cannellini (white) beans (or ~6-7 28oz cans) week 2 day 4 recipe: portuguese kale white bean soup (p. 2 of 3) ingredients (continued) 5 bunches 4 bunches kale, torn into pieces (very roughly 2”x2” sized) ~1 cup (=~8) ~¾ cup (=~6) lemons, juiced ...save some zest in case needed //add to taste instructions cook beans note: km will have pre-soaked the beans. rinse soaked beans. in a separate 12 qt pot: cover with fresh water, bring to boil and right away turn to a low simmer, skim if needed, toss in a stalk of fresh rosemary. add to main soup pot about 10:30. locate & prepare ingredients strain off the oil from the oil packed sun-dried tomatoes saving the oil, and use it to saute the onions in step below. set aside tomatoes. when beans are done, use bean broth and/or water as needed to make bouillon with better than bouillon. dice onions, carrots, fresh fennel, potatoes (usually veggie choppers). kale: remove thick stem from center, tear into large bite sized pieced wash lemons zest 1-2 lemons (=scrape off the thin outermost yellow layer of skin) using either the microplane (sharp!) or box grater (suggest wearing the cut-resistant glove for either). set aside in case needed at the end. juice lemons using juicer (near rice cooker). lightly toast the fennel seeds dry in small skillet. grind using spice grinder. chop garlic in mini cuisinart on chop setting (best if thawed) week 2 day 4 recipe: portuguese kale white bean soup (p. 3 of 3) sauté be sure heat-saver disk (on stove shelf) is placed under stock pot using the reserved sun-dried tomato oil if you have it, or else olive oil, sauté the onions until they are getting soft. add in chopped garlic and 2 tsp salt. saute another minute add the ground fennel and diced fennel and cook for ~10 minutes. stir in the carrots, potatoes, thyme, sun-dried tomatoes and black pepper and cook for ~20 minutes. combine & cook soup about 10:30: add tomatoes, bouillon and beans. stir well, bring to a boil and reduce to simmer. be sure there is a pot-saver/heat disperser under the pot. simmer until potatoes are just tender. add greens about 11:30, stir in the kale. final seasoning stir in (some) lemon juice & zest to taste and salt to taste. serve with a large bowl of parmesan

title: Quick Mushroom Gravy
text: all recipes / side quick mushroom gravy tags: vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free, nut-free week 3 day 3 recipe: quick mushroom onion gravy page 1 of 2 equipment 2 largest skillets, 10qt stock pot or largest of the small pots ingredients 48 with supper leftovers 48 with no supper leftovers or 36 w/supper olive oil, as needed 2lbs 1 ½ lbs onions chopped 2lbs 1 ½ lbs regular white or brown mushrooms, sliced 4.5 qts 3.5 qts stock: cups of water as shown + 1tsp btbouillon “no-chicken” per cup. (avoid mushroom btb, it has soy ingredients) 2 tbls 1 ½ tbls sage (double if using fresh) 2 tbls 1 ½ tbls thyme (double if using fresh) 5 tbls ?? 4 tbls ?? tamari less? to taste–the bouillon is quite salty!! 4 tbls 3 tbls sherry vinegar 2 tsp 1 ½ tsp black pepper if needed if needed salt (taste after adding tamari…really doubt this is needed) ¾ cups ½ cup corn starch dissolved in cold water..may need more. (qty shown is of the corn starch, use enough cold water to dissolve well, about equal quantity water: cornstarch). recipe: mushroom onion gravy page 2 of 2 instructions: brown mushrooms & onions use the 2 largest skillets and brown mushrooms and onions at the same time. cook the mushrooms at least until all the water is gone. ideally get the onions a bit browned, but at least very soft. when done, you could “deglaze” the pans: put a cup or so of stock water in the pans and stir it up to capture the flavored oil and caramelized bits, pour it back into the stock pot. stock mix the bouillon and water until dissolved (for ~1qt of the water, use some hot tea-urn water to dissolve the bouillon). add rest add all other ingredients except cornstarch. thicken mix cornstarch with enough cold water to dissolve it. add to the gravy. bring to a boil for 3-5 minutes until it thickens. return to simmer. taste and adjust seasoning if needed.

title: Quinoa
text: all recipes / side quinoa tags: vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free, nut-free, soy-free day 1 recipe: quinoa page 1 of 1 equipment large strainer, rice cooker clean rice cooker if needed ingredients #48 (lunch only) 10 cups quinoa (note we sometimes have red, sometimes white quinoa, use what you can find and prefer) 12 ½ cups water (ratio of q:w we use is 1:1 ¼) instructions ~ 10:30: rinse the quinoa very thoroughly or it has a bitter taste, using the large double-mesh strainer and running your fingers through them (may take several batches). put the rinsed grains into the rice cooker (not turned on). they can sit there rinsed until it’s time to add the water and cook. just before 11:00: add water (as above) in the ratio of 1 ¼ cups of water for each cup of quinoa. 11:00: plug in and turn on the cooker. it will take about 45mins to cook, then it switches to warm. set a timer to check when it should be done. let it sit for a few minutes, then carefully open the lid and fluff it with a wood or plastic tool . if there is time, cover the pot with 2-3 clean white towels and gently set the lid back down. this will absorb excess moisture and help the quinoa be fluffier. you must unplug the machine to turn off the “warming”. serve with wooden spoons so as not to scratch the container

title: Ratatouille
text: all recipes / side ratatouille tags: vegetarian, gluten-free, nut-free, soy-free day 3 recipe: ratatouille page 1 of 3 equipment large rondo pan with lid, 2-3 lg baking sheets, small stock pot ingredients 50 servings with supper leftovers and more! 50 servings no supper leftovers note: lgr qty won’t fit in the rondo, good to save some for supper in any case: for middle or left column: move ~6-8qts to to a small stock pot and set aside for supper soup base (see p. 3 instructions for where to do this) 8 7 globe eggplant, cubed to 1” cubes coat rondo coat rondo olive oil (and some spray) 5lbs 3 onions 6lbs 5lbs mushrooms, chunks (eg quartered) 20 14 garlic 2 6lb cans =7 28oz 1 6lb + 1 28oz =4.5 28oz diced tomatoes (note: 1 6lb can = ~3.5 28oz cans) 3 6oz cans 1 ½ cans tomato paste 5t 3t basil 5t 3t thyme (& maybe ~4 t fresh oregano from garden?) 5t 3t fennel seeds, toasted and ground 1 cup ¾ c chopped parsley 15 12 red/yellow/orange bell peppers, 1” chunks 4 bulbs 3 bulbs fresh fennel bulbs, ~1” dice 13lbs 10 lbs zucchini, ~ 1” chunks to taste to taste salt & pepper to taste (est ~1t salt at least) 1 bunch ¾ bu fresh basil garnish, washed & slivered recipe: ratatouille page 2 of 3 instructions roast eggplant & maybe fennel set the oven to 375. (you can put eggplant (and fennel) in as soon as ready, no need to wait for pre-heat) (eggplant should be set up on large baking sheets spread in a single layer.) spray the paper with olive oil spray. optionally, do the same with the fresh fennel (or it can just be added in with mushrooms). roast the eggplant (& fennel) cubes for about 30 minutes, stirring once. set aside. you may also roast the peppers and even the zucchini if you have time and oven space. (while it roasts, get the polenta ready for the oven..other recipe). prep chop the garlic in the mini-cuis (chops better when thawed) lightly toast 4 t fennel seeds in small skillet watching closely, grind in spice grinder (wipe or brush out spice grinder before and after..) sauté coat the rondo with olive oil to about 1/8” and sauté the onion. when the onions gets translucent, add mushrooms (& fresh fennel if using, whether pre-roasted or not). saute until they soften. add the tomato paste to the onions & sauté a couple of minutes add the garlic and sauté briefly. option: drain the tomatoes, saving the liquid to add in as needed or for future use in left-overs casserole. add the tomatoes, dried herbs and parsley. let the sauce simmer for ~15 minutes recipe: ratatouille page 3 of 3 instructions continued add vegetables add the zucchini and eggplant //here is where you should shift some off into a side stock-pot both for space and to save for supper. if andrea fella is teaching: set aside a no-pepper version for her (incl. enough for leftovers if having): could: add some celery or extra fennel if we have it to her version instead of bell-peppers add bell-peppers to main version put a heat deflector under the rondo pan!! the stew can simmer anywhere from 45-90 minutes, stir often. maybe cover if not too juicy. prep sides, season, garnish wash and cut the basil leaves into thin strips. set-up a side bowl of parmesan cheese. about 30 minutes before serving time, check that the vegetables are all soft and taste the seasoning. add more herbs if needed, salt and pepper to taste. garnish with the slivered fresh basil if using. serve in the rondo pot.

title: Red Lentil Dal
text: all recipes / entree red lentil dal tags: vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free, nut-free, soy-free recipe: red lentil dal equipment 32 oz stockpot (largest one) note: to ease this day, you may want to prepare the spice mix during the work period or even sometime the day before. ingredients #servings with supper leftovers #servings no supper leftovers [qty] [qty] [ingredient description] 4 ½ qts red lentils (d1:c3) 9 qts water (add more if needed) 1 cup chopped ginger up to 2 qts baked yams, mashed (optional, if available or use 29 oz can of pumpkin puree 5 lbs diced onions 15 cloves minced in cuisinart garlic spice mix (shared by 2 dishes): cumin seed 6 ½ t, toasted & ground coriander seed 6 ½ t, toasted & ground fenugreek seeds 1 ½ t, toasted & ground turmeric 4 ½ t brown mustard seeds 5 ½ t 1/2t cayenne pepper (add more if needed) 3-4 juice of lemons salt to taste recipe: red lentil dal instructions start lentils simmering rinse the lentils in the strainer under running water. tends to clump, separate with your fingers. this may take several batches in the strainer. put lentils & water in the stock pot. bring to a boil and skim off foam. after foam is skimmed off, lower heat, add chopped ginger and cubed yams. reduce to an active simmer. check frequently that it is still actively simmering, but not over-boiling and stir often all the way to the bottom. always put a heat-deflector under this pot . to stir, you may want to stand on a stool and use the big paddle. if it seems to be getting too thick, you can add more water. it should be thick, but still pourable. while it simmers, prepare the yams, spices & garlic check if there are leftover yams, peel and mash if not already done, or get out a can of pumpkin puree (or skip this if none). chop the garlic in the mini-cuisinart. toast the cumin, coriander and fenugreek. use the small skillet, keep the heat low and wait for it to start to be fragrant and a little brown, but not very (& not burned!). grind them (you may grind together) in the spice grinder. add tumeric and brown mustard seeds set aside 4 t of the mix to add to the cauliflower. stir and check lentils frequently, this dish is easy to burn! recipe: red lentil dal instructions continued... sauté onions & spices use the large skillet, coat it lightly (~ 1/8”) with canola oil. sauté the onions over med/low heat until soft. add the garlic and sauté another minute. add the spice mix and cayenne and continue to sauté over low heat for 1-2 minutes. set aside if not time to add to the dal. stir and check lentils frequently, this dish is easy to burn! blend the lentils, add the remaining ingredients when the lentils are soft (maybe ~11:15), add the yams or pumpkin. using the immersion blender, blend the dal to a smooth consistency, being careful not to submerge the blender beyond the stem, and using a spoon to stir up the dal from the bottom. add the onion/spice mixture to the dal, stirring well. cook for about 5 minutes and then add the lemon juice & maybe zest to taste, stirring well. salt to taste. when it’s ready you can put a lid on it and leave it turned off, it will stay warm.

title: Roast Brussels Sprouts
text: all recipes / side roast brussels sprouts tags: vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free, nut-free, soy-free roast brussels sprouts page 1 of 1 equipment 2 large baking sheets ingredients: #servings with no supper leftovers 25lbs brussels sprouts, cut in half lengthwise unless tiny salt & pepper olive oil instructions preheat oven to 400 toss in large bowl with oil, salt & pepper to taste. spread out on large baking sheets (no parchment). put most of them face down if cut in half. put tray in oven, check & stir every 20 mins. probably takes about 45 minutes. done when tender and nicely browning.

title: Roast Butternut Squash
text: all recipes / side roast butternut squash tags: vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free, nut-free, soy-free recipe: roasted butternut squash equipment large baking sheets (est 3-4) ingredients: #servings 1 case butternut squash (peeling left on, seeds removed, cut into big pieces, typically 4 pcs out of the round end, 2-4 pcs out of the thinner end of each). for smaller retreat, just do it all, have more for soup later. oil to coat instructions: preheat oven to 400 (or ok to put in not pre-heated) oil each piece if not done already roast ~2 hours (allow the whole morning, can be unpredictable, ok to serve at room temp if done early), test doneness with a fork, should be very soft, browning lightly.

title: Roast Squash
text: all recipes / side roast squash tags: vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free, nut-free, soy-free roast squash page 1 of 2 equipment 4 large baking sheets ingredients: #servings with supper leftovers #servings no supper leftovers 30lbs 25lbs mixed yellow squash and zucchini 5 onions 4 onions red onion, slivered salt olive oil instructions preheat oven to 400 veggie choppers/km will leave squash cut up and salted in a colander to drain over a bowl. lunch cook should thoroughly rinse salt off the squash. using white towel(s), pat dry in batches and put into a large bowl. add in slivered red onion if using. toss with olive oil. spread out on baking sheets (no parchment). if making along with cornbread, we will cook in two batches to free up half the oven for later and serve with half at room-temp, half hot. put tray in oven, check & stir every 20 mins. probably takes about 40 minutes. done when soft and nicely browning.

title: Roasted Butternut Squash
text: all recipes / side roasted butternut squash tags: vegetarian, gluten-free, nut-free, soy-free week 2 day 4 recipe: roasted butternut squash equipment large baking trays ingredients: butternut squash peel left on, chunked ~6-8 pcs per squash, optional olive oil mixed herbs (optional, good to keep this plain for diets and maybe make herbal or maple butters) optional: rub large pieces of squash with olive oil, sprinkle tops with mixed herbs (avoid garlic for diets, good to keep this plain and make maple butter as below) place pieces on large baking trays. bake at 375 for 1 ½ to 2 hours total (allow for even more). done when quite soft and slightly brown. ok to turn off oven and leave them in there if done early. serve with regular and non-dairy butter. or for an extra treat: make maple butter: in robo or min-cuis mix butter, maple syrup and maybe nutmeg to taste, make a version with vegan butter.

title: Roasted Cabbage with Fennel
text: all recipes / side roasted cabbage with fennel tags: vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free, nut-free, soy-free week 2 day 1 recipe: roasted cabbage with orange & fennel page 1 of 1 equipment : large bowl, 4 large baking sheets ingredients 48 servings with supper lo 36 servings w/supper lo [qty] [ingredient description] 8 heads 6 heads cabbage (regular white/green), cored and cut into wedges as needed olive oil 4 tbls 3 tbls fennel seed 2 2 oranges juiced and zested instructions preheat oven to 400. toss cabbage wedges with olive oil in large bowl. we aren’t trying to keep the wedges together, let it all fall apart and get covered in oil. spread onto large baking sheets with parchment. sprinkle with fennel. put in oven about 11:00 and start checking about 11:45. done when lightly browning on the edges. transfer to a large bowl to serve. toss with orange juice and zest. lightly salt to taste.

title: Roasted Cubed Tofu
text: all recipes / entree roasted cubed tofu tags: vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free, nut-free week 2 day 5 recipe: roasted cubed tofu page 1 of 1 equipment huge salad bowl to toss, maybe smaller one to serve ingredients (sauce quantities approximate, use your judgement) 48 servings 36 servs 9lbs 7lbs cubed extra firm (or firm) tofu as needed light olive oil ?⅓ cup rice vinegar ?½ cup tamari small amt sesame oil ?½ cup white sesame seeds (optional) instructions mix oil, vinegar, tamari, sesame oil toss cubed tofu in mixture spread on parchment on large baking trays roast at 350 for ?40 mins? check every 15 mins or so, turn when brown on bottom sprinkle with sesame seeds & serve in a large bowl

title: Roasted Root Vegetables
text: all recipes / side roasted root vegetables tags: vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free, nut-free, soy-free day 6 (or alt 5) recipe: roasted root vegetables page 1 of 1 equipment large baking sheets, large mixing bowl ingredients serves ~50 10lbs beets, 1” cubed 10lbs yams, 1” cubed 2lbs carrots, 1” chunked (sometimes more of above and no carrots) **actually any mix of these vegetables, weights are a suggestion, should total about 22 lbs to lightly coat olive oil, either use bowl and toss or use spray instructions preheat (probably both) ovens to 400. toss each kind of vegetables separately with enough olive oil to lightly coat. consider chopping up and adding some rosemary from the garden! line as many baking sheets as needed with parchment paper (probably already set up by veggie choppers). spread the oiled vegetables among the number of sheets needed to keep them only 1 level deep and keep vegetable types separate in case they are done at different times. veggies go in ~10:45. stir and turn every half hour. done when tender and starting to caramelize. as they are done, transfer to a metal bowl and serve.

title: Roasted Zucchini Carrots and Corn
text: all recipes / side roasted zucchini carrots and corn tags: vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free, nut-free, soy-free day 2 recipe: roasted zucchini, carrots and corn page 1 of 2 equipment 3 full sized baking sheets or a mix of large and small to fit. ingredients 50# servings with supper leftovers 50# servings no supper leftovers or 35 w/sup [qty] [qty] [ingredient description] 17lbs 12lbs zucchini ½ case=11lbs + 6 (or 1) extra lbs 12lbs 10lbs carrots olive oil spray 3lbs 2lbs frozen corn recipe: roasted carrots, zucchini and corn page 2 of 2 instructions note: you may not be able to fit all the zucchini on sheets, if not, steam the extras and save them for the supper casserole. preheat both ovens to 375. line the pans used for the carrots with parchment paper. don’t line the pans for the zucchini. if veggie choppers already put on trays, spray with spray olive oil, or else hand mix with oil in bowls and then spread on trays. the carrots benefit from extra long cooking, the corn gets added last, so try this timing (with help from a timer): 10:40 put the carrots in 11:00 put the zucchini in and stir the carrots 11:30 stir both & pour the corn over top of all pans, return to oven. (11:40 you will be putting tortillas in the oven about here…you may have to combine veggies into fewer pans to make room–lower oven temp for tortillas when veggies done) 11:45 check for doneness. the zucchini and carrots should be softened (not mushy but easy to fork through) and beginning to brown slightly when done, empty them all in a 4” hotel pan and mix.

title: Slaw Salad
text: all recipes / salad slaw salad tags: vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free week 2 day 5 recipe: slaw salad page 1 of 1 equipment huge salad bowl to toss, maybe smaller one to serve ingredients 48 servings 36 servs 4 lg hds 3 lg hds white cabbage and/or napa cabbage 1 med hd ¾ med hd red cabbage 1 ½ lb 1 ¼ lb carrot shredded ~2 cups ~1 ½ cup chopped mint (try left side kitchen garden, or bought) if needed baby spinach (to fill the bowl & lighten it up) 1 recipe slaw dressing: consult km --options that work from salad dressings file: peanut lime is best if no peanut allergies, or save some out undressed or use sesame ginger (good with lime version), ginger miso 3lbs? 2 lbs peanuts (serve on the side) (~1 lg white serving bowl worth) instructions thinly shred all cabbage (if napa by hand, white & purple using the wider blade in the robo). (this does get eaten up & shrinks if pre-dressed, so pile it up & do use all 5 cabbages even if it’s looking like a lot in the smaller salad bowl.) use shredded carrots we have or do some more wash and chop mint toss altogether with spinach if using to fill a salad bowl. maybe save some out undressed, dress the rest. tip: mix in huge salad bowl over the pan rack, move to smaller to serve serve with bowl of peanuts on the side

title: Soup Cornbread Sides
text: all recipes / side soup cornbread sides tags: vegetarian, gluten-free, nut-free, soy-free soup & cornbread sides equipment med. & small bowls ingredients 3 16 oz containers sour cream in 2 white oval bowls ~3lbs shredded cheddar in 2 white oval bowls or one large serving bowl (eg blue one) 4 bunches cilantro chopped (if on hand) in small/medium bowl butter & earthbal for cornbread

title: Steamed Broccoli W2
text: all recipes / side steamed broccoli w2 tags: vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free, nut-free, soy-free recipe: steamed broccoli equipment 2-6” hotel pans, 2 steamer pans, 2 lids we’re doing a whole case, so you may need to do 2 rounds, it can all be finished a bit early, anytime from 11:30 onward or so and be served room temperature if needed. setup 2 steamer assemblies: get the two 6” deep (deepest) solid pans and fill them with 2” of water. set the water filled pans across 2 burners each. divide in the 2 perforated pans as much broccoli as will fit with the lid fully closed set the perforated pans in the water filled pans and put a lid on each instructions turn on both burners. let the broccoli steam for about 5 minutes after the water comes to a boil. carefully lift the lid and check on it. when it looks done, remove the perforated pans from the base pans and empty the broccoli into a large metal serving bowl. refill one or both pans with any remaining broccoli and steam for just 2-3 minutes (we may use some of these for further baking, so leave barely done). leave the pans on the counter (out of the water) so we can serve more if needed.

title: Steamed Broccoli
text: all recipes / side steamed broccoli tags: vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free, nut-free, soy-free day 6 recipe: steamed broccoli page 1 of 1 equipment 2-6” hotel pans, 2 steamer pans, 2 lids you may need to wash the steamer pans used for the tempeh to reuse for the broccoli, or maybe the veggie choppers have set it up already. we’re doing a whole case, so you may need to do 2 rounds, it can all be finished a bit early, anytime from 11:30 onward or so and be served room temperature if needed. setup 2 steamer assemblies: get the two 6” deep (deepest) solid pans and fill them with 2” of water. set the water filled pans across 2 burners each. divide in the 2 perforated pans as much broccoli as will fit with the lid fully closed set the perforated pans in the water filled pans and put a lid on each instructions turn on both burners. let the broccoli steam for about 5 minutes after the water comes to a boil. carefully lift the lid and check on it. when it looks done, remove the perforated pans from the base pans and empty the broccoli into a large metal serving bowl. refill one or both pans with any remaining broccoli and steam for just 2-3 minutes (we may use some of these for further baking, so leave barely done). leave the pans on the counter (out of the water) so we can serve more if needed.

title: Steamed or Roasted Green Beans
text: all recipes / side steamed or roasted green beans tags: vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free, nut-free, soy-free alt day 6 recipe: roasted or steamed green beans page 1 of 1 should be 13 lbs of green beans …if there are a lot more than that, they are intended for another upcoming meal (eg chicken tofu) roasted (actually steamed a bit first..): equipment: 2 large baking trays, foil toss beans in olive oil, sprinkle with salt and maybe pepper. heat oven to 350 these will need to be done early to have time for the tempeh to use the oven. they can be served room temp. we found it best to “steam” them for 20-30 minutes first by covering the trays of beans with foil, when almost soft enough to eat, remove the foil and roast for another ~10 mins until slightly browning. or simple steamed: equipment steamer pan setup (either 1 re-used for 2 batches or 2 setups) you may need to wash the steamer pans used for the tempeh to reuse for the beans. these can be done anytime and served either warm or room temp. steam the beans for ??20 minutes until they are as soft as you like them. be sure to check that the water doesn’t all boil off.

title: Supper Bean Casserole Or Soup
text: all recipes / entree supper bean casserole or soup tags: vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free, nut-free, soy-free day 3 supper recipe: bean casserole or soup pg. 1 of 1 equipment: lg mixing bowl, 2 2” full-sized hotel pans with lids, or 20qt soup pot the idea: improvise casseroles or soup out of leftover tortilla bar ingredients. ingredients (potential ingredients, use what we have & be creative) for casserole: leftover rice (&maybe quinoa and/or corn tortillas torn up. need only a thin layer of grain (maybe 3 qts total). leftover pinto beans (if less than 4 qts, open some cans of black beans to have this much) leftover veggies of any kind (add more frozen corn or frozen green beans to make at least 3qts veggies) leftover salsa, or open another jar if needed to make it moist and tasty could spice up if needed with salt, pepper, ground cumin, garlic powder etc. (usually only needed if you used a lot of new plain ingredients). for soup: any/all of the above, but very light on the rice or quinoa & tortillas. add bouillon to bring to a soup consistency. could add more canned tomatoes, but probably not needed. aim for 14-18 quarts, depending on the size, age & appetite of the group. instructions casserole suggestion: layer the casseroles with a light layer of rice and tortillas on the bottom, then mix together then beans, vegs & rest. a layer of torn up tortillas works well as a topping (we don’t put cheese on top anymore, only serve on the side). soup: add all beans & veg to soup pot, thin with bouillon (1 tsp btb to 1 cup water), thicken with a little rice or torn up tortillas if wanted. serve either version with cheese & vegan cheese, cilantro if we have enough.

title: Supper Black Bean Soup with Veg
text: all recipes / soup supper black bean soup with veg tags: vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free, nut-free, soy-free day 6 supper recipe: black bean soup w/ corn and tomato equipment: largest soup pot (to stay warm) ingredients: leftover black bean soup with corn & tomato instructions add as needed to make ~16qts: add your leftovers to the soup pot. augment as needed to have ~16qts adding: canned tomatoes frozen corn, up to 5 packs makes it interesting better than bouillon always put thick soups on a flame disperser and stir often but lightly if bottom is getting burned, don’t scrape it up. bring to a full boil (or 180), turn off fire, put lid on, the big pots will stay warm until 5:00. probably best to save any leftover chips for the final snack.

title: Supper Dal Soup or Casserole
text: all recipes / soup supper dal soup or casserole tags: vegetarian, gluten-free, nut-free, soy-free day 5 supper recipe: dal soup or casserole soup: use largest 32 qt stock pot, making ~15-16 qts soup ingredients what you have leftover curried cauliflower (if you made plain steamed, look at the curry recipe and add some of those spices and some frozen peas) ~4qts leftover dal ~3 med cans tomatoes with juice 1 lg can coconut milk broth water + bouillon paste as needed to make total ~15-16 qts of soup 1-2 qts leftover rice instructions: mix it all up, bring to a boil, taste, turn off, cover and should keep hot for the afternoon. serve with sides of leftover raita or yogurt, and leftover chutney or raisins. casserole: fill two 2” deep hotel pans at least half full casserole ingredients for ~48 leftover dal (~ 4-5 quarts..if less than this, add a can of white or garbanzo beans. leftover cauliflower and peas (add more frozen peas if short). mix veggies with 2 small cans of coconut milk. leftover rice (~ 4-5 quarts, if short, make some more on the stove) if you added a lot of new unseasoned stuff, stir in 1-2 tsp curry powder. instructions: layer food into the 2 pans: rice, veggies, dal. serve with sides of leftover raita or yogurt, and leftover chutney or raisins.

title: Supper Miso Soup
text: all recipes / soup supper miso soup tags: vegan, dairy-free, nut-free day 6 supper recipe: miso soup page 1 of 1 equipment: 20qt stock pot //or 32qt if 20qt will be used for noodles ingredients for ~48 1 sheet kombu (if we have any) 10 sheet pack nori, cut into squares ~2” 3lbs tofu, diced small (½”) (if no extra in fridge, use aseptic if any) 3.5 cups miso (ideally red, or whatever we have) (3.5 cups = ~1 ¾ tubs) ⅓ cup tamari 13 quarts water 3lbs carrots, small dice 8 bunches chopped scallions including ~⅔ of the green part 5lbs mushrooms, thick slices (maybe pre-sautéd if time) supper recipe: miso soup instructions in the morning: add all but 1 qt of water + kombu sheet and simmer ~an hour. remove kombu. add nori, mushrooms & carrots. mix miso with another quart of water, prep scallions & tofu. put these in fridge for later. at 5:00 add in tofu, tamari, miso/water. ~5:25 just before serving, add scallions.

title: Supper Moroccan Soup
text: all recipes / soup supper moroccan soup tags: vegetarian, gluten-free, nut-free, soy-free alt week 2 day 7 supper recipe: moroccan soup equipment : 2 soup warmers, & 32 qt stock pot ingredients left over morroccan chickpea stew, any quinoa pilaf leftover extend to make ~14-16 quarts. add as needed: red lentils (up to ~6 cups??) water mixed with some bouillon paste maybe some more of the spices from the moroccan stew recipe note: if there is almost nothing to start with: see the recipe for moroccan red lentil soup under simple soups file. instructions make the soup on the stove in the large stock pot if it is thick and at 175 degrees by lunch time, should stay warm all afternoon with fire off and lid on. if very watery, might not, so transfer to soup warmers (under toasters). set up a lg bowl of greek or regular yogurt for a side.

title: Supper Peanut Casserole
text: all recipes / entree supper peanut casserole tags: vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free, soy-free supper recipe: african peanut casserole equipment: 2 2” hotel pans with domed lids (on top of pan rack) the idea: improvise casseroles out of leftover african peanut stew, roast cabbage if any, rice. ingredients (in this case, potential ingredients, use what we have & be creative) for ~48 min ~3-4 qts leftover rice, make some on stove top if not enough min ~6-8 qts leftover african peanut stew--add some canned chickpeas if not enough optional any leftover roasted cabbage instructions you may want to layer the casseroles with grain on the bottom, then the stew and cabbage, or mix it all up. fill the 2 pans evenly with the mix and cover them with domed lids, label them and put them in the fridge. check that serving signs list the ingredients you wind up using.

title: Supper Rata Minestrone Soup
text: all recipes / soup supper rata minestrone soup tags: vegetarian, gluten-free, nut-free, soy-free day 4 supper recipe: supper minestrone soup equipment: 2nd largest stock pot (the one with the pasta insert?) & soup warmers? ingredients: leftover ratatouille and extras casseroles: first: if andrea fella is teaching & there are leftovers for her, maybe make a med. glass bowl of leftover polenta + her no-bell-pepper ratatouille for her to microwave (don’t put in oven) if enough leftovers: make ~18 quarts soup with leftover ratatouille (hopefully ~8qts left), adding better than bouillon broth, any/all of the following as needed: more canned tomatoes (1-2 28oz cans?) sometimes there are “extra” zucchini’s prepped for the rata more garlic leftover white beans &/or ~2 28oz cans white beans or garbanzos ?frozen green beans (1-2 packs) more “italian” herbs from ratatouille recipe if we have gf pasta: pre-make it, rinse & cool it. add cooked pasta just before serving in the evening. when hot: when it’s done, or just before lunch, transfer to soup warmers for the afternoon. at 5:00pm: if prepared: add pre-cooked & cooled gluten-free pasta. setup cheese: setup a bowl of parmesan and “white” vegan cheese on the side.

title: Supper Shepards Pie
text: all recipes / entree supper shepards pie tags: vegetarian, nut-free supper recipe: shepard’s pie equipment : 2 2” deep full sized hotel pans with lids ingredients left over mashed potatoes, chicken-fried tofu, green beans, gravy optional supplements: frozen or other leftover veggies if needed, bouillon if needed, rice, cans of white beans to supplement tofu? if there isn’t enough left to make something tasty out of, first: check freezer for suitable leftovers to use, or make a simple soup out of what we have or can run out & get ingredients for. instructions spray pans layer “as you like it”. simple suggestion: crumble tofu & mix with veggies & gravy, top with mashed potatoes option: making a smaller dish with no cheese and sprinkling maybe parmesan on top to give it some browning & more flavor.

title: Supper Tofu Spread
text: all recipes / side supper tofu spread tags: vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free, nut-free supper: tofu spread ingredients: tofu 6lbs veganaise 2c celery, fine dice 4c tumeric 2t dijon mustard ½ cup…more to taste tamari ½ cup …more to taste nut. yeast 6t parsley 1 bu dill and/or taragon 1 bu each scallions, chopped 3 bu salt 1 t (start with less, add more to taste) pepper 1 t (start with less, add more to taste cayenne ½ t (start with less, add more to taste) corn cakes 8 packs instructions: crumble the tofu to the texture of crumbled eggs... chop celery & scallions wash & chop the parsley, dill, taragon. add the other ingredients and mix. taste for salt, pepper, seasoning. refrigerate until serving time. serve with corn cakes in a towel lined basket.

title: SW Black Bean Stew Soup
text: all recipes / soup sw black bean stew soup tags: vegetarian, gluten-free, nut-free, soy-free southwestern black bean stew page 1 of 2 equipment 32qt (largest) stock pot, maybe 2nd stock pot for excess, mini cuisinart for ~50 with supper leftovers: ¼ less (for ~36 w/ supper) note: the left-column make a lot, intended for 2 meals for 50 as needed olive oil for saute 6 lbs 4.5 llbs chopped yellow onion, med dice 12 stalks 9 stalks celery, small dice 2x6lb cans 1 lg 2 med tomatoes with liquid ½ cup 4.5 t cumin (either whole lightly toasted & ground or preground) ½ cup 4.5 t oregano 2t 1 ¾ t paprika 1t ¾ t chili powder 5bls 4 lb green bell peppers, small dice 5lbs 4 lb mixed red/yellow/orange bell peppers, small dice 7 lbs 5-6 lbs zucchini, ½ “ dice (in 4ths (6ths if huge) lengthwise, then ½” chunks) 5x28oz cans 4 cans black beans (use liquid) 4 bags 3 bags frozen corn 9 4oz cans 7 4oz cans hatch green chilies ~4-6 qts ~4.5 qts water as needed (should be a fairly dense soup) black bean stew/soup page 2 of 2 instructions saute heat olive oil in stock pot and add onions. saute until translucent. add ingredients add celery, chili powder, oregano, and cumin, paprika to saute mixture and cook for a few minutes. add tomatoes, bring to a boil and lower to a simmer. simmer for at least half an hour. add peppers, zucchini, beans and water as needed to make the quantity desired. bring to boil, simmer until time for last step. **consider separating out some into a smaller stock pot as a guarantee of leftovers, and because this gets very full.. finish add corn & green chilies about 20 mins before serving. add salt as needed. serve with cheddar, cilantro & sour cream.

title: Tempeh Ruebens and Fixings
text: all recipes / entree tempeh ruebens and fixings tags: vegetarian, nut-free alt day 6 recipe: tempeh ruebens and fixings page 1 of 3 equipment 2 lg baking sheets for tempeh, pitcher or bowl to mix sauce ingredients #servings (no planned leftovers) note: 10/2025 removed steaming step, experiments showed not needed. 15 8oz packs tempeh, sliced 4 per pack (see km instructions, am yogi does this) note: case = 12 packs, so case + 3 extra ¾ c. light olive oil ¼ c. sesame oil 2 c. tamari 2 c. rice vinegar 4 c. water 3 packs swiss cheese, pieces cut in half maybe: sunshine burgers for no-soy people (put out sign pointing to freezer, they can microwave them) alt day 6 recipe: tempeh ruebens and fixings page 2 of 3 instructions set-up and prep preheat both ovens to 350. slice each package in half across the center, then each half piece through the thickness dimension to make two thin patties. that is, if the half-piece is ~½ “ thick rectangle, the resulting patties will be ¼” thick rectangles. tip: maybe use 2 white scrapers to hold the piece safely on its side (the km will demonstrate, probably the morning yogi will do it) mix marinade & start on prepping sides mix the marinade: lite olive oil, sesame oil, rice vin. & tamari & water. handy to use a large plastic pitcher. layout the slices in the flat on the baking sheets, not overlapping. pour the marinade over the slices. put the pans in the ovens about 10:45. continue working on sides & the veg. after about half an hour (~11:15), turn over all the tempehs. add water or more marinade if it is getting dry. we are now serving the cheese on the side, see “fixings” page. alt day 6 recipe: tempeh rueben fixings page 3 of 3 ingredients #servings with supper leftovers #servings no supper leftovers see note==> rye bread..3 loaves of bread =60 slices usually serves a full house. for smaller group, figure ~ 1 ½ slices per wheat-eater. 1 ½ slices per non wheat eater gf bread 4-24 ounce jars sauerkraut , drained russian dressing “recipe”: veganaise 32oz ketchup 6 t horseradish 2 t 1 jar dijon mustard 3 packs swiss cheese, sliced in half, arrange on a dinner plate ~6 bags chips (assuming 5oz terra chip bags) instructions set-up sides make the russian (just mix the veganaise, ketchup and horseradish—see ingredients list). setup sauerkraut (drain), mustard (serve in the jar), chips, cheese layout the rye bread on the large baking sheets, overlapping the pieces so it fits on maybe 1 full and 1 half-sized baking sheet. don’t cover it so that it more toasts than steams. put in in about 11:30 and check it frequently.

title: Thai Yellow Curry W2
text: all recipes / entree thai yellow curry w2 tags: neither, gluten-free, dairy-free, nut-free, soy-free week 2 day 5 recipe: thai yellow curry page 1 of 2 equipment rondo + 10-12 qt stockpot ingredients 48 servings with supper leftovers 48 servings no supper leftovers or ~36 w/supper ¼ cup as needed canola or coconut oil 4 lbs 3 bls onion thinly sliced ½ cup 6 tbls ginger minced 20 cloves 15 cloves garlic minced ¾ cup 9 tbls thai curry paste (maeploy brand yellow is what we use) 2 t 1 ½ t turmeric ~30-35 lbs ~23-28 lbs mixed vegetables, for example (but use whatever you have): 5lbs 4 lbs yams cubed 7ea 5 ea cauliflower 7ea 5-6 ea eggplant, cubed 6lbs 5 lbs zucchini,cubed 5lbs 3 lbs yukon potatoes note: avoid using bell peppers if andrea is teaching 9 lbs 7 lbs extra firm tofu, cut into in ¾” cubes cooked & served separately, see other recipe 3 6 lb cans 2 lg + 1 sm coconut milk week 2 day 5 recipe: thai curry page 2 of 2 instructions (if you wish: see note at the bottom from thina for a better? version) ***note: this full recipe is enough for a full rondo plus ~8-10 qts in one of the smaller stock-pots. it works to get down to the *** step below in the rondo, then separate out the 2 quantities and proportionally divide up any additional vegetables. then you can set aside the other pot to use for the leftover supper. pre-roast eggplant & maybe others if using eggplant, pre-roast it to lose bitterness & help it absorb sauce better. if room in the oven, it’s tasty to pre-roast some other hard veggies like cauliflower, carrots, zucchini, yams (not broccoli). roast tofu see separate recipe, we usually serve this separately, both for diets and for table interest. saute spices add oil to rondo, heat to medium/high and add onions and saute until translucent. add garlic, ginger, curry paste and turmeric and cook for a minute or two until fragrant. taste sauce & adjust spices if needed. add veggies once onions and spice mix is ready, add coconut milk. try not to let it fully boil once you add the coconut, it will separate (still edible if it does, but not ideal). add veggies hardest first, tenderest last, something like: ~10:30 raw carrots, yams, squash, potatoes, peppers, zucchini, roasted eggplant (*** see above) ~11:40 raw cauliflower and/or other pre-roasted veggies ~11:50 raw broccoli if having any thina recommends: use only 1 big coco milk and maybe 2 small cans. and 1 jar better than bouillon. use 1 small can coco as oil to melt the curry paste (don’t worry about oil separating). then you can add all hard veggies, including onions, and add rest of coco milk and better than bouillon and then rest of softer veggies. i only roasted the eggplants. and you can have whatever veggies you wish. when veggies are cooked, it’s good to go!

title: Vegan Cornbread
text: all recipes / side vegan cornbread tags: vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free, nut-free recipe: vegan gf cornbread pg 1 of 2 equipment 4 half-sized 2” hotel pans (cooks more evenly than 2 full size), 2 large mixing bowls, 2 small mixing bowls ingredients for ~48-50 1 ⅓ cup vegan egg replacer (in pantry baking box?) note: bob’s v-egg has soy, the other “ener-g” box brand doesn’t or ground flax seed (in freezer?) 4 cups warm water for flax or vegan egg 7 ½ cups rice milk (or alternative milk of choice, check allergies) ¾ cup + 1 t apple cider vinegar 10 ⅔ cups gluten-free flour 10 ⅔ cups bob’s medium grind cornmeal (check pantries for ~32oz bags of this, can use polenta if none, the med. grind makes it lighter) 3 t + 1 ½ tsp salt ½ cup+1 ½ t baking powder 4 ¾ tsp baking soda 2 ⅔ cups canola oil 2 ⅔ cups pumpkin pulp (canned/boxed) 2 ⅔ cups sweetener: maple syrup, honey, or sugar (check with km to accommodate any dietary restrictions) alt recipe: vegan cornbread pg 2 of 2 instructions heat oven to 375 degrees. grease pans. mix v-egg or ground flax and warm water separately, let set for 5-10 minutes to thicken (will need to whisk the v-egg). mix alternative milk of choice and vinegar and let set while preparing other ingredients. in a large mixing bowl, mix dry ingredients: corn meal, gf flour, baking powder, baking soda and salt in one bowl. in a separate mixing bowl, mix together oil, pumpkin, sweetener, “milk” mixture, flax mixture. leave wets and drys separate until just ready to go in oven. mix just until combined, be careful not to overmix. place mixture into 4 half-sized 2 inch-deep hotel pans (stored on the island near pantry door). bake for 40-50 min? or until golden brown and cooked in the center. test by patting for firmness & toothpick or knife comes out clean. start checking after 30 mins.
