title: White Bean Side
text: all recipes / side white bean side tags: vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free, nut-free, soy-free day 3 recipe: white beans with rosemary for side page 1 of 1 equipment 12 or 16 qt stock pot ingredients: assume km soaked the dry beans...if not, either try quick soak method during veggie chop/first sit period or use canned (or instant pot if you know how) for ~50 for no left or ~36 with lo this idea is to offer this as a vegan “condiment” to add to the ratatouille and then mix any leftovers into the supper casserole. 2.5 qts dry 1 ¾ qts dry cannellini beans 4 fresh sprigs rosemary from the garden = 2 to cook with, 2 for garnish ~ ¼ cup olive oil 1 t 2t salt instructions for dry beans: start first thing (9:30): strain off soaking water. cover with fresh water. toss in 2 rosemary stalks. bring to a boil, reduce to simmer. cook until soft. strain into a serving bowl. remove rosemary, toss with olive oil. garnish with fresh rosemary stalk. for canned beans: same as above, but only cook long enough to reheat, don’t over cook. could start about 11:00. for instant pot not tested cover with water, add oil & rosemary. if pre-soaked, pressure cook on high for ~7mins, if not, ~50 mins.

title: Red Pepper Dressing Notes from Max Swanger
text: all recipes / salad red pepper dressing notes from max swanger tags: vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free, nut-free, soy-free red pepper dressing notes from max swanger the red pepper dressing is using the jars of roasted peppers i got. put them in vitamix (drain and split them in two batches) add red wine vinegar-blend-drissle in olive oil and season to taste with salt and pepper. usually about 1:3 in terms of vinegar to oil… like maybe try 3/4 c vinegar to 2 1/4 cup oil per batch-should work. you can probably put it all in there at once and it will prob. still emulsify…start with 1tsp each salt/pepper that’s what i was going to do.

title: Rosemary-Chocolate Chip Cookies
text: all recipes / dessert rosemary-chocolate chip cookies tags: vegan, dairy-free rosemary­chocolate chip cookies (makes 15 cookies) ● ½ c refined coconut oil softened (not melted) ● 2 t loosely packed rosemary chopped fresh ● ⅓ c brown sugar ● ¼ c sugar ● ¼ c non­dairy mylk ● 1 t ground flaxseed ● 2 tsp vanilla ● 1 ⅓ c flour ● ½ tsp salt ● ½ tsp baking soda ● ½ c chocolate chips 1.heat oven to 350 2.beat together coconut oil and rosemary then add sugars and beat well. 3.add mylk and flaxseed and beat again for 30 seconds or so. 4.add about half of the flour and remaining dry ingredients, mix well. 5.scoop about 2 t portions of cookie dough and gently flatten on cookie sheet. 6.bake 10­12 minutes until bottoms are golden brown.

title: Saag Paneer
text: all recipes / entree saag paneer tags: vegetarian, gluten-free, nut-free, soy-free saag refers to an indian vegetable dish in which spinach or other dark greens are stewed with ginger, garlic, fresh chiles and spices until meltingly soft. as the name suggests, saag paneer includes paneer, a mild indian cheese that is firm enough to cook without melting. the heat of the serrano chiles balances the creamy richness, but for a milder dish, remove the seeds before mincing the chiles. the fresh greens are finely chopped before cooking, to help them break down faster into a silky gravy. thawed chopped frozen spinach can be used to save time, but make sure to drain well and squeeze out the excess liquid first. finish the dish with a little heavy cream (or plain yogurt) to lend body and richness. serve with steamed rice and/or indian flatbread (such as naan). any leftovers can be refrigerated for up to 2 days. yield: 4 servings ingredients 1 pound fresh baby spinach (about 8 packed cups) 2 tablespoons ghee 8 ounces paneer, cut into 1-by-½-inch pieces ½ cup finely chopped yellow onion kosher salt and black pepper 1 tablespoon freshly grated peeled ginger (from a 2-inch piece) 2 teaspoons grated garlic (from about 3 cloves) 1 serrano chile, stemmed and minced ½ teaspoon ground coriander ¼ teaspoon ground cumin ½ cup heavy cream steamed rice and/or indian flatbread, for serving preparation in a food processor, working in batches, pulse spinach until minced but not puréed. do not pack the spinach too tightly or it won't get evenly chopped. you should have about 3 packed cups of minced spinach. heat 1 tablespoon ghee over medium in a large nonstick skillet. when it shimmers, add paneer and cook, turning occasionally, until golden all over, 5 to 7 minutes. using tongs or a fish spatula, transfer cheese to a plate, leaving as much ghee as possible in the skillet. reduce heat to medium-low, add the remaining 1 tablespoon ghee and the onion, and season with salt and pepper. cook, stirring occasionally, until softened but not browned, about 5 minutes. add ginger, garlic and chile, and cook, stirring occasionally, until fragrant and well incorporated, 1 minute. stir in coriander and cumin until well blended. add minced spinach and ½ cup water, and increase the heat to medium. season with salt and pepper and cook, stirring occasionally, until spinach is completely soft and most of the liquid is absorbed, about 8 minutes. stir in heavy cream and paneer until well incorporated. season with salt and pepper. transfer to a serving bowl. divide rice and/or flatbread among 4 shallow bowls or plates. pass the saag paneer to spoon on top.

title: Salad to go with Thai Cauliflower Soup
text: all recipes / salad salad to go with thai cauliflower soup tags: vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free salad to go with thai cauliflower soup (option for first full day supper, instead of greek salad bar) 1 (or ~½ of large one) red cabbage: shred or manually thinly slice 1 napa cabbage: thinly sliced 2lbs frozen green beans: steam until thawed 2 cups of chopped mint leaves (either bought or from the garden outside the kitchen door) ~2 cups shredded carrots optional: see if we bought some mung bean sprouts (the fat white kind) optional: see if we bought some extra bell peppers. (make sure you leave 15 for the ratatouille meal.) mix all the above with enough baby kale to fill the medium salad bowl. maybe mix it in the giant one and serve in the medium. make 1 batch of peanut lime dressing below, set up in 2 small pitchers. set up and serve as sides: 2 bunches cilantro, 2lbs of peanuts for peanut lime dressing: 2 ¼ c peanut butter 2 c water // more if needed if too thick 1 ¾ c lime juice (10-12 limes) & zest of 4 limes //ok to top off with lemons if you can’t get enough lime juice from the limes ¾ c rice vinegar 3 t sesame oil ½ c agave // maybe more, taste it at the end ½ c tamari //maybe less if not low-sodium? 6 cloves garlic //the vitamix will mince it 1 t roughly chopped ginger //the vitamix will mince it 1 ½ c light olive oil mix pb & water in a bowl to thin. add that & all but oil to the vitamix, mix. drizzle in oil while mixing.

title: Salted Choc Chip Cookies Vegan GF
text: all recipes / dessert salted choc chip cookies vegan gf tags: vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free, nut-free, soy-free salted chocolate chip cookies (vegan, gf) note: for best texture, make dough day before & fridge overnight yield: approximately 60 (18) cookies usually get 5x6 each on 2 lg baking sheets = 60 3.5x (1x orig in parens) 7c (2) cups bob’s (or trader joe’s) 1-1 gf is preferred brand 3 ½ t (1) tsp. baking powder 2 ½ t (3/4) tsp. baking soda 1 ¾ t (1/2) tsp. salt 4 ¼ c (1 ¼) cup dark choc chips (= 2 bags, more is fine too) ----- 1 ¾ c (1/2) cup sugar 1 ¾ c (1/2) cup (packed) light brown sugar 2c (1/2 cup + 1 tablespoon) canola or lite olive oil 1c + ½ t (1/4 cup + 1 tablespoon) water ----- sea salt for garnish in a large bowl, whisk together flour, baking powder, baking soda, and salt. add the chocolate chips to the flour mixture and toss to coat. in a separate large bowl, whisk [best to use electric hand mixer] the sugars briskly with the oil and water until smooth and incorporated, about 2 minutes. note: use fresh, soft light brown sugar. if there are clumps, break them up with the back of a spoon or your hand before whisking. add the flour mixture to the sugar mixture, and then stir with a wooden spoon or a rubber spatula until just combined and no flour is visible. do not overmix. cover with plastic wrap. b refrigerate the dough for at least 12 hours and up to a day or two. preheat the oven to 350°. line a rimmed sheet pan with parchment paper. remove dough from the refrigerator and use clean bare/gloved hands] to portion dough into 2-inch mounds. for a size guide: try to get 8x5=40 per full sized sheet pan or 4x5 = 20 per half pan. do: partially flatten each ball with fingers or fork (they don’t spread out much at all). tip: use a white plastic scraper to make clear rows between cookies. sprinkle the balls of dough (very lightly!) with coarse-grained sea salt , and bake for 15-20 minutes, or until the edges are golden. best to use only the top rack of the oven, or watch the bottom rack very carefully, it will burn easily. //check starting at about 12 mins, our ovens are variable in behavior. let cool completely before lifting off the pans to serve. from vogue.com excerpted from ovenly by agatha kulaga and erin patinkin (harlequin). copyright © 2014. photographs by winona barton-ballentine. we love to experiment with our base recipes. this dough is incredibly versatile and easy to work with. try adding in fresh herbs or spices, substituting flavored oils, or dress them up by sandwiching some buttercream in between two cookies and offer them as party favors. you can get creative and try these combinations or create your own! here are some of our favorite variations: *substitute the chocolate chips with flaked coconut and toasted almonds, and add in ¼ teaspoon almond extract to the oil/water mixture. *instead of canola oil, use half hazelnut oil and half safflower oil and add dark chocolate pieces instead of chocolate chips. *mix one tablespoon of ground cinnamon into the flour mixture, and add milk chocolate chips and currants. *prepare your favorite buttercream recipe and add in ¼ cup bourbon (or even champagne). mix until smooth and sandwich in between two cookies to make cookie sandwiches.

title: Sesame Ginger Dressing
text: all recipes / salad sesame ginger dressing tags: vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free, nut-free sesame ginger dressing page 1 of 1 equipment: vitamix, bowl ingredients for a pre-tossed salad for 48 as a pre-tossed salad, either the supper noodle or rice, or a slaw. double these quantities for a self-serve dressing. 1 ¼ c lime juice+zest of 2-3 limes, or rice vinegar or mixture 1 tbls grated ginger (good to use the microplane) ½ cup ginger, chopped in mini-cuisinart 6 tbls tamari 3 tbls agave 3 tbls sesame oil 6 cloves garlic, minced in mini-cuis or 1 ½ tsp garlic powder 2tbls siracha sauce ¼ cup toasted white sesame seeds (& more in salad, see above) ½ to 1tbls salt (add ½ t & see...probably need more in final salad) 2 cups light olive oil instructions: blend all but oil in vitamix. drizzle in oil & blend again.

title: Sherry Shallot Vinaigrette FOG
text: all recipes / salad sherry shallot vinaigrette fog tags: vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free, nut-free, soy-free sherry shallot vinaigrette 1 ½ qt 1 ½ cup sherry vinegar 12 shallots 1 t dijon mustard 2 ¼ cup olive oil 2 ¼ cup canola oil 1 t salt ½ t white pepper thinly slice the shallots sauté the shallots in some of the olive oil. put vinegar, mustard, seasonings in the blender and blend. add the shallots with their oil and just pulse it a couple of times (we don’t want the shallots totally liquified..) transfer to a larger container and whisk in the rest of the oils. taste (drizzle a little into a separate spoon) and adjust salt, pepper or mustard. for one meal: fill 2 small pitchers. serve with smallest ladles.

title: Sherry Shallot Vinaigrette Salad Dressing
text: all recipes / salad sherry shallot vinaigrette salad dressing tags: vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free, nut-free, soy-free recipe: sherry shallot vinaigrette salad dressing equipment vitamix, ~4qt plastic container & whisk, 2 pitchers ingredients for 1 batch (~48 servs) 1 ½ cup sherry vinegar 2 very large shallots (like small onions..check onion area if we have any) 2 t dijon mustard 2 ¼ cups olive oil 2 ¼ cups light olive oil 1 tsp salt ½ tsp white pepper instructions remove outer papery skin & thinly slice the shallots sauté the shallots in some of the olive oil. put vinegar, mustard, seasonings in the blender and blend. drizzle rest of oil into the running vitamix and blend well. add the shallots with their oil and just pulse it a couple of times (we don’t want the shallots totally liquified..) taste and adjust salt & pepper if needed. divide between 2 small pitchers. cover & store in fridge (if not for today, label and date also).

title: Simple Miso Soup
text: all recipes / soup simple miso soup tags: vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free, nut-free simple miso soup (maybe offer on last night with noodle salad) ..from rachel 15 sheets nori cut in large squares 3.5 cups miso 3.5 cups cubed tofu 7 cups chopped scallions heat 15 quarts of water to a low simmer. add 15 sheets of nori cut into large squares. simmer for 5 minutes add 3.5 cups of white miso ( blended with some hot water to avoid clumping) add 3.5 cups of extra firm tofu. ( i used the silken tofu from the yogi fridge, so there should have been 11 left in the main fridge for the next retreat) simmer for another 5 minutes. before serving. add finely chopped scallions.... i used what we had left from the produce order. the recipe says 7 cups. pretty sure i had about half that.

title: Smoked Paprika Dressing
text: all recipes / salad smoked paprika dressing tags: vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free, nut-free, soy-free recipe: smoked paprika vinaigrette equipment vitamix, juicer, 2 pitchers ingredients for 1 batch (~48 servs) 2 ½ cups red wine vinegar 1 cup agave ¼ cup dijon mustard ¼ cup lime juice 2 t smoked paprika 2 t oregano 2 cloves garlic ½ cup chopped shallot 3 cup olive oil 1 t pepper 1 t salt instructions juice limes in juicer next to rice cooker add all ingredients except oil in vitamix container and mix on low. drizzle oil into vitamix mixing while you do. gradually increase speed until all emulsified. divide between 2 small pitchers. cover & store in fridge (if not for today, label and date also).

title: Spiced Chickpea Stew Turmeric Coconut
text: all recipes / entree spiced chickpea stew turmeric coconut tags: vegetarian, gluten-free, dairy-free, nut-free, soy-free spiced chickpea stew with coconut and turmeric by alison roman time 55 minutes rating (20313) michael graydon & nikole herriott for the new york times. prop stylist: kalen kaminski. spiced chickpeas are crisped in olive oil, then simmered in a garlicky coconut milk for an insanely creamy, basically-good-for-you stew that evokes stews found in south india and parts of the caribbean. while the chickpeas alone would be good as a side dish, they are further simmered with stock, bolstered with dark, leafy greens of your choosing and finished with a handful of fresh mint. when shopping, be sure to avoid low-fat coconut milk, coconut milk meant for drinking or cream of coconut: all are very different and would not be suitable here. orig ingredients (see below for irc qts) yield: 4 to 6 servings 1⁄4 cup olive oil, plus more for serving 4 garlic cloves, chopped 1 large yellow onion, chopped 1 (2-inch) piece ginger, finely chopped kosher salt and black pepper 11⁄2 teaspoons ground turmeric, plus more for serving 1 teaspoon red-pepper flakes, plus more for serving 2 (15-ounce) cans chickpeas, drained and rinsed 2 (15-ounce) cans full-fat coconut milk 2 cups vegetable or chicken stock 1 bunch swiss chard, kale or collard greens, stems removed, torn into bite-size pieces 1 cup mint leaves, for serving yogurt, for serving (optional) toasted pita, lavash or other flatbread, for serving (optional) preparation step 1 heat 1⁄4 cup oil in a large pot over medium. add garlic, onion and ginger. season with salt and pepper, and cook, stirring occasionally until onion is translucent and starts to brown a little at the edges, 3 to 5 minutes. step 2 add 11⁄2 teaspoons turmeric, 1 teaspoon red-pepper flakes, and the chickpeas, and season with salt and pepper. cook, stirring frequently, so the chickpeas sizzle and fry a bit in the spices and oil, until they’ve started to break down and get a little browned and crisp, 8 to 10 minutes. remove about a cup of chickpeas and set aside for garnish. step 3 using a wooden spoon or spatula, further crush the remaining chickpeas slightly to release their starchy insides. (this will help thicken the stew.) add coconut milk and stock, and season with salt and pepper. step 4 bring to a simmer, scraping up any bits that have formed on the bottom of the pot. cook, stirring occasionally, until stew has thickened, 30 to 35 minutes. (taste a chickpea or two, not just the liquid, to make sure they have simmered long enough to be as delicious as possible.) if after 30 to 35 minutes, you want the stew a bit thicker, keep simmering until you've reached your desired consistency. determining perfect stew thickness is a personal journey! step 5 add greens and stir, making sure they’re submerged in the liquid. cook until they wilt and soften, 3 to 7 minutes, depending on what you’re using. (swiss chard and spinach will wilt and soften much faster than kale or collard greens.) season again with salt and pepper. step 6 divide among bowls and top with mint, reserved chickpeas, a sprinkle of red-pepper flakes and a good drizzle of olive oil. serve alongside yogurt and toasted pita if using; dust the yogurt with turmeric if you'd like. had very little left for 48, might want to up to 9x orig x8 32-48? maybe a little more on the chicks & broth rr ptional) pick up 2 qts some greek?

title: Spinach Mushroom Lasagna
text: all recipes / entree spinach mushroom lasagna tags: vegetarian, nut-free, soy-free spinach mushroom lasagna equip: 2 hotel pans @24 each (cut 6x4), plus an 8x8 no-dairy-gf alt. ingredients: 5lbs (half case) mushrooms cut chunky 4lbs onions, med. dice 20cl garlic, chopped in chopper as needed bottled pasta sauce (note how much we use..) to make 8 qts sauce (3c is for alt) 10 x10oz frozen spin bags (2 is for alt version) 5x32oz ricotta 4 tubs tj goat = 2cups 8 eggs, beaten 2t nutmeg 4c bread crumbs (2c for topping, maybe 2c for cheese mix) 8c shredded mozzarella 4c parmesan for alt version: maybe soy cheese? 2 lemons 1t nutmeg 1 box gf noodles 3lbs firm tofu (and will use some sauce & spinach as noted above) lasagna instructions: be sure spinach is out to thaw early. saute onions, garlic & mushrooms w/ 2t salt. cook till liquid is mostly gone. mix with bottled pasta sauce to amount to ~7.5qts total (put mushr mix in 8qt container and open sauce bottles to fill). we might use some plain pasta sauce for the bottom layers.. strain, press spinach (maybe with gloves, wring it out). set aside 1cup for alt version. make cheese mix: ricotta + goat + nutmeg + beaten eggs + squeezed dry spinach, maybe add 1-2 c. breadcrumbs (leave 2 cups total for topping). make alt filling: blend tofu, lemon juice, nutmeg & mix with spinach. mix 4c parmesan, 2c moz, 2c bread crumbs for topping. preboil gf noodles? maybe: setup a ramekin of cheese & sauce for no-soy no-gluten person? layer as described on back side → layers for 1 hotel pan //consider using 4” deep just to have no spillover… 2c sauce //maybe use plain sauce for this w/out chunky mushrooms 7 ½ sheets tjs lasagna noodles 5c cheese/spin mix 3 c sauce 3c mozzarella 7 ½ sheets tjs lasagna noodles 5c cheese/spin mix 3c sauce 7 ½ sheets tjs lasagna noodles 3 c sauce topping (~4cups per pan) layers for alt: (need 6-7 servings?) ½ c. sauce sheets gf noodles ½ alt filling 1 c. sauce soy cheese layer? noodles ½ alt filling 1 c. sauce soy cheese layer?

title: Split Pea Soup
text: all recipes / soup split pea soup tags: vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free, nut-free, soy-free supper recipe: split pea soup p 1 of 2 equipment: largest 32qt soup pot ingredients for ~48-52 for saute olive oil 8 cups onions, chopped 7 cups celery diced (~½” dice) 9 cups carrots, diced (~½ “ dice) 2 tsp salt 4 bay leaves 1 ½ t smoked paprika (maybe more later, but start easy on this) 3 t marjoram 3 t turmeric 2 t ground cumin ¾ tsp cayenne pepper (maybe more later, but start easy on this) 12 cups yellow or green split peas, rinsed 11 quarts water (mixed with a jar of better than bouillon) 1 ¼ cup lemon juice 1 bunch parsley, chopped opening supper recipe: yellow split pea soup p 2 of 2 instructions saute saute onions over medium heat until softened add carrots & celery, saute over medium heat (~30 mins) add tumeric, cayenne, marjoram, smoked paprika, salt saute ~5 more minutes add peas & broth mix 2 qts hot water (use tea water) with a jar of better than bouillon vegan “chicken” broth add peas, bouillon mix and the other 9qts of water bring to boil, reduce to simmer. simmer an hour or more until peas are soft & creamy. taste and maybe adjust seasonings. if needed: puree partially with immersion blender (leave some chunks of carrots/celery). 12:00 leave soup @ ~180 but burner turned off, should stay hot. 5:15 finish stir in lemon juice and parsley and adjust seasonings (esp. probably add more salt). adapted from vegetarian times december 2013

title: Steamed Broccoli
text: all recipes / side steamed broccoli tags: vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free, nut-free, soy-free alt week 2 day 7 recipe: steamed broccoli page 1 of 1 equipment 2-6” hotel pans, 2 steamer pans, 2 lids you may need to wash the steamer pans used for the tempeh to reuse for the broccoli, or maybe the veggie choppers have set it up already. we’re doing a whole case, so you may need to do 2 rounds, it can all be finished a bit early, anytime from 11:30 onward or so and be served room temperature if needed. setup 2 steamer assemblies: get the two 6” deep (deepest) solid pans and fill them with 2” of water. set the water filled pans across 2 burners each. divide in the 2 perforated pans as much broccoli as will fit with the lid fully closed set the perforated pans in the water filled pans and put a lid on each instructions turn on both burners. let the broccoli steam for about 5 minutes after the water comes to a boil. carefully lift the lid and check on it. when it looks done, remove the perforated pans from the base pans and empty the broccoli into a large metal serving bowl. refill one or both pans with any remaining broccoli and steam for just 2-3 minutes (we may use some of these for further baking, so leave barely done). leave the pans on the counter (out of the water) so we can serve more if needed.

title: Artichoke Hummus
text: all recipes / side artichoke hummus tags: vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free, nut-free, soy-free week 2 day 1 (optional) supper recipe: artichoke hummus page 1 of 1 equipment : large bowl, robo coupe, large ceramic serving bowl, leftover container if making the double size. ingredients 8cups=typical last day snack only (blue bowl) 16 cups=for a supper with leftovers you will need to make this in 2or 4 batches to fit in the robo coupe, so add some of each item to each batch as you go and hand mix the batches. 1 lg (48oz) jar 2 lg (~48oz) jars artichoke hearts, drained, maybe save 2-3 small pieces for garnish 1/2 cup=4 lems 1 cup=8 lems lemon juice (number of lemons estimated) 1 cup 2 cups water ¾ cup 1 ½ cups tahini ½ cup 1 cup ev olive oil 2x28oz 4x28oz cans of chickpeas 8 cloves 16 cloves garlic ¼ tsp ½ tsp cayenne ?2-3 tsp? ?4-6 tsps? salt to taste as needed for garnish: either artichoke pieces, or parsley or nasturtium instructions 2 batches 4 batches assemble the robo coupe with the clear bowl and blade. add roughly proportional parts of each ingredient to make each batch. blend using pulse at first, then leave on “on” for a full minute or so to get smooth consistency. mix all the batches. serve in a large ceramic bowl with garnish.

title: Beans, greens and mushrrom soup
text: all recipes / soup beans, greens and mushrrom soup tags: vegetarian supper recipe: bean, greens, and mushroom soup equipment: largest pot ingredients for ~48 leftover bean dish from previous day 10-12 quarts veggie broth herbs? additions? instructions empty ingredients into large pot and bring to boil. place into soup warmers and keep at 165 degrees until dinner.

title: Black Bean Soup Supper
text: all recipes / soup black bean soup supper tags: vegetarian, gluten-free, nut-free, soy-free week 2 day 3 supper recipe: leftover black bean soup w/ corn & tomato equipment: largest soup pot (to stay warm) ingredients: leftover black bean soup with corn & tomato instructions for soup: add your leftovers to the soup pot. augment as needed to have ~16qts (or less if lots of 8 precepts) adding: canned tomatoes frozen corn, up to 5 packs makes it interesting better than bouillon always put thick soups on a flame disperser and stir often but lightly if bottom is getting burned, don’t scrape it up. bring to a full boil (or 180), turn off fire, put lid on, the big pots will stay warm until 5:00. do not serve with chips, they are reserved for other meals. sides: set up what’s available of sour creams, or cheddar cheese, cilantro.

title: Butternut Soup
text: all recipes / soup butternut soup tags: vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free, nut-free, soy-free supper recipe: butternut soup p 1 of 2 equipment: ?20qt soup pot (largest is ideal, but probably being used for lunch) ingredients for ~48 for ~36 however much <== leftover roasted butternut squash, peeled 15-20lbs 12-15 lbs pre-cubed butternut squash (whatever was ordered) ~4lbs 3 lbs white or gold potatoes, cubed for saute for saute olive oil 3 lbs 2 ¼ lbs onions, chopped 10 cloves 8 cloves garlic chopped 1 jar btb in ~8 qts water ¾ jar btb in ~6 qts water better than bouillon vegan chicken broth mix this up and add as needed to make desired qty of soup (maybe 14 qts or 11 qts for smaller) 3 tbls 2 ½ tbls dried thyme 1 cup ¾ cup chopped parsley 2 lemons 1 ½ lemon lemon juice & zest (add to taste) 2 tsp 1 ½ tsp black pepper (add to taste) 2 tsp 1 ½ tsp salt (add to taste, probably need more!) supper recipe: butternut soup p 2 of 2 instructions saute saute onions until transparent, add garlic briefly simmer add butternuts & potatoes, thyme and stock bring to boil & reduce to simmer when partly done, add parsley finish add lemon, salt, pepper to taste about noon: cover & turn off fire. test that it is 165. should hold at ~145-165 till supper. check it at 5 and maybe reheat. or you could transfer to the soup warmers & keep those on low all afternoon.

title: Carrot Ginger Soup
text: all recipes / soup carrot ginger soup tags: vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free, nut-free, soy-free supper recipe: carrot ginger soup equipment ingredients for ~48 ½ cup olive oil 4 cups onions chopped 15 lbs carrot 1 large can coconut milk 6-8 quarts vegetable broth 4-6 inches ginger minced in cuisinart (more if desired) instructions saute onions in a large pot saute onions in olive oil until tender. add ingredients add remaining ingredients, bring to a boil and then down to a simmer and cook until butternut squash is easily pierced with a fork. 20-30 min. emulsify using an emulsifying blender blend, blend until smooth. season with salt and pepper.

title: Cauliflower Soup
text: all recipes / soup cauliflower soup tags: vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free, nut-free, soy-free day 1 supper recipe: cauliflower soup pg 1 of 2 this is usually prepped on opening day but served at first full day supper. best idea is to get it all prepped on opening day, then cook it on opening day when the big 32 qt pot is available and it will keep hot all afternoon. note: there are 2 flavors of this: original (rather plain) and thai. we usually serve the original with a spinach/greek salad bar and the thai with a slaw (see those recipes). we rarely do this now, especially the slaw, we don’t usually have the extra ingredients unless pre-arranged with produce orderer. ingredients for ~48 1 case minus 2 heads cauliflower cut into pieces (save the extra 2 heads for the dal day later in the week) use 8lg or 10 med heads (varies by size how many is in a case). 4lbs 4 lbs yellow potatoes, cubed (optional if don’t have) 18 cloves garlic (chopped in mini cuis) 4lbs onions chopped 8 quarts water 1 jar veggie bouillon (more ingredients next page..) day 1 supper recipe: cauliflower soup pg 2 of 2 do one or the other of these: for original: 2 lemons zest of lemon and juice of one lemon (maybe more..) 3 tbls dijon mustard ½ bunch parsley ½ cup olive oil for thai version: check we have the extra ingredients 1 cup chopped ginger (chopped in the mini-cuisinart) //leave 1lb for later ⅓ cup thai yellow curry paste (mae ploy tub: look in top of kitchen fridge for open one or pantry for new) 4 limes juice and zest (optional if don’t have) //leave 14 for later 3 bu cilantro rough chopped including stems (on the side) instructions saute saute onions until soft, add garlic & saute a minute or so with ~2tsp salt. if doing thai version : add the ginger here. add main ingredients add cauliflower, (potatoes), water, and bouillon and cook until tender. salt and pepper to taste finish blend with immersion blender and finish with rest of flavors of your choice. setup cilantro for a side.

title: Leftover Lentil Salad
text: all recipes / salad leftover lentil salad tags: vegetarian, gluten-free, soy-free week 2 day 1 supper recipe: leftover lentils & greek salad page 1 of 1 equipment : large bowl ingredients 48 servings 16 cups what there is left: leftovers (serve combined or not, however you like): lentil grape salad (consider if you had a no-nut version, make a no-nut supper version also). roasted yams, beets, carrots quinoa what else is refreshing: set up elements of the greek salad bar from wk1 day 1, eg: spinach kalamata olives pumpkin seeds tomatoes feta cheese maybe cucumbers (probably skip the chickpeas if you have lentil salad left) whatever dressing is left? greek lemon or balsamic are good.

title: Loaded Nachos
text: all recipes / entree loaded nachos tags: vegetarian, gluten-free, nut-free, soy-free week 2 day 5 supper recipe: loaded nachos equipment 2 lg baking sheets + 1 half-sheet for no cheese ingredients for ~50 for ~36 typical: for 50 2 lg dairy, ½ vegan; for 36 1 ½ d, ½ v 1 ½ bags 1 bag tortilla chips (costco’s giant 48-serving bags) 6 qts 4 qts canned black beans, maybe leftover burgers etc. ~2.5 lbs ~2 lbs shredded cheddar, vegan cheddar (1 bag) ~2 qts 1 ½ qts slicedblack olives (= 1 red bag of costco), strained 8 sm cans 6 sm cans green chilies, strained ~2 jars ~1 ½ salsa (no need to open early, just set out jars) 8 bunches 6 bu scallions, chopped 1 jar 1 jar bottled jalapenos (as a side if we have any, optional) 2 pints 2 pints sour cream (as a side) instructions (during the morning we just get ready, dish is assembled at 5:00) setup for later use (storage containers ok, not pretty-ware): beans, cheddar, black olives, green chilies, scallions setup nice for serving on the side: jalapenos, sour cream at 3:50, km: setup pans with thick layer of chips, locate rest. at 5:00, km: turn both ovens on to 400. sprinkle chips w/ beans, scal, oliv, chilis, salsa, chese ~5:15 stick into hot ovens for ~10 -15mins till warm and cheese melted.

title: Moroccan Soup
text: all recipes / soup moroccan soup tags: vegetarian, gluten-free, nut-free, soy-free week 2 day 7 supper recipe: moroccan soup equipment largest soup pot fill to ~15-16 qts ingredients note: if you have almost nothing left, there is a recipe for a moroccan red lentil soup maybe printed in the soups folder or online in “other recipes” for ~48 ~2qts left over rice pilaf or make more ~7qts or more left-over moroccan stew as needed more canned tomatoes, better than bouillon mixed per jar instructions, any leftover veggies that fit, maybe some raisins or dried apricots. up 2-4 qts if very short, add some dry red lentils if you’ve added so much that it’s bland, saute some more onions, see original recipe for ideas for spices to add. bring to a full boil, turn off fire, put on lid, it will stay hot until 5:00. serve with yogurts if you have some, cilantro if you have some.

title: Peanut Casserole
text: all recipes / entree peanut casserole tags: vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free, soy-free week 2 day 2 supper recipe: peanut casserole or soup equipment 2 2” hotel pans or ~16qts soup in largest soup pot (to stay warm) ingredients: leftover peanut stew, roasted cabbage and rice instructions for either: chop up the leftover cabbage into bite sized pieces for casseroles: mix or layer whatever you have leftover of rice, cabbage and peanut stew. if not enough to make 2x2” casseroles (or 1-1½ if a lot of 8 precepts), a soup is probably easier to pad out. cover & fridge. for soup: add your leftovers to the soup pot (using no more than ~2qts rice, ie not too thick). augment as needed to have ~16qts (or less if lots of 8 precepts) using: canned tomatoes any not needed zucchini or kale or cabbage? (check with km) maybe frozen green beans? better than bouillon consult on flavor if not enough (maybe more peanut butter? salt? lemon? ) bring to a rapid boil, turn off fire, put lid on, the big pots will stay warm until 5:00. at 3:50: reheat casseroles during talk, done when 165 degrees.

title: Sesame Noodle or Rice Salad
text: all recipes / salad sesame noodle or rice salad tags: vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free day 6 supper recipe: sesame rice (or noodle) salad page 1 of 2 equipment: rice cooker or 20qt w/ pasta insert, large sauce pan, lg skillet, vitamix, huge salad bowl to mix, 2nd largest to serve km has 2 choices here: rice or noodles, peanut or sesame/ginger dressing. (consider nut allergies.) ingredients: for ~48 either: 6 cups raw short grain brown rice (assume cooked the day before) or: 5 boxes annie chun brown-rice noodles 3lbs asparagus (cut into 1” pieces), blanched ~2lbs snap peas or snow peas (cut in half or thirds), raw 3lbs carrots, small dice, blanched (or can use 2-3cups shredded) broc. stems saved broccoli stems, small dice, blanched 1 pack peas frozen (use raw, or could chop of green beans if no peas). 2 whole cucumbers, small dice 4 bunches scallions sliced small ¾ cup toasted white sesame seeds (& more in dressing see below) dressing: choose either sesame ginger or peanut sesame (filed under salad dressings) optional sides: 2 little jars pickled ginger mixed herbs: bowl of chopped cilantro & mint mixed with a little oil. supper recipe sesame rice (ornoodles) page 2 of 2 instructions make rice or noodles easiest to do the day before if not using rice cooker then. if using noodles, do on the day in 20qt pasta cooker insert. add some sesame oil to the boiling water. drain & rinse with cold water. make dressing also easy to do the day before. choose either one of: sesame peanut dressing or sesame ginger dressing. consider peanut allergies --maybe save some undressed salad & toss with simple oil, rice vinegar & ginger. prep veggies cut up veggies as specified in ingredients list. steam just a little, still slightly crunchy: carrots, broccoli stems, asparagus leave raw: snap or snow peas, frozen peas, cucumber. prep seeds using large skillet, spread out total of 1 cup white sesame seeds. put on low flame and watch carefully. remove when just lightly brown. some go in dressing, some in salad. toss toss all veggies, grain and ( setting aside a nut allergy portion? ) dressing in one of the super-huge salad bowls. transfer to next-largest to serve. cover, refrigerate & re-toss before serving. ideal to take out of fridge at 3:50 & let it come nearer to room temp.

title: Shepherds Pie
text: all recipes / entree shepherds pie tags: vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free, soy-free week 2 day 4 supper recipe: shepherd’s pie equipment 2 2” hotel pans or ~16qts soup in largest soup pot (to stay warm) ingredients: leftover peanut stew, roasted cabbage and rice instructions for either: chop up the leftover cabbage into bite sized pieces for casseroles: mix or layer whatever you have leftover of rice, cabbage and peanut stew. if not enough to make 2x2” casseroles (or 1-1½ if a lot of 8 precepts), a soup is probably easier to pad out. cover & fridge. for soup: add your leftovers to the soup pot (using no more than ~2qts rice, ie not too thick). augment as needed to have ~16qts (or less if lots of 8 precepts) using: canned tomatoes any not needed zucchini or kale or cabbage? (check with km) maybe frozen green beans? better than bouillon consult on flavor if not enough (maybe more peanut butter? salt? lemon? ) bring to a rapid boil, turn off fire, put lid on, the big pots will stay warm until 5:00. at 3:50: reheat casseroles during talk, done when 165 degrees.

title: Spinach Salad
text: all recipes / salad spinach salad tags: vegetarian, gluten-free, nut-free, soy-free day 1 supper recipe: spinach salad bar page 1 of 1 equipment serving bowls, lg baking sheet ingredients for ~48 3 ½ cups pumpkin seeds (roasted, see below) 3lb (¾ of the bucket) feta cheese, crumbled (save leftover & rest for lentil salad day) 2 29oz cans garbanzo beans, drained ~4-5 cups kalamata olives, drained (check if leftovers in fridge) 4 pints cherry tomatoes, rinsed *may be located in pantry, halved if time 1 case baby spinach (supper yogi will prep this) 2 small pitchers balsamic dressing (should be leftover from before) instructions toast pumpkin seeds do this first thing to finish using oven early turn on oven to 350 (can put seeds in before preheated) spread seeds on baking sheet and roast for 15-20 mins until they start lightly browning. check and stir at 10 mins setup rest set-up leftover balsamic dressing in 2 small pitchers, cover with plastic and put in fridge. set-up all other sides (except spinach) cover and label. put tomatoes and seeds in the pantry, rest in fridge together on “supper” shelf.

title: Thai Casserole
text: all recipes / entree thai casserole tags: vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free week 2 day 6 supper recipe: thai casserole equipment 2 2” hotel pans ingredients for ~48 ~6qts left over rice or make more ~7qts left-over thai veggies (or add more from freezer) maybe more other leftover veggies if any, or more frozen veg, or canned tomatoes? or more tofu, extra spinach if not needed for salad?? or more coconut milk as needed, instructions mix or layer whatever you have of the above into the 2 casseroles. cover & fridge. at 3:50: reheat during talk, done when 165 degrees.

title: Thai Cauliflower Soup
text: all recipes / soup thai cauliflower soup tags: vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free, nut-free, soy-free first day supper recipe: thai cauliflower soup this is usually prepped on opening day but served at first full day supper. best idea is to get it all made except for the “final touches” on opening day or even day before (as soon as you have the produce), then reheat it on first full day when the big 32 qt pot is available and it will keep hot all afternoon. ingredients for ~48 10 hds (1 case -2) cauliflower: 2 heads cut into edible size flowerets, 8 heads rough chopped for later blending. [set aside the other 2 from the case of 12 for another recipe later] 5lbs yellow onions, diced medium 1 ½ cups ginger, minced in small cuisinart 30 cloves garlic, minced in small cuisinart 2-3 fresh jalapeno peppers, seeded, chopped fine (optional) ~¾ cup fresh lime juice, maybe ~10 limes? and zest of ~5 of them ⅔ cup yellow thai curry paste ⅔ of a lg can coconut milk simple stock: 1 jar bouillon mixed with ~3 qts hot tea machine water to dissolve, add with more water or lemongrass stock (see below) to a total of ~16 quarts of soup (of soup, not just of stock, maybe ~6 qts stock total??) 1 bu optional: scallions, chopped white & light green parts 2 bags frozen peas salt to taste at end optional: stock for ambitious cooks who have extra time: make stock with ~20 lemon grass stalks, ?galangal, kaffir lime leaves instructions saute saute onions until, add ginger, garlic, jalapenas & saute a minute or so. add ingredients and cook add rough chopped cauliflower and stock (either diluted bouillon or fancy) to not quite cover the cauliflower…and let cook until cauliflower is soft. blend with immersion blender until smooth add curry paste & blend that in. add florets. this should now be about noon: insure it’s over 170. put a lid on it, turn off the gas and it will stay hot all afternoon. [or cool and save to reheat when needed] final touches at 5:00pm test temp, put it on a flame disperser and turn the gas back on to low/med. if time: head the coconut milk in a sauce pan enough to melt fat, but not to boil. add in the coconut milk. make sure it is ~165 but try not to let it come back to a boil (separates the coconut milk). add lime zest and juice to taste. add salt to taste if needed ~5mins before serving: add the peas (probably thawing in the fridge). serve with cilantro (listed under the salad prep, they both call for it) and optionally the chopped scallions.

title: Thai Salad
text: all recipes / salad thai salad tags: vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free day 1 supper recipe: thai slaw salad page 1 of 1 this is to be served with 1 batch of peanut lime dressing (see salad dressings) equipment serving bowls ingredients for ~48 ½ large or 1 small red cabbage, shredded in robocoupe or by hand 1 napa cabbage shredded (easiest by hand) 2lbs frozen green beans, steam until thawed and edible 2 cups mint leaves, chopped (check garden if not ordered) 2 cups shredded carrots (take from salad bar supply) mung bean sprouts (optional if we bought some) baby kale add to above to make a full medium sized salad bowl 2lbs peanuts serve whole on side (also good with 3bu chopped cilantro on side, but we probably offer that with the soup) instructions mix all except (cilantro) & peanuts. serve those and the dressing on the side.

title: Vegan Cheesy Broccoli Soup
text: all recipes / soup vegan cheesy broccoli soup tags: vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free, soy-free alt day 6 supper recipe: broccoli soup page 1 of 2 equipment: largest 32 quart stock pot, vitamix, immersion blender note: ideally put cashews to soak at breakfast, ready to use by 9:30, soup is ok but just grittier if not pre-soaked ingredients for ~48 5 cups cashews, soaked in water to cover by about 2” 1 case broccoli, rough chop heads into florets/chunks, optional: could trim some stems and chop (trim very deeply, be sure to get all the tough stringy stuff off) 4lbs yukon type potatoes, 1” cubed (or a bit larger ok) 4lbs onions, medium diced ¾ cup minced garlic (use mini cuisinart) 2 cups nutritional yeast 1 lemon juice and zest 1 jar better than bouillon ~6 quarts water–use ~3 quarts from hot tea urn into a metal pitcher to dissolve the bouillon, then add the other 3 qts cold to taste salt & pepper (maybe white pepper?) optional: could serve with cheddar and vegan cheddar on side day 6 supper recipe: broccoli soup page 2 of 2 instructions prep blend cashews in their water in the vitamix until smooth mix bouillon with 3 quarts hot tea urn water. chop garlic in mini-cuisinart put a heat-deflector under the pot. saute onions in olive oil, add garlic when onions are soft, watch so it doesn’t burn. add liquids add broth, yeast & cashew blend to onions. mix. add rest add potatoes, (most of the) broccoli & rest of water. you may need to cook down the broccoli a bit to fit in the rest. (it all reduces down a lot when done & blended). use the big wooden paddle to turn the ingredients so all the broccoli gets cooked. cook until broc and potatoes are soft enough to eat and temp is >= 180. blend using the large immersion blender, blend the soup. maybe put the pot on the floor or on a step stool, easier to hold the big blender. season add lemon juice and zest, salt and pepper to taste. get back to ~180, turn off burner, put on lid & leave on stove for supper.

title: Vegan Cornbread
text: all recipes / side vegan cornbread tags: vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free, nut-free, soy-free recipe: vegan gf cornbread pg 1 of 2 equipment 4 half-sized 2” hotel pans (cooks more evenly than 2 full size), 2 large mixing bowls, 2 small mixing bowls ingredients for ~48-50 for ~36 (3 half pans) note: recently upped left quantity to fill 4 half-pans 1 ⅓ cup 1 cup vegan egg replacer (in pantry baking box?) note: bob’s v-egg has soy, the other “ener-g” box brand doesn’t, prefer that one or ground flax seed (in freezer?) 4 cups 3 cups warm water for flax or vegan egg 7 ½ cups 5 ½ cups + 2 tbls rice milk (or alternative milk of choice, check allergies) ¾ cup + 1 t ½ cup + 1 tbls + 2 tsp apple cider vinegar 10 ⅔ cups 8 cups gluten-free flour 10 ⅔ cups 8 cups bob’s medium grind cornmeal (check pantries for ~32oz bags of this, can use polenta if none, the med. grind makes it lighter) 3 t + 1 ½ tsp 2 t + 2 t salt ½ cup+1 ½ t ¼ cup + 3 tbls + ¼ tsp baking powder 4 ¾ tsp 3 ½ tsp baking soda 2 ⅔ cups 2 cups canola oil 2 ⅔ cups 2 cups pumpkin pulp (canned/boxed) 2 ⅔ cups 2 cups brown sugar ( not honey, to keep it vegan) alt recipe: vegan cornbread pg 2 of 2 instructions heat oven to 375 degrees. grease pans. mix v-egg or ground flax and warm water separately, let set for 5-10 minutes to thicken (will need to whisk the v-egg). mix alternative milk of choice and vinegar and let set while preparing other ingredients. in a large mixing bowl, mix dry ingredients: corn meal, gf flour, baking powder, baking soda and salt in one bowl. in a separate mixing bowl, mix together oil, pumpkin, sweetener, “milk” mixture, flax mixture. leave wets and drys separate until just ready to go in oven. mix just until combined, be careful not to overmix. place mixture into 3 or 4 half-sized 2 inch-deep hotel pans (stored on the island near pantry door). bake for 40-50 min? or until golden brown and cooked in the center. test by patting for firmness & toothpick or knife comes out clean. start checking after 30 mins.

title: Sweet Potato Hummus
text: all recipes / side sweet potato hummus tags: vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free, nut-free, soy-free sweet potato hummus adapted from martha stewart on the web ingredients for 4 cups 1 pound sweet potatoes, peeled and cut into 1-inch pieces assuming we are starting from leftover baked ones: just peel and mash, try about 2 cups 1 can (19.5 ounces) chickpeas, drained and rinsed 1/4 cup fresh lemon juice (from 1 lemon) 1/4 cup tahini 2 tablespoons olive oil 2 teaspoons ground cumin 1 garlic clove, chopped coarse salt and ground pepper whole-wheat pita and crudites such as red pepper and broccoli

title: Tarragon Dressing
text: all recipes / salad tarragon dressing tags: vegetarian, gluten-free, dairy-free, nut-free, soy-free tarragon vinaigrette gather all ingredients below and two vitamix containers. you will double this recipe: add the ingredients to the first vitamix container then repeat with the second container. ingredients for one vitamix container (do this twice ) 1 cup water 6 cloves garlic 3 1/2 cup canola oil + additional oil to cover garlic for poaching 2 cup rice vinegar ¼ cup honey ¼ cup dijon mustard 1 box of tarragon (approx. ½ cup) add 1 cup water to each vitamix container. add 3 1/2 cup canola oil to each vitamix container. poach garlic: place 12 whole garlic cloves in the smallest skillet and cover with canola oil. simmer in medium heat for about 5 minutes. watch closely. add 6 cloves and half the oil to each vitamix container. (adding it to the cool oil/water prevents garlic from further cooking) rinse the tarragon and pick the leaves off the stems. add remaining ingredients to first vitamix container. repeat with second vitamix container. blend all ingredients. fill 2 small pitchers with each salad dressing made.

title: Tarragon Dressing
text: all recipes / salad tarragon dressing tags: vegetarian, gluten-free, dairy-free, nut-free, soy-free tarragon vinaigrette (instructions for double recipe) gather all ingredients below, the vitamix container and a second 2 or 4 quart container with lid. you will double this recipe by putting a set of the below ingredients in each container. it’s easiest to add each ingredient to both containers, then go to the next ingredient. ingredients for one container (you will put this much in each one) 1 cup water 1 tsp garlic powder (on spice shelf far left) 3 ¾ cup canola oil 2 cup rice vinegar ¼ cup honey ¼ cup dijon mustard 1 box of tarragon (approx. ½ cup, fine to use the whole box) rinse 2 boxes of tarragon and pick the leaves off the stems, divide pile back in half. add the above ingredients list to each container. blend the contents of the vitamix container using the vitamix. fill 2 small pitchers with it. pour second set of ingredients into the vitamix container and mix it. pour the mixed dressing back in the mixing container, cover, label and put in the fridge.

title: Tarragon Salad Dressing
text: all recipes / salad tarragon salad dressing tags: vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free, nut-free, soy-free recipe: tarragon salad dressing equipment vitamix, 2 pitchers, (extra 2qt square container with green lid for second batch) ingredients for 1 batch (~48 servs) note: you may be asked to make 2 batches, first read instructions below for how to do that...these are the quantities for one batch 1 ½ cup rice vinegar 1 ½ cup water 1 tsp garlic powder ¼ cup dijon mustard ¼ cup agave ½ tsp salt ½ clamshell fresh tarragon leaves (pick off from stems) (could use ~1 ½ tsp? dry if no fresh…taste for qty) ½ bunch fresh parsley (cut off main trunk of stems, ok to use rest) (=~½ cup packed down) 3 ½ cups light olive oil instructions rinse herbs, no need to chop, vitamix will do it. add all except oils in vitamix container and mix on low. if making 2 batches, measure a second batch except oils into square container. drizzle oils into vitamix mixing while you do. gradually increase speed until all emulsified. divide between 2 small pitchers. for second batch: pour measured container ingredients into vitamix and blend. add second batch of oils as above. pour back into container, label, date and store in fridge for later.

title: Tarragonl Dressing
text: all recipes / salad tarragonl dressing tags: vegetarian, gluten-free, dairy-free, nut-free, soy-free tarragon vinaigrette (instructions for double recipe) updated by chris 7/30/2015 for a bit milder & less gather all ingredients below, the vitamix container and a second 2 quart (smallest square) container with lid. you will double this recipe by putting a set of the below ingredients in each container. it’s easiest to add each ingredient to both containers, then go to the next ingredient. ingredients for one container (you will put this much in each of the vitamix and the side container) 1 ½ cups rice vinegar 1 ½ cups water 1 tsp garlic powder (on spice shelf far left) ¼ cup honey (tip: coat cup with oil, honey slides right out) ¼ cup dijon mustard ½ tsp salt ½ clamshell fresh tarragon (could use ~1 ½ ? tsp dry if no fresh) ½ bunch fresh parsley (approx. ½ cup packed down) 3 ½ cups canola oil rinse the tarragon. add the above ingredients list to each container. blend the contents of the vitamix container using the vitamix. fill 2 small pitchers with it. pour second set of ingredients into the vitamix container and mix it. pour the mixed dressing back in the mixing container, cover, label and put in the fridge.

title: Thai Noodle Salad Recipe Feasting At Home
text: all recipes / salad thai noodle salad recipe feasting at home tags: vegetarian, dairy-free thai noodle salad with peanut sauce author:sylvia fountaine | feasting at home prep time:15cook time:15 total time:30 minutesyield:6-8 description a simple delicious recipe for thai noodle salad with peanut sauce, loaded up with healthy veggies. vegan and gluten free, this make-ahead salad is perfect for midweek lunches or large gatherings. add sesame ginger tofu for added protein! watch the video. ingredients thai peanut sauce (you may not need all- so save extras for another use.) 6 ounces dry noodles (brown rice noodles, pad thai style rice noodles, soba noodles, linguini) 4 cups mix of red cabbage, carrots and radish, shredded or grated 1 red bell pepper, nely sliced 3 scallions, sliced 1/2 bunch cilantro, chopped (or sub basil and mint) 1 tablespoon (or less, or more) jalapeño, nely chopped 1/4–1/2 cup roasted, crushed peanuts ( optional garnish) 5 thin slices ginger- cut across the grain, about the size of a quarter. 2 cloves garlic 1/2 cup peanut butter ( or sub almond butter!) 4/14/25, 10:53 am thai noodle salad recipe | feasting at home https://www.feastingathome.com/thai-noodle-salad-with-peanut-sauce/print/16470/ 1/3 add this baked sesame ginger tofu (optional) instructions 1. cook noodles. *see notes for rice noodles. cook pasta according to directions on the package. drain and chill under cold running water, drain. 2. peanut sauce. while noodles are cooking, add all the peanut sauce ingredients to a blender and blend until smooth. (you can do this up to 3 days ahead and refrigerate.) 3. prep your veggies. slice, grate, and chop. 1/2 cup fresh orange juice ( roughly 1 large orange) 1/3 cup fresh lime juice ( roughly 2 limes) 1/4 cup soy sauce or gf braggs liquid amino acids (note: tamari will turn this unpleasantly dark) 1/3 cup honey, agave, or maple syrup 1/4 cup toasted sesame oil 1 – 1 1/2 teaspoons cayenne pepper ( or a squirt of sriracha sauce) 1 teaspoon salt 4/14/25, 10:53 am thai noodle salad recipe | feasting at home https://www.feastingathome.com/thai-noodle-salad-with-peanut-sauce/print/16470/ 2/3 serving size: 1 cupcalories: 214 sugar: 10 gsodium: 280.5 mg fat: 9.8 gsaturated fat: 1.6 gcarbohydrates: 29.9 gfiber: 2 g protein: 2.9 gcholesterol: 0 mg 4. combine. place shredded veggies, bell pepper, scallions, cilantro and jalapeño into a serving bowl. toss. add the cold noodles to the serving bowl and toss again. pour some peanut sauce over top and toss well to combine- no need to use all, just use enough to coat it well, generously. (save any extra sauce for any leftover salad, as it can soak up the sauce overnight.) 5. taste. adjust the salt (to your liking), add chili akes if you want, or more lime, and serve, garnishing with roasted peanuts and cilantro and a lime wedge. notes nutrition find it online: https://www.feastingathome.com/thai-noodle-salad-with-peanut-sauce/ rice noodles: if cooking pad thai style rice noodles, pour boiling water over the noodles in a baking dish, let soak until softened, drain. salad will keep 4 days in the fridge. 4/14/25, 10:53 am thai noodle salad recipe | feasting at home https://www.feastingathome.com/thai-noodle-salad-with-peanut-sauce/print/16470/ 3/3

title: Thai Noodle Salad with Peanut Sauce
text: all recipes / salad thai noodle salad with peanut sauce tags: vegetarian, dairy-free thai noodle salad with peanut sauce author: sylvia fountaine | feasting at home prep time: 15 cook time: 15 total time: 30 minutes yield: 6-8 description a simple delicious recipe for thai noodle salad with peanut sauce, loaded up with healthy veggies. vegan and gluten free, this make-ahead salad is perfect for midweek lunches or large gatherings. add sesame ginger tofu for added protein! watch the video. ingredients times 6 for irc: 36 6 ounces dry noodles ( brown rice noodles , pad thai style rice noodles , soba noodles , linguini) 24 4 cups mix of red cabbage, carrots and radish, shredded or grated 6 1 red bell pepper, finely sliced 18 3 scallions, sliced 3bu 1/2 bunch cilantro, chopped (or sub basil and mint) 6t 1 tablespoon (or less, or more) jalapeño, finely chopped 3c 1/4–1/2 cup roasted, crushed peanuts ( optional garnish) thai peanut sauce (you may not need all- so save extras for another use.) 30`5 thin slices ginger- cut across the grain, about the size of a quarter. 12 2 cloves garlic 3c 1/2 cup peanut butter ( or sub almond butter!) 3c 1/2 cup fresh orange juice ( roughly 1 large orange) 1c 1/3 cup fresh lime juice ( roughly 2 limes) 1 ½ c 1/4 cup soy sauce or gf braggs liquid amino acids (note: tamari will turn this unpleasantly dark) 2c 1/3 cup honey , agave , or maple syrup 1 ½ 1/4 cup toasted sesame oil taste 1 – 1 1/2 teaspoons cayenne pepper ( or a squirt of sriracha sauce) taste 1 teaspoon salt add this baked sesame ginger tofu (optional) sesame ginger tofu – made with soy sauce (or coconut aminos or tamari) sesame oil , miso, ginger, garlic and chili paste. marinate. 400 f oven, bake it for 30-35 minutes instructions cook noodles. *see notes for rice noodles. cook pasta according to directions on the package. drain and chill under cold running water, drain. peanut sauce. while noodles are cooking, add all the peanut sauce ingredients to a blender and blend until smooth. (you can do this up to 3 days ahead and refrigerate.) prep your veggies. slice, grate, and chop. combine. place shredded veggies, bell pepper, scallions, cilantro and jalapeño into a serving bowl. toss. add the cold noodles to the serving bowl and toss again. pour some peanut sauce over top and toss well to combine- no need to use all, just use enough to coat it well, generously. (save any extra sauce for any leftover salad, as it can soak up the sauce overnight.) taste. adjust the salt (to your liking), add chili flakes if you want, or more lime, and serve, garnishing with roasted peanuts and cilantro and a lime wedge. notes rice noodles: if cooking pad thai style rice noodles, pour boiling water over the noodles in a baking dish, let soak until softened, drain. salad will keep 4 days in the fridge. nutrition serving size: 1 cup calories: 214 sugar: 10 g sodium: 280.5 mg fat: 9.8 g saturated fat: 1.6 g carbohydrates: 29.9 g fiber: 2 g protein: 2.9 g cholesterol: 0 mg

title: Thin Mint Cookies
text: all recipes / dessert thin mint cookies tags: vegan, dairy-free vegan thin mints makes 65 cookies 1 ¥% cup all-purpose flour (or gluten-free all-purpose flour) 1 cup sugar ¥2 cup cocoa powder 4 teaspoon salt ya teaspoon baking soda 34 cup vegan margarine 3 tablespoons soy, almond, or rice milk 1 teaspoon pure vanilla extract y2 teaspoon pure peppermint extract chocolate coating this chocolate coating recipe will coat half the cookies (about 32) 2 cups semisweet chocolate chips (dairy-free) 1 tablespoon vegan margarine y/2 teaspoon peppermint extract to make the cookies » ina food processor, pulse flour, sugar, cocoa powder, salt, and baking soda until combined. add margarine, milk, vanilla, and mint extract. pulse a few more times until the mixture comes together. transfer the mixture to a large bowl and knead it with your hands until it comes together and all the flour is incorporated. chill the dough in the refrigerator for 1 hour.preheat the oven to 350 degrees f and line two large baking sheets with parchment paper or silpats. remove dough from refrigerator. roll a heaping teaspoon of cookie dough into a ball and place onto prepared baking sheets, leaving about 3 inches in between each ball. evenly flatten the dough with your fingertips so that it is about % inch thick and bake for 12-14 minutes. let cool completely. to make the chocolate coating melt chocolate chips and margarine in a double boiler or microwave. stir in the mint extract and mix until smooth. dip completely cooled cookies into the chocolate.

title: TOFU scramble for no
text: all recipes / entree tofu scramble for no tags: vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free, nut-free tofu scramble for no-egg for 2 servings: 1 teaspoon nutritional yeast 1/4 teaspoon turmeric 1/4 teaspoon ground cumin 1/4 teaspoon paprika 1 tablespoon water pinch sea salt 1/8 teaspoon black pepper olive oil spray 1 scallion, finely diced 1 clove garlic, minced 1/2 package firm tofu, very well drained 1 tablespoon very finely chopped parsley directions in a small bowl, mix together nutritonal yeast, turmeric, cumin, paprika, water, salt, and pepper. set aside. mist a frying pan with olive oil and place it over medium heat. once hot, add scallion and garlic, and saute until fragrant, about 2 minutes. crumble tofu into the pan, breaking it up with your fingers. pour seasoning over tofu and mix well, trying to color as much tofu as possible. cook for 2 minutes or until tofu is hot throughout. toss in parsley and continue to stir for another 1 to 2 minutes. once cooked, serve with favorite sides and toppings, such as sliced avocado, whole-grain crackers or toast, sliced tomato, bacon (regular or meat-free), salsa, and/or hot sauce.

title: Vegan Bacon for Potato Bar
text: all recipes / side vegan bacon for potato bar tags: vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free, nut-free recipe: vegan bacon (optional) equipment 3-4 large baking sheets ingredients #servings with supper leftovers #servings no supper leftovers 6 lbs tofu [qty] thinly sliced 1 cup liquid smoke ½ - ¾ cup nutritional yeast 3 cups tamari olive oil spray instructions arrange tofu preheat ovens to 400 degrees. arrange tofu in one layer on baking sheets mix marinade and bake mix tamari and liquid smoke and spread evenly over the tofu. place tofu in oven and bake for 45-60 minutes until tofu is crispyish but not burned. remove from oven when you reach desired texture. chop and finish once tofu is cooled chop into small pieces to put on potatoes and add the nutritional yeast and mix.

title: Vegan (GF) Banana Choc Chip Cupcakes
text: all recipes / dessert vegan (gf) banana choc chip cupcakes tags: vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free vegan (can be gf) banana chocolate chip cupcakes from vegan cupcakes take over the world ingredients for 4 dozen = 48..these are fine made all gf. or you can make 4dz reg plus 1 dz gf. 1dz 5 dz 4 dz ½ c 2 ½ c 2 cups mashed very ripe bananas 1 ¼ c 6 ¼ c 5 cups flour (all-purpose or bob’s 1-1 gluten free) ¼ t 1 ¼ t 1 tsp baking soda 1t 5 t 4 tsp baking powder ½ t 2 ½ t 2 tsp salt ¾ c 3 ¾ c 3 cups granulated (regular white) sugar ¼ c+1 ½ t 1 ⅔ c 1 ⅓ cup canola oil ½ c+3t 3 ⅓ c 2 ⅔ cups rice milk 2t 8 t 6 tsp vanilla extract ½ t (2 tsp almond extract...don’t think we have missed skipping this, but good with!) ¾ c 3 ¾ c 3 cups dark or semi-sweet chocolate chips preheat oven to 350 line 4 muffin tins with paper cupcake liners. mash bananas until quite smooth. sift/mix flour, baking soda, baking powder, salt and sugar in a large bowl and mix. (or just mix..we never sift). in a separate bowl, whisk together the oil, rice milk, vanilla, (almond), and mashed banana. fold wet ingredients into dry ingredients, mixing to just combine (don’t over mix). fold in chocolate chips. fill liners ⅔ full. you could add a couple of choc chips to top each one. bake for 20-22 minutes (maybe more in our right oven)...until inserted knife or toothpick comes out clean. cool completely on wire rack. (if not for today, store in lidded ant-proof container!) optional chocolate icing: 2 ½ cups confectioners’ (aka powdered) sugar 1 ½ tablespoons cocoa ½ teaspoons ground cinnamon 7 tablespoons earth balance, melted (~40 secs in microwave) 3 tablespoons soy or rice milk //check diets 1 ½ teaspoons vanilla extract directions 1. place sugar and cinnamon in a small bowl. add the melted earth bal, soy milk, and vanilla and stir with a fork until smooth. let it come back to room temp to judge consistency. the mixture should look opaque. if looks too liquid, add a little extra powdered sugar. best kept at room temp unless overnight, then fridge and bring back to room temp. pipe on with a sandwich type plastic bag with one tip-end cut off a small bit. enough for a squiggle on each of 5dz.

title: Vegan (GF) Pumpkin Choc Chip Cupcakes
text: all recipes / dessert vegan (gf) pumpkin choc chip cupcakes tags: vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free, nut-free vegan (can be gf) pumpkin chocolate chip cupcakes adapted from vegan cupcakes take over the world, isa moskowitz et.al. ingredients for 4 dozen = 48 (i got 5 doz out of it...all got eaten!) 4 cups canned pumpkin (hint: 2 cans=~ 3 ½ cups, sot if you have leftover baked yams, mash some of those to save opening a third can) 1 ⅓ cup canola oil 4 cups granulated (regular white) sugar 1 cup rice milk 4 tsp vanilla extract 5 cups all-purpose flour or bob’s “1-1” gluten free flour 2 tsp baking powder 2 tsp baking soda 2 tsp cinnamon 1 tsp salt 3 cups chocolate chips (about 1 ½ bags, use a few more to put 1-2 on top of each one) preheat oven to 350 line 4-5 muffin tins with paper cupcake liners. in bowl, mix well the flour, baking powder, baking soda, cinnamon and salt. in a separate bowl, stir together pumpkin, oil, sugar, rice milk and vanilla. mix well, then stir in chocolate chips. add dry to wet and stir with a fork. fill liners ⅔ full. you could add a couple of choc chips to top each one esp. if not icing. bake for 20-25 minutes (maybe more in our right oven)...until they are looking lightly browned and an inserted knife or toothpick comes out clean. cool completely on wire rack. (if not for today, store in lidded ant-proof container!) optional cinnamon icing: 2 ½ cups confectioners’ (aka powdered) sugar 1 ½ teaspoons ground cinnamon 7 tablespoons earth balance, melted (~40 secs in microwave) 3 tablespoons soy or rice milk //check diets 1 ½ teaspoons vanilla extract directions 1. place sugar and cinnamon in a small bowl. add the melted earth bal, soy milk, and vanilla and stir with a fork until smooth. let it come back to room temp to judge consistency. the mixture should look opaque. if looks too liquid, add a little extra powdered sugar. best kept at room temp unless overnight, then fridge and bring back to room temp. pipe on with a sandwich type plastic bag with one tip-end cut off a small bit. enough for a squiggle on each of 5dz.

title: Vegan GF Cornbread
text: all recipes / side vegan gf cornbread tags: vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free, nut-free, soy-free tab 3 vegan gluten free cornbread –need to buy ½ gal full fat oatley adapted from nisha vora rainbowplantlife.com this fits nicely in two 2”deep hotel pans each cut 6x8. this can take a couple of hours of off & on attention from someone (km?) so consider that. some approx. times below. measurements with “g” need a precision grams scale (we have one or more above the spice shelf, looks like an ipad). ingredients: ½ gallon oatly full fat oat milk (from whole fds) 4 tbls apple cider vinegar 1170g stone-ground medium corn meal (not the polenta, that is too coarse) 564g gluten free all-purpose flour 8tbls=½ cup baking powder 3 tsp salt 336g vegan butter, melted 336g extra virgin olive oil 240g brown sugar 504g agave 24g=6t finely chopped (use spice grinder) rosemary (from the kitchen garden) directions (timing aiming for still warm to serve): preheat oven to 400 (with the vulcan, try 450 and watch it) ~10:15? stir vinegar and oat milk and set aside at least 10-20 minutes to curdle in a large bowl combine flour, cornmeal, baking powder and salt. whisk well. ~10:30? pour in the melted vegan butter, oil, brown sugar, agave & curdled oatmilk. careful not to overmix, some lumps ok. should look like pancake mix. fold in the rosemary. allow batter to rest 10min to 1 hour. ~11:10 heat the empty pans in the over while batter is resting for about 10 minutes. remove from over, add more lumps of vegan butter to melt and coat the pan. sprinkle pan bottom with cornmeal. pour in batter, dividing between 2 pans. ~11:20 bake 25-35 minutes (in vulcan, rotate frount/back and top/bottom half way thru, might take longer than 25. test with toothpick or knife. cool for 15 mins before slicing 5x8 each pan.
